370.s:
agnir uvāca
uktāni yamamārgāṇi vakṣye 'tha maraṇe nṛṇāṃ /
ūṣmā prakupitaḥ kāye tīvravāyusamīritaḥ //
370.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
उक्तानि यममार्गाणि वक्ष्ये ऽथ मरणे नृणां /
ऊष्मा प्रकुपितः काये तीव्रवायुसमीरितः //
370.m: Agni said: / The paths of Yama have been described. Now I shall speak of men's death: / the bodily heat, aggravated in the body and stirred up by violent wind,

370.s:
śarīramuparudhyātha kṛtsnāndoṣānruṇaddhi vai /
chinatti prāṇasthānāni punarmarmāṇi caiva hi //
370.d:
शरीरमुपरुध्याथ कृत्स्नान्दोषान्रुणद्धि वै /
छिनत्ति प्राणस्थानानि पुनर्मर्माणि चैव हि //
370.m: obstructing the body, indeed blocks all the bodily humours; / it cuts off the locations of the vital breath and also the vulnerable vital parts (marmans).

370.s:
śaityāt prakupito vāyuśchidramanviṣyate tataḥ /
dve netre dvau tathā karṇau dvau tu nāsāpuṭau tathā //
370.d:
शैत्यात् प्रकुपितो वायुश्छिद्रमन्विष्यते ततः /
द्वे नेत्रे द्वौ तथा कर्णौ द्वौ तु नासापुटौ तथा //
370.m: The wind, provoked by cold, then searches for an opening: / the two eyes, the two ears, and the two nostrils,

370.s:
ūrdhvantu sapta cchidrāṇi aṣṭamaṃ vadanaṃ tathā /
etaiḥ prāṇo viniryāti prāyaśaḥ śubhakarmaṇāṃ //
370.d:
ऊर्ध्वन्तु सप्त च्छिद्राणि अष्टमं वदनं तथा /
एतैः प्राणो विनिर्याति प्रायशः शुभकर्मणां //
370.m: the seven upper apertures, and the mouth as the eighth; / through these the vital breath usually departs in the case of those who performed auspicious deeds.

370.s:
adhaḥ pāyurupasthañca anenāśubhakāriṇāṃ /
:n
1 piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā tuvnyasediti ña..
:p 310
mūrdhānaṃ yogino bhittvā jīvo yātyatha cecchayā //
370.d:
अधः पायुरुपस्थञ्च अनेनाशुभकारिणां /
:न्
1 पिण्डं कृत्वा तुव्न्यसेदिति ञ..
:प् 310
मूर्धानं योगिनो भित्त्वा जीवो यात्यथ चेच्छया //
370.m:
The anus and generative organ are below; through these it departs for evildoers.
[Footnote]
1. Manuscript ña reads *piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā tuvnyasediti*.
[Page 310]
Cleaving open the crown of the head, the soul (jīva) of a yogin departs at will.

370.s:
antakāle tu samprāpre prāṇe 'pānamupasthite /
tamasā saṃvṛte jñāne saṃvṛteṣu ca marmasu //
370.d:
अन्तकाले तु सम्प्राप्रे प्राणे ऽपानमुपस्थिते /
तमसा संवृते ज्ञाने संवृतेषु च मर्मसु //
370.m: When the final time has arrived, the vital breath (prāṇa) has reached the downward breath (apāna), / consciousness is enveloped by darkness, and the vulnerable points (marmans) are closed,

370.s:
sa jivo nābhyadhiṣṭānaścālyate mātariśvanā /
bādhyamāṇaścānayate aṣṭāṅgāḥ prāṇavṛttikāḥ //
370.d:
स जिवो नाभ्यधिष्टानश्चाल्यते मातरिश्वना /
बाध्यमाणश्चानयते अष्टाङ्गाः प्राणवृत्तिकाः //
370.m: that soul, seated in the navel, is shaken by the wind; / being afflicted, it brings along the eight limbs consisting of the functions of the vital breaths.

370.s:
cyavantaṃ jāyamānaṃ vā praviśantañca yoniṣu /
prapaśyanti ca taṃ siddhā devā divyena cakṣupā //
370.d:
च्यवन्तं जायमानं वा प्रविशन्तञ्च योनिषु /
प्रपश्यन्ति च तं सिद्धा देवा दिव्येन चक्षुपा //
370.m: Siddhas and deities behold with divine vision / that [soul] falling, being born, or entering wombs.

370.s:
gṛhṇāti tatkṣaṇādyoge śarīrañcātivāhikam /
ākāśavāyutejāṃsi vigrahādūrdhvagāminaḥ //
370.d:
गृह्णाति तत्क्षणाद्योगे शरीरञ्चातिवाहिकम् /
आकाशवायुतेजांसि विग्रहादूर्ध्वगामिनः //
370.m: Instantly, through union, it assumes a subtle transit body (ātivāhika); / ether, wind, and fire go upward from the physical form;

370.s:
jalaṃ mahī ca pañcatvamāpannaḥ puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ /
ātivāhikadehantu yamadūtā nayanti taṃ //
370.d:
जलं मही च पञ्चत्वमापन्नः पुरुषः स्मृतः /
आतिवाहिकदेहन्तु यमदूता नयन्ति तं //
370.m: water and earth [dissolve], and the person is considered to have undergone dissolution into the five elements. / The messengers of Yama lead him in his subtle transit body

370.s:
yāmyaṃ mārgaṃ mahāghoraṃ ṣaḍaśītisahasrakam /
annodakaṃ nīyamāno bāndhavair dattamaśnute //
370.d:
याम्यं मार्गं महाघोरं षडशीतिसहस्रकम् /
अन्नोदकं नीयमानो बान्धवैर् दत्तमश्नुते //
370.m: along Yama's very dreadful path, measuring eighty-six thousand [yojanas]; / while being led, he eats the food and water given by his relatives.

370.s:
yamaṃ dṛṣṭvā yamoktena citraguptena ceritān /
prāpnoti narakānraudrāndharmī śubhapathair divam //
370.d:
यमं दृष्ट्वा यमोक्तेन चित्रगुप्तेन चेरितान् /
प्राप्नोति नरकान्रौद्रान्धर्मी शुभपथैर् दिवम् //
370.m: Having seen Yama, by the decree of Citragupta as declared by Yama, / he reaches the terrible hells, while the righteous man goes to heaven along auspicious paths.

370.s:
bhujyante pāpibhirvakṣye narakāṃstāś ca yātanāḥ /
aṣṭāviṃśatirevādhaḥkṣiternarakakoṭayaḥ //
370.d:
भुज्यन्ते पापिभिर्वक्ष्ये नरकांस्ताश् च यातनाः /
अष्टाविंशतिरेवाधःक्षितेर्नरककोटयः //
370.m: I shall describe those hells and the torments suffered by sinners: / beneath the earth there are twenty-eight crores of hells,

370.s:
saptamasya talasyānte ghore tamasi saṃsthitāḥ /
ghorākhyā prathamākoṭiḥ sughorā tadadhaḥsthitā //
370.d:
सप्तमस्य तलस्यान्ते घोरे तमसि संस्थिताः /
घोराख्या प्रथमाकोटिः सुघोरा तदधःस्थिता //
370.m: situated in terrifying darkness at the end of the seventh subterranean realm. / The first crore is called Ghorā; Sughorā is situated beneath that;

370.s:
atighorā mahāghorā ghorarūpā ca pañcamī /
ṣaṣṭhī taralatārākhyā saptamī ca bhayānakā //
370.d:
अतिघोरा महाघोरा घोररूपा च पञ्चमी /
षष्ठी तरलताराख्या सप्तमी च भयानका //
370.m: Atighorā, Mahāghorā, and Ghorarūpā is the fifth; / the sixth is named Taralatārā, and the seventh is Bhayānakā;

370.s:
bhayotkaṭā kālarātrī mahācaṇḍā ca caṇḍayā /
kolāhalā pracaṇḍākhyā padmā narakanāyikā //
:p 311
370.d:
भयोत्कटा कालरात्री महाचण्डा च चण्डया /
कोलाहला प्रचण्डाख्या पद्मा नरकनायिका //
:प् 311
370.m:
Bhayotkaṭā, Kālarātrī, Mahācaṇḍā, and Caṇḍā; / Kolāhalā, the one named Pracaṇḍā, and Padmā, the mistress of hells;
[Page 311]

370.s:
padmāvatī bhīṣaṇā ca bhīmā caiva karālikā /
vikarālā mahāvajrā trikoṇā pañcakoṇikā //
370.d:
पद्मावती भीषणा च भीमा चैव करालिका /
विकराला महावज्रा त्रिकोणा पञ्चकोणिका //
370.m: Padmāvatī, Bhīṣaṇā, Bhīmā, Karālikā, / Vikarālā, Mahāvajrā, Trikoṇā, Pañcakoṇikā,

370.s:
sadīrghā vartulā saptabhūmā caiva subhūmikā /
dīptamāyāṣṭāviṃśatayaḥ koṭayaḥ pāpiduḥkhadāḥ //
370.d:
सदीर्घा वर्तुला सप्तभूमा चैव सुभूमिका /
दीप्तमायाष्टाविंशतयः कोटयः पापिदुःखदाः //
370.m: Sadīrghā, Vartulā, Saptabhūmā, Subhūmikā, / and Dīptamāyā: these are the twenty-eight crores that bring misery to sinners.

370.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatikoṭīnāṃ pañca pañca ca nāyakāḥ /
rauravādyāḥ śatañcaikaṃ catvāriṃśaccatuṣṭayaṃ //
370.d:
अष्टाविंशतिकोटीनां पञ्च पञ्च च नायकाः /
रौरवाद्याः शतञ्चैकं चत्वारिंशच्चतुष्टयं //
370.m: Of the twenty-eight crores, each has five leaders; / beginning with Raurava, they are one hundred and forty-four [in number]:

370.s:
tāmiśramandhatāmiśraṃ mahārauravarauravau /
asipatraṃ vanañcaiva lohabhāraṃ tathaiva ca //
370.d:
तामिश्रमन्धतामिश्रं महारौरवरौरवौ /
असिपत्रं वनञ्चैव लोहभारं तथैव च //
370.m: Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, Mahāraurava, Raurava, / the Forest of Sword Leaves (Asipatravana), Lohabhāra,

370.s:
narakaṃ kālasūtrañca mahānarakameva va /
sañjīvanaṃ mahāvīci tapanaṃ sampratāpanaṃ //
370.d:
नरकं कालसूत्रञ्च महानरकमेव व /
सञ्जीवनं महावीचि तपनं सम्प्रतापनं //
370.m: the hell Kālasūtra, and Mahānaraka, / Sañjīvana, Mahāvīci, Tapana, Saṃpratāpana,

370.s:
saṅghātañca sakākolaṃ kudmalaṃ pūtimṛttikaṃ /
lohaśaṅkumṛjīṣañca pradhānaṃ śālmalīṃ nadīm //
370.d:
सङ्घातञ्च सकाकोलं कुद्मलं पूतिमृत्तिकं /
लोहशङ्कुमृजीषञ्च प्रधानं शाल्मलीं नदीम् //
370.m: Saṅghāta, Kakola, Kudmala, Pūtimṛttika, / Lohaśaṅku, Ṛjīṣa, the prominent Śālmalī, the river [Vaitaraṇī]:

370.s:
narakānviddhi koṭīśanāganvai ghoradarśanān /
pātyante pāpakarmāṇa ekaikasminbahuṣvapi //
370.d:
नरकान्विद्धि कोटीशनागन्वै घोरदर्शनान् /
पात्यन्ते पापकर्माण एकैकस्मिन्बहुष्वपि //
370.m: know these terrible-looking hells to be the lords of the crores. / Evil-doers are thrown into each one and into many of them.

370.s:
mārjārolūkagomāyugṛghrādivadanāś ca te /
tailadroṇyāṃ naraṃ kṣiptvā jvālayanti hutāśanaṃ //
370.d:
मार्जारोलूकगोमायुगृघ्रादिवदनाश् च ते /
तैलद्रोण्यां नरं क्षिप्त्वा ज्वालयन्ति हुताशनं //
370.m: They [the messengers] have faces like cats, owls, jackals, vultures, and the like; / having thrown a man into a cauldron of oil, they kindle a fire.

370.s:
ambarīṣeṣu caivānyāṃstāmrapātreṣu cāparān /
ayaḥpātreṣu caivānyān bahuvahnikaṇeṣu ca //
370.d:
अम्बरीषेषु चैवान्यांस्ताम्रपात्रेषु चापरान् /
अयःपात्रेषु चैवान्यान् बहुवह्निकणेषु च //
370.m: Others they throw into frying-pans, others into copper vessels, / others into iron vessels, and amid many sparks of fire.

370.s:
śūlāgrāropitāścānye chidyante narake 'pare /
tāḍyante ca kaśābhistu bhojyante cāpyayoguḍān //
370.d:
शूलाग्रारोपिताश्चान्ये छिद्यन्ते नरके ऽपरे /
ताड्यन्ते च कशाभिस्तु भोज्यन्ते चाप्ययोगुडान् //
370.m: Others are impaled on the tips of spears; others are cut to pieces in hell; / they are beaten with whips and forced to eat iron pellets.

370.s:
yamadūtair narāḥ pāṃśūnviṣṭhāraktakaphādikān /
taptaṃ madyaṃ pāyayanti pāṭayanti punarnarān //
370.d:
यमदूतैर् नराः पांशून्विष्ठारक्तकफादिकान् /
तप्तं मद्यं पाययन्ति पाटयन्ति पुनर्नरान् //
370.m: The messengers of Yama make men drink dust, feces, blood, phlegm, and the like, / and boiling liquor, and then split them open again.

370.s:
yantreṣu pīḍayanti sma bhakṣyante vāyasādibhiḥ /
:p 312
tailenoṣṇena sicyante chidyante naikaghā śiraḥ //
370.d:
यन्त्रेषु पीडयन्ति स्म भक्ष्यन्ते वायसादिभिः /
:प् 312
तैलेनोष्णेन सिच्यन्ते छिद्यन्ते नैकघा शिरः //

370.s:
hā tāteti krandamānāḥ svakannidanti karma te /
mahāpātakajānghorānnarakānprāpya garhitān //
370.d:
हा तातेति क्रन्दमानाः स्वकन्निदन्ति कर्म ते /
महापातकजान्घोरान्नरकान्प्राप्य गर्हितान् //
370.m: Crying out, “Alas, father!” they reproach their own actions, / having reached the horrific and despicable hells born of the great sins (mahāpātakas).

370.s:
karmakṣayātprajāyante mahāpātakinastviha /
mṛgaśvaśūkaroṣṭrāṇāṃ brahmahā yonimṛcchati //
370.d:
कर्मक्षयात्प्रजायन्ते महापातकिनस्त्विह /
मृगश्वशूकरोष्ट्राणां ब्रह्महा योनिमृच्छति //
370.m: When their karma is exhausted, the great sinners are born here [on earth]: / the killer of a brahmin enters the wombs of deer, dogs, pigs, and camels.

370.s:
kharapukkaśamlecchānāṃ madyapaḥ svarṇahāryapi /
kṛmikīṭapataṅgatvaṃ gurugastṛṇagulmatāṃ //
370.d:
खरपुक्कशम्लेच्छानां मद्यपः स्वर्णहार्यपि /
कृमिकीटपतङ्गत्वं गुरुगस्तृणगुल्मतां //
370.m: The drinker of liquor or the thief of gold enters the wombs of donkeys, Pukkaśas, and Mlecchas; / the violator of the Guru's bed becomes a worm, insect, or moth, or a blade of grass or shrub.

370.s:
brahmahā kṣayarogī syāt surāpaḥ śyāvadantakaḥ /
svarṇahārī tu kunakhī duś carmā gurutalpagaḥ //
370.d:
ब्रह्महा क्षयरोगी स्यात् सुरापः श्यावदन्तकः /
स्वर्णहारी तु कुनखी दुश् चर्मा गुरुतल्पगः //
370.m: The killer of a brahmin becomes consumptive; the drinker of liquor gets black teeth; / the thief of gold gets deformed nails; the defiler of the Guru's bed gets bad skin.

370.s:
yo yena saṃspṛśatyeṣāṃ sa talliṅgo 'bhijāyate /
annahartā māyāvī syānmūko vāgapahārakaḥ //
370.d:
यो येन संस्पृशत्येषां स तल्लिङ्गो ऽभिजायते /
अन्नहर्ता मायावी स्यान्मूको वागपहारकः //
370.m: Whoever associates with these takes on their marks when reborn. / A stealer of food becomes deceitful; a stealer of speech becomes mute;

370.s:
dhānyaṃ hṛtvātiriktāṅgaḥ piśunaḥ pūtināsikaḥ /
tailahṛttailapāyī syāt pūtivaktrastu sūcakaḥ //
370.d:
धान्यं हृत्वातिरिक्ताङ्गः पिशुनः पूतिनासिकः /
तैलहृत्तैलपायी स्यात् पूतिवक्त्रस्तु सूचकः //
370.m: one who steals grain gets a redundant limb; a slanderer gets a stinking nose; / an oil-thief becomes a cockroach (tailapāyin); an informer gets a foul-smelling mouth;

370.s:
parasya yoṣitaṃ hṛtvā brahmasvamapahṛtya ca /
araṇye nirjane deśe jāyate brahmarākṣasaḥ //
370.d:
परस्य योषितं हृत्वा ब्रह्मस्वमपहृत्य च /
अरण्ये निर्जने देशे जायते ब्रह्मराक्षसः //
370.m: having abducted another's wife and stolen a brahmin's property, / one is born as a brahmarākṣasa in a desolate forest region.

370.s:
ratnahārī hīnajātirgandhān chuchundarī śubhān /
patraṃ śākaṃ śikhī hṛtvā mukharo dhānyahārakaḥ //
370.d:
रत्नहारी हीनजातिर्गन्धान् छुछुन्दरी शुभान् /
पत्रं शाकं शिखी हृत्वा मुखरो धान्यहारकः //
370.m: A stealer of jewels is born in a low caste; of pleasant perfumes, a muskrat; / stealing leaves or vegetables, a peacock; an embezzler of grain becomes babbling;

370.s:
ajaḥ paśuṃpayaḥ kāko yānamuṣṭraḥ(1) phalaṃ kapiḥ /
madhu daṃśaḥ phalaṃ gṛdhro gṛhakāka upaskaraṃ //
370.d:
अजः पशुंपयः काको यानमुष्ट्रः(1) फलं कपिः /
मधु दंशः फलं गृध्रो गृहकाक उपस्करं //
370.m: one who steals a beast becomes a goat; milk, a crow; a conveyance, a camel; fruit, a monkey; / honey, a gadfly; fruit, a vulture; household utensils, a house crow;

370.s:
śivatrī vastraṃ sārasañca jhallī lavaṇahārakaḥ /
ukta ādhyātmikastāpaḥ śastrādyair ādhibhautikaḥ //
370.d:
शिवत्री वस्त्रं सारसञ्च झल्ली लवणहारकः /
उक्त आध्यात्मिकस्तापः शस्त्राद्यैर् आधिभौतिकः //
370.m: one who steals cloth becomes afflicted with leukoderma; of cranes, a cricket; a thief of salt [becomes an insect]. / Affliction from oneself (ādhyātmika) has been described; affliction from other beings (ādhibhautika) is caused by weapons and the like;

370.s:
grahāgnidevapīḍādyair ādhikaivika īritaḥ /
:n
1 yānaṃ vasta+iti kha..

kṛcchrair vrataiś ca dānādyair viṣṇupūjādibhirnaraḥ //

370.d:
ग्रहाग्निदेवपीडाद्यैर् आधिकैविक ईरितः /
:न्
1 यानं वस्त+इति ख..
:प् 313
त्रिथा तापं हि संसारं ज्ञानयोगाद्विनाशयेत् /
कृच्छ्रैर् व्रतैश् च दानाद्यैर् विष्णुपूजादिभिर्नरः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नरकनिरूपणं नाम
सप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथैकसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
यमनियमाः
370.m:
affliction from supernatural causes (ādhidaivika) is said to be caused by torment from planets, fire, gods, and the like.
[Footnote]
1. Manuscript kha reads *yānaṃ vasta+iti*.
[Page 313]
A person should destroy the threefold affliction of worldly existence (saṃsāra) through the yoga of knowledge,
through severe votive observances (kṛcchras), gifts, and worship of Viṣṇu and the like.
Thus ends the three hundred and seventieth chapter, named "Description of the Hells", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and seventy-first chapter.
The Restraints and Observances

371.s:
agnir uvāca
saṃsāratāpamuktyarthaṃ vakṣyāmy aṣṭāṅgayogakaṃ /
brahmaprakāśakaṃ jñānaṃ(1) yogastatraikacittatā //
371.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
संसारतापमुक्त्यर्थं वक्ष्याम्य् अष्टाङ्गयोगकं /
ब्रह्मप्रकाशकं ज्ञानं(1) योगस्तत्रैकचित्तता //
371.m:
Agni said:
For the sake of liberation from the torment of saṃsāra, I shall explain the eightfold yoga.
Knowledge reveals Brahman; yoga is the single-pointedness of mind therein.

371.s:
cittavṛttirnirodhaś ca jīvabrahmātmanoḥ paraḥ /
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryāparigrahau //
371.d:
चित्तवृत्तिर्निरोधश् च जीवब्रह्मात्मनोः परः /
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहौ //
371.m:
It is the supreme cessation of the modifications of the mind between the individual self and the self that is Brahman.
Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness —

371.s:
yamāḥ pañca smṛtā niyamādbhuktimuktidāḥ /
śaucaṃ santoṣatapasī svādhyāyeśvarapūjane //
371.d:
यमाः पञ्च स्मृता नियमाद्भुक्तिमुक्तिदाः /
शौचं सन्तोषतपसी स्वाध्यायेश्वरपूजने //
371.m:
these are traditionally remembered as the five restraints, yielding worldly enjoyment and liberation by rule.
Ritual purity, contentment, ascetic austerity, self-study of scripture, and worship of God —

371.s:
bhūtāpīḍā hy ahiṃsā syādahiṃsā dharma uttamaḥ /
yathā gajapade 'nyāni(2) padāni pathagāmināṃ(3) //
371.d:
भूतापीडा ह्य् अहिंसा स्यादहिंसा धर्म उत्तमः /
यथा गजपदे ऽन्यानि(2) पदानि पथगामिनां(3) //
371.m:
Non-injury to living beings is non-violence; non-violence is the highest dharma.
Just as the footprints of other path-goers [are contained] in an elephant's footprint,

371.s:
evaṃ sarvamahiṃsāyāṃ dharmārthamabhidhīyate /
udvegajananaṃ hiṃsā santāpakaraṇantathā //
371.d:
एवं सर्वमहिंसायां धर्मार्थमभिधीयते /
उद्वेगजननं हिंसा सन्तापकरणन्तथा //
371.m:
so all [virtue] is stated to reside within non-violence for the sake of dharma.
Causing agitation is violence, as is inflicting torment,

371.s:
rukkṛtiḥ śonitakṛtiḥ paiśunyakaraṇantathā /
:n
1 brahmaprakāśanaṃ jñānamiti ña..
2 yathā nāgapade 'nyānīti ka..
3 padagāmināmiti kha.. , ja.. ca
:p 314
hitasyātiniṣedhaś ca marmodghāṭanameva ca //
371.d:
रुक्कृतिः शोनितकृतिः पैशुन्यकरणन्तथा /
:न्
1 ब्रह्मप्रकाशनं ज्ञानमिति ञ..
2 यथा नागपदे ऽन्यानीति क..
3 पदगामिनामिति ख.. , ज.. च
:प् 314
हितस्यातिनिषेधश् च मर्मोद्घाटनमेव च //
371.m:
causing pain, shedding blood, and likewise slander,
[Footnote]
1 In manuscript ña: "brahmaprakāśanaṃ jñānam"
2 In manuscript ka: "yathā nāgapade 'nyāni"
3 In manuscripts kha and ja: "padagāminām"
[page 314]
excessive obstruction of what is beneficial, and laying bare vulnerable points,

371.s:
sukhāpahnutiḥ saṃrodho badho daśavithā ca sā /
yadbhūtahitamatyantaṃ vacaḥ satyasya lakṣaṇaṃ //
371.d:
सुखापह्नुतिः संरोधो बधो दशविथा च सा /
यद्भूतहितमत्यन्तं वचः सत्यस्य लक्षणं //
371.m:
deprivation of happiness, confinement, and killing — thus it is of ten kinds.
Speech that is entirely beneficial to living beings is the defining mark of truthfulness.

371.s:
satyaṃ brūyātpriyaṃ brūyānna brūyātsatyamapriyaṃ /
priyañca nānṛtaṃ brūyādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ //
371.d:
सत्यं ब्रूयात्प्रियं ब्रूयान्न ब्रूयात्सत्यमप्रियं /
प्रियञ्च नानृतं ब्रूयादेष धर्मः सनातनः //
371.m:
One should speak the truth; one should speak what is pleasing; one should not speak an unpleasant truth;
and one should not speak an agreeable falsehood: this is the eternal dharma.

371.s:
maithunasya parityāgo brahmacaryantadaṣṭadhā /
smaraṇaṃ kīrtanaṃ keliḥ prekṣyaṇaṃ guhyabhāṣaṇaṃ //
371.d:
मैथुनस्य परित्यागो ब्रह्मचर्यन्तदष्टधा /
स्मरणं कीर्तनं केलिः प्रेक्ष्यणं गुह्यभाषणं //
371.m:
Celibacy is the renunciation of sexual union; it is of eight kinds:
remembering, speaking about it, dalliance, gazing, secret conversation,

371.s:
saṅkalpo 'dhyavasāyaś ca kriyānirvṛttireva ca /
etanmaithunamaṣṭāṅgaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ //
371.d:
सङ्कल्पो ऽध्यवसायश् च क्रियानिर्वृत्तिरेव च /
एतन्मैथुनमष्टाङ्गं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः //
371.m:
resolve, determination, and the actual performance of the act —
this the wise declare to be eightfold sexual engagement.

371.s:
brahmacaryaṃ kriyāmūlamanyathā viphalā kriyā /
vasiṣṭhaś candramāḥ śukro devācāryaḥ pitāmahaḥ //
371.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यं क्रियामूलमन्यथा विफला क्रिया /
वसिष्ठश् चन्द्रमाः शुक्रो देवाचार्यः पितामहः //
371.m:
Celibacy is the foundation of ritual acts; otherwise, an act is fruitless.
Vasiṣṭha, Candramas, Śukra, the teacher of the gods [Bṛhaspati], and the Grandfather [Brahmā] —

371.s:
tapovṛddhā vayovṛddhāste 'pi strībhirvimohitāḥ /
gauḍī paiṣṭī ca mādhvī ca vijñeyāstrividhāḥ surāḥ //
371.d:
तपोवृद्धा वयोवृद्धास्ते ऽपि स्त्रीभिर्विमोहिताः /
गौडी पैष्टी च माध्वी च विज्ञेयास्त्रिविधाः सुराः //
371.m:
though mature in ascetic austerity and mature in years, even they were thoroughly deluded by women.
Liquor is to be understood as threefold: made from molasses, made from flour, and made from honey.

371.s:
caturthī strī surā jñeyā yayedaṃ mohitaṃ jagat /
mādyati pramadāṃ dṛṣṭvā surāṃ pītvā tu mādyati //
371.d:
चतुर्थी स्त्री सुरा ज्ञेया ययेदं मोहितं जगत् /
माद्यति प्रमदां दृष्ट्वा सुरां पीत्वा तु माद्यति //
371.m:
Woman is to be known as a fourth liquor, by which this world is intoxicated;
one is intoxicated simply by looking upon a woman, whereas one is intoxicated [only] by drinking liquor.

371.s:
yasmāddṛṣṭamadā nārī tasmāttānnāvalokayet /
yadvā tadvāparadravyamapahṛtya balānnaraḥ //
371.d:
यस्माद्दृष्टमदा नारी तस्मात्तान्नावलोकयेत् /
यद्वा तद्वापरद्रव्यमपहृत्य बलान्नरः //
371.m:
Because a woman intoxicates upon being seen, therefore one should not gaze at her.
A man who forcibly carries off another's property, whatever it may be,

371.s:
avaśyaṃ yāti tiryaktvaṃ jagdhvā caivāhutaṃ haviḥ /
kaupīnācchādanaṃ vāsaḥ kanthāṃ śītanivāriṇīṃ //
371.d:
अवश्यं याति तिर्यक्त्वं जग्ध्वा चैवाहुतं हविः /
कौपीनाच्छादनं वासः कन्थां शीतनिवारिणीं //
371.m:
inevitably attains birth as an animal, as does one who eats an unoffered oblation.
A covering loincloth, garments, a patched cloth warding off the cold,

371.s:
pāduke cāpi gṛhṇīyāt kuryānnānyasya saṃgrahaṃ /
dehasthitinimittasya vastrādeḥ syātparigrahaḥ //
371.d:
पादुके चापि गृह्णीयात् कुर्यान्नान्यस्य संग्रहं /
देहस्थितिनिमित्तस्य वस्त्रादेः स्यात्परिग्रहः //
371.m:
and sandals one may accept; one should make no accumulation of anything else.
Possessions such as clothing should be only for the sake of the body's maintenance.

371.s:
śarīraṃ dharmasaṃyuktaṃ rakṣaṇīyaṃ prayatnataḥ /
śaucantu dvividhaṃ proktaṃ vāhyamabhyantaraṃ tathā //
:p 315
371.d:
शरीरं धर्मसंयुक्तं रक्षणीयं प्रयत्नतः /
शौचन्तु द्विविधं प्रोक्तं वाह्यमभ्यन्तरं तथा //
:प् 315
371.m:
The body, united with dharma, must be protected with diligence.
Ritual purity is stated to be twofold: external as well as internal.
[page 315]

371.s:
gṛjjalābhyāṃ smṛtaṃ vāhyaṃ bhāvaśuddherathāntaraṃ /
ubhayena śuciryastu sa śucirnetaraḥ śuciḥ //
371.d:
गृज्जलाभ्यां स्मृतं वाह्यं भावशुद्धेरथान्तरं /
उभयेन शुचिर्यस्तु स शुचिर्नेतरः शुचिः //
371.m:
External [purity] is known to be through earth and water; internal is from the purification of disposition.
He who is pure in both respects is truly pure; no other is pure.

371.s:
yathā kathañcitprāptyā ca santoṣastuṣṭirucyate /
manasaścendriyāṇāñca aikāgryaṃ tapa ucyate //
371.d:
यथा कथञ्चित्प्राप्त्या च सन्तोषस्तुष्टिरुच्यते /
मनसश्चेन्द्रियाणाञ्च ऐकाग्र्यं तप उच्यते //
371.m:
Contentment is called satisfaction with whatever is obtained somehow or other.
Single-pointedness of the mind and the senses is called ascetic austerity.

371.s:
tajjayaḥ sarvadharmebhyaḥ sa dharmaḥ para ucyate /
vācikaṃ mantrajapyādi mānasaṃ rāgavarjanaṃ //
371.d:
तज्जयः सर्वधर्मेभ्यः स धर्मः पर उच्यते /
वाचिकं मन्त्रजप्यादि मानसं रागवर्जनं //
371.m:
Mastery of that is above all dharmas; that is declared to be the supreme dharma.
Vocal [austerity] consists of recitation of mantras and the like; mental is the abandonment of passion;

371.s:
śārīraṃ devapūjādi sarvadantu tridhā tapaḥ /
praṇavādyāstato vedāḥ praṇave paryavasthitāḥ //
371.d:
शारीरं देवपूजादि सर्वदन्तु त्रिधा तपः /
प्रणवाद्यास्ततो वेदाः प्रणवे पर्यवस्थिताः //
371.m:
bodily consists of the worship of deities and the like: thus ascetic austerity is of three kinds in all respects.
The Vedas begin with the Praṇava, and therefore are established in the Praṇava.

371.s:
vāṅmayaḥ praṇavaḥ sarvaṃ tasmātpraṇavamabhyaset /
akāraś ca tathokāro makāraścārdhamātrayā //
371.d:
वाङ्मयः प्रणवः सर्वं तस्मात्प्रणवमभ्यसेत् /
अकारश् च तथोकारो मकारश्चार्धमात्रया //
371.m:
The Praṇava is all that is made of speech; therefore one should practise the Praṇava.
The letter 'A', the letter 'U', and the letter 'M' with a half-mora —

371.s:
tisro mātrāstrayo vedāḥ lokā bhūrādayo guṇāḥ /
jāgratsvapnaḥ suṣuptiś ca brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ //
371.d:
तिस्रो मात्रास्त्रयो वेदाः लोका भूरादयो गुणाः /
जाग्रत्स्वप्नः सुषुप्तिश् च ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः //
371.m:
these three morae are the three Vedas, the worlds beginning with Bhūḥ, the guṇas,
waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara,

371.s:
pradyumnaḥ śrīrvāsudevaḥ sarvamoṅgārakaḥ kramāt /
amātro naṣṭamātraś ca dvaitasyāpagamaḥ śivaḥ //
371.d:
प्रद्युम्नः श्रीर्वासुदेवः सर्वमोङ्गारकः क्रमात् /
अमात्रो नष्टमात्रश् च द्वैतस्यापगमः शिवः //
371.m:
Pradyumna, Śrī, and Vāsudeva: in succession, the syllable Oṃ is everything.
Partless, with morae dissolved, Śiva is the departure of duality.

371.s:
oṅkāro vidito yena sa munirnetaro muniḥ /
caturthī mātrā gāndhārī prayuktā mūrdhnilakṣyate //
371.d:
ओङ्कारो विदितो येन स मुनिर्नेतरो मुनिः /
चतुर्थी मात्रा गान्धारी प्रयुक्ता मूर्ध्निलक्ष्यते //
371.m:
He by whom the syllable Oṃ is known is a sage; no other is a sage.
The fourth mora, gāndhārī, when applied, is perceived at the crown of the head.

371.s:
tatturīyaṃ paraṃ brahma jyotirdīpo ghaṭe yathā /
tathā hṛtpadmanilayaṃ dhyāyennityaṃ japennaraḥ //
371.d:
तत्तुरीयं परं ब्रह्म ज्योतिर्दीपो घटे यथा /
तथा हृत्पद्मनिलयं ध्यायेन्नित्यं जपेन्नरः //
371.m:
That is the fourth state, the supreme Brahman, a light like a lamp inside a jar.
Likewise, residing in the lotus of the heart, a man should constantly meditate upon it and recite it.

371.s:
praṇavo dhanuḥ śaro hy ātmā brahma tallakṣyamucyate /
apramattena veddhavyaṃ śaravattanmayo bhavet //
371.d:
प्रणवो धनुः शरो ह्य् आत्मा ब्रह्म तल्लक्ष्यमुच्यते /
अप्रमत्तेन वेद्धव्यं शरवत्तन्मयो भवेत् //
371.m:
The Praṇava is the bow, the self is the arrow, and Brahman is said to be that target;
it must be pierced without distraction, and like the arrow one should become identified with it.

371.s:
etedekākṣaraṃ brahma etadekākṣaraṃ paraṃ /
detadekākṣaraṃ jñātvā yo yadicchati tasya tat //
371.d:
एतेदेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म एतदेकाक्षरं परं /
देतदेकाक्षरं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत् //
371.m:
This single syllable is Brahman; this single syllable is the supreme.
Having known this single syllable, whatever one desires becomes one's own.

371.s:
chando 'sya devī gāyatrī antaryāmī ṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ /
:p 316
devatā paramātmāsya niyogo bhuktimuktaye //
371.d:
छन्दो ऽस्य देवी गायत्री अन्तर्यामी ऋषिः स्मृतः /
:प् 316
देवता परमात्मास्य नियोगो भुक्तिमुक्तये //

371.s:
bhūragnyātmane hṛdayaṃ bhuvaḥ prājāpatyātmane /
śiraḥ svaḥsūryātmane ca śikhā kavacamucyate //
371.d:
भूरग्न्यात्मने हृदयं भुवः प्राजापत्यात्मने /
शिरः स्वःसूर्यात्मने च शिखा कवचमुच्यते //
371.m:
"Bhūḥ, to the self of Agni" is the heart; "Bhuvaḥ, to the self of Prajāpati" is the head;
and "Svaḥ, to the self of the Sun" is the topknot; the armor is declared [next].

371.s:
oṃbhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥkavacaṃ satyātmane tato 'strakaṃ /
vinyasya pūjayedviṣṇuṃ japedvai bhuktimuktaye //
371.d:
ओंभूर्भुवः स्वःकवचं सत्यात्मने ततो ऽस्त्रकं /
विन्यस्य पूजयेद्विष्णुं जपेद्वै भुक्तिमुक्तये //
371.m:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ" is the armor; then "to the self of Truth" is the weapon.
Having performed the ritual deposition, one should worship Viṣṇu and perform recitation for worldly enjoyment and liberation.

371.s:
juhuyācca tilājyādi sarvaṃ sampadyate nare /
yastu dvādaśasāhasraṃ japamanvahamācaret //
371.d:
जुहुयाच्च तिलाज्यादि सर्वं सम्पद्यते नरे /
यस्तु द्वादशसाहस्रं जपमन्वहमाचरेत् //
371.m:
One should also offer oblations of sesame, clarified butter, and other substances; everything is accomplished for that person.
He who daily performs twelve thousand recitations —

371.s:
tasya dvādaśabhirmāsaiḥ paraṃ brahma prakāśate /
animādi koṭijapyāllakṣātsārasvatādikaṃ //
371.d:
तस्य द्वादशभिर्मासैः परं ब्रह्म प्रकाशते /
अनिमादि कोटिजप्याल्लक्षात्सारस्वतादिकं //
371.m:
to him the supreme Brahman shines forth in twelve months.
Supernatural powers such as atomicity come from ten million recitations, and eloquence and the like from one hundred thousand.

371.s:
vaidikastāntriko miśro viṣṇārvai trividho makhaḥ /
trayānāmīpsitenaikavidhinā harimarcayet //
371.d:
वैदिकस्तान्त्रिको मिश्रो विष्णार्वै त्रिविधो मखः /
त्रयानामीप्सितेनैकविधिना हरिमर्चयेत् //
371.m:
Sacrifice to Viṣṇu is threefold: Vedic, Tantric, and mixed.
One should worship Hari by one chosen rule out of the three.

371.s:
praṇamya daṇḍavadbhūmau namaskāreṇa yo 'rcayet /
sa yāṅgatimavāpnoti na tāṃ kratuśatair api //
371.d:
प्रणम्य दण्डवद्भूमौ नमस्कारेण यो ऽर्चयेत् /
स याङ्गतिमवाप्नोति न तां क्रतुशतैर् अपि //
371.m:
Having bowed like a staff on the ground, he who worships with prostration
attains a state that one does not attain even with a hundred sacrificial rites.

371.s:
yasya deve parā bhaktiryathā deve tathā gurau /
tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yamaniyamā nāmaikasaptatyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ
:p 317
:ś atha dvisaptyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
āsanaprāṇāyāmapratyāhārāḥ
371.d:
यस्य देवे परा भक्तिर्यथा देवे तथा गुरौ /
तस्यैते कथिता ह्य् अर्थाः प्रकाशन्ते महात्मनः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे यमनियमा नामैकसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः
:प् 317
:श् अथ द्विसप्त्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
आसनप्राणायामप्रत्याहाराः
371.m:
He who has supreme devotion to the deity, and as to the deity, so to the guru —
to that great soul these truths that have been spoken shine forth.
Thus ends the three hundred and seventy-first chapter, named "Restraints and Observances", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[page 317]
Now begins the three hundred and seventy-second chapter.
Posture, Breath Control, and Sensory Withdrawal

372.s:
agnir uvāca
āsanaṃ kamalādyuktaṃ tadbaddhvā cintayetparaṃ /
śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ //
372.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
आसनं कमलाद्युक्तं तद्बद्ध्वा चिन्तयेत्परं /
शुचौ देशे प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्थिरमासनमात्मनः //
372.m:
Agni said:
The posture is said to be the lotus and others; having assumed that, one should contemplate the Supreme.
Having established a firm seat for oneself in a clean place,

372.s:
nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ celājinakuśottaraṃ /
tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yātacittendriyakriyaḥ //
372.d:
नात्युच्छ्रितं नातिनीचं चेलाजिनकुशोत्तरं /
तत्रैकाग्रं मनः कृत्वा यातचित्तेन्द्रियक्रियः //
372.m:
neither too elevated nor too low, overlaid with cloth, an animal skin, and kuśa grass,
having made the mind single-pointed there, with the activities of the mind and senses restrained,

372.s:
upaviśyāsane yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye /
samakāyaśīragrīvaṃ dhārayannacalaṃ sthiraḥ //
372.d:
उपविश्यासने युञ्ज्याद्योगमात्मविशुद्धये /
समकायशीरग्रीवं धारयन्नचलं स्थिरः //
372.m:
seated on the posture, steady, holding the body, head, and neck erect and motionless,
one should practise yoga for the purification of the self,

372.s:
samprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svandiśaścānavalokayan /
pārṣṇibhyāṃ vṛṣaṇau rakṣaṃs tathā prajananaṃ punaḥ //
372.d:
सम्प्रेक्ष्य नासिकाग्रं स्वन्दिशश्चानवलोकयन् /
पार्ष्णिभ्यां वृषणौ रक्षंस् तथा प्रजननं पुनः //
372.m:
gazing at the tip of one's own nose and not looking around at the directions,
guarding the testicles with the heels and likewise the genitals again,

372.s:
urubhyāmuparisthāpya vāhū tiryak prayatnataḥ /
dakṣiṇaṃ karapṛṣṭhañca nyaseddhāmatalopari //
372.d:
उरुभ्यामुपरिस्थाप्य वाहू तिर्यक् प्रयत्नतः /
दक्षिणं करपृष्ठञ्च न्यसेद्धामतलोपरि //
372.m:
placing the arms across the thighs with care,
and one should place the back of the right hand on the left palm,

372.s:
unnamya śanakair vakraṃ mukhaṃ viṣṭabhya cāgrataḥ /
prāṇaḥ svadehajo vāyustasyāyāmo nirodhanaṃ //
372.d:
उन्नम्य शनकैर् वक्रं मुखं विष्टभ्य चाग्रतः /
प्राणः स्वदेहजो वायुस्तस्यायामो निरोधनं //
372.m:
raising the chin slowly, fixing the mouth forward.
Prāṇa is the wind born of one's own body; its extension is its restraint.

372.s:
nāsikāpuṭamaṅgulyā pīḍyaiva ca pareṇa ca /
ādaraṃ recayedvāyuṃ recanādrecakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
372.d:
नासिकापुटमङ्गुल्या पीड्यैव च परेण च /
आदरं रेचयेद्वायुं रेचनाद्रेचकः स्मृतः //
372.m: Pressing the nostril with the finger, one should carefully / expel the breath through the other; because of expelling (recana), it is called recaka.

372.s:
vāhyena vāyunā dehaṃ dṛtivat pūrayedyathā /
tathā purṇaś ca santiṣṭhet pūraṇāt pūrakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
372.d:
वाह्येन वायुना देहं दृतिवत् पूरयेद्यथा /
तथा पुर्णश् च सन्तिष्ठेत् पूरणात् पूरकः स्मृतः //
372.m: Just as one would fill a bellows with external air, / so one should remain filled in the body; because of filling (pūraṇa), it is called pūraka.

372.s:
na bhuñcati na gṛhṇāti vāyumantarvāhiḥsthitam /
sampūrṇakumbhavattiṣṭhedacalaḥ sa tu kumbhakaḥ //
:p 318
372.d:
न भुञ्चति न गृह्णाति वायुमन्तर्वाहिःस्थितम् /
सम्पूर्णकुम्भवत्तिष्ठेदचलः स तु कुम्भकः //
:प् 318
372.m:
Neither expelling nor taking in the breath that remains inside and outside, / one should stand motionless like a completely filled jar; that is kumbhaka.
[Page 318]

372.s:
kanyakaḥ(1) sakṛdudghātaḥ sa vai dvādaśamātrikaḥ /
madhyamaś ca dvirudghātaś caturviṃśatimātrikaḥ //
372.d:
कन्यकः(1) सकृदुद्घातः स वै द्वादशमात्रिकः /
मध्यमश् च द्विरुद्घातश् चतुर्विंशतिमात्रिकः //
372.m: The lowest [prāṇāyāma] has a single impact, consisting of twelve measures; / the middle one has two impacts, consisting of twenty-four measures;

372.s:
uttamaś ca trirudghātaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśattālamātrikaḥ /
svedakampābhidhātānām jananaścottamottamaḥ //
372.d:
उत्तमश् च त्रिरुद्घातः षट्त्रिंशत्तालमात्रिकः /
स्वेदकम्पाभिधातानाम् जननश्चोत्तमोत्तमः //
372.m: and the highest has three impacts, consisting of thirty-six beat-measures. / The highest of the highest produces sweat, trembling, and leaping.

372.s:
ajitānnāruhedbhūmiṃ hikkāśvāsādayas tathā /
jite prāṇe khalpadojavinmūtrādi prajāyate //
372.d:
अजितान्नारुहेद्भूमिं हिक्काश्वासादयस् तथा /
जिते प्राणे खल्पदोजविन्मूत्रादि प्रजायते //
372.m: Until it is conquered, he should not ascend the ground, lest hiccups, asthma, and the like occur; / when the breath is conquered, lightness of the body and scantiness of feces and urine are produced.

372.s:
ārogyaṃ śīghragāmitvamutsāhaḥ svarasauṣṭhavam /
balavarṇaprasādaś ca sarvadoṣakṣayaḥ phalaṃ //
372.d:
आरोग्यं शीघ्रगामित्वमुत्साहः स्वरसौष्ठवम् /
बलवर्णप्रसादश् च सर्वदोषक्षयः फलं //
372.m: Health, quickness of movement, zeal, excellence of voice, / strength, brightness of complexion, and the destruction of all disorders are the fruit.

372.s:
japadhyānaṃ vināgarbhaḥ sa garbhastatsamanvitaḥ /
indriyāṇāṃ jayārthāya sa garbhaṃ dhārayetparaṃ //
372.d:
जपध्यानं विनागर्भः स गर्भस्तत्समन्वितः /
इन्द्रियाणां जयार्थाय स गर्भं धारयेत्परं //
372.m: Without recitation and meditation it is agarbha; accompanied by them, it is sagarbha. / For the sake of conquering the senses, one should practice the supreme sagarbha [prāṇāyāma].

372.s:
jñānavairāgyayuktābhyāṃ prāṇāyāmavaśena ca /
indriyāṃś ca vinirjitya sarvameva jitaṃ bhavet //
372.d:
ज्ञानवैराग्ययुक्ताभ्यां प्राणायामवशेन च /
इन्द्रियांश् च विनिर्जित्य सर्वमेव जितं भवेत् //
372.m: By means of knowledge and detachment, and through the mastery of breath control, / having completely conquered the senses, everything indeed becomes conquered.

372.s:
indriyāṇyeva tatsarvaṃ yat svarganarakāvubhau /
nigṛhītavisṛṣṭāni svargāya narakāya ca //
372.d:
इन्द्रियाण्येव तत्सर्वं यत् स्वर्गनरकावुभौ /
निगृहीतविसृष्टानि स्वर्गाय नरकाय च //
372.m: The senses alone are all that constitutes both heaven and hell: / restrained, they lead to heaven; released, to hell.

372.s:
śarīraṃ rathamityāhurindriyāṇyasya vājinaḥ /
manaś ca sārathiḥ proktaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ kaśaḥ(2)smṛtaḥ //
372.d:
शरीरं रथमित्याहुरिन्द्रियाण्यस्य वाजिनः /
मनश् च सारथिः प्रोक्तः प्राणायामः कशः(2)स्मृतः //
372.m: They say the body is a chariot; its horses are the senses; / the mind is called the charioteer, and breath control is remembered as the whip.

372.s:
jñānavairāgyaraśmibhyāṃ sāyayā vidhṛtaṃ manaḥ /
śanair niścalatām eti prāṇāyāmaikasaṃhitam //
372.d:
ज्ञानवैराग्यरश्मिभ्यां सायया विधृतं मनः /
शनैर् निश्चलताम् एति प्राणायामैकसंहितम् //
372.m: Held firmly by the reins of knowledge and detachment, / the mind, joined uniquely with breath control, gradually attains motionlessness.

372.s:
jalavinduṃ kuśāgreṇa māse māse pivettu yaḥ /
saṃvatsaraśataṃ sāgraṃ prāṇayāmaś ca tatsamaḥ //
372.d:
जलविन्दुं कुशाग्रेण मासे मासे पिवेत्तु यः /
संवत्सरशतं साग्रं प्राणयामश् च तत्समः //
372.m: If someone were to drink a drop of water on the tip of a kuśa grass blade month after month / for a full hundred years, breath control is equal to that [austerity].

372.s:
indriyāṇi prasaktāni praviśya viṣayodadhau /
:n
1 kanyasa iti ña..
2 prāṇāyāmo 'ṅkuśa iti jha..
:p 319
āhṛtya yo nigṛhṇāti pratyāhāraḥ sa ucyate //
372.d:
इन्द्रियाणि प्रसक्तानि प्रविश्य विषयोदधौ /
:न्
1 कन्यस इति ञ..
2 प्राणायामो ऽङ्कुश इति झ..
:प् 319
आहृत्य यो निगृह्णाति प्रत्याहारः स उच्यते //
372.m:
When the senses, clinging [to objects], plunge into the ocean of sense objects,
[Notes]
1. "kanyasa" according to manuscript ña.
2. "prāṇāyāmo 'ṅkuśa" according to manuscript jha.
[Page 319]
withdrawing and restraining them is called pratyāhāra (sensory withdrawal).

372.s:
uddharedātmanātmānaṃ majjamānaṃ yathāmbhasi /
bhoganadyativegena(1) jñānavṛkṣaṃ samāśrayet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe āsanaprāṇāyāmapratyāhārā nāma
dvisaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha trisaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dhyānam
372.d:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं मज्जमानं यथाम्भसि /
भोगनद्यतिवेगेन(1) ज्ञानवृक्षं समाश्रयेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे आसनप्राणायामप्रत्याहारा नाम
द्विसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ त्रिसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
ध्यानम्
372.m:
One should rescue oneself by oneself when sinking as if in water; / against the overwhelming current of the river of worldly pleasures, one should resort to the tree of knowledge.
Thus ends the three hundred and seventy-second chapter, entitled 'Posture, Breath Control, and Sensory Withdrawal', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the three hundred and seventy-third chapter.
Meditation

373.s:
agnir uvāca
dhyai cintāyāṃ smṛto dhāturviṣṇucintā muhūrmuhuḥ /
anākṣiptena manasā dhyānamityabhidhīyate //
373.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ध्यै चिन्तायां स्मृतो धातुर्विष्णुचिन्ता मुहूर्मुहुः /
अनाक्षिप्तेन मनसा ध्यानमित्यभिधीयते //
373.m: Agni said: / The root dhyai is remembered in the sense of reflection; constant reflection upon Viṣṇu / with an undistracted mind is called meditation (dhyāna).

373.s:
ātmanaḥ samanaskasya muktāśeṣopadhasya ca /
brahmacintāsamā śaktirdhyānaṃ nāma taducyate //
373.d:
आत्मनः समनस्कस्य मुक्ताशेषोपधस्य च /
ब्रह्मचिन्तासमा शक्तिर्ध्यानं नाम तदुच्यते //
373.m: The capacity of the self, equipped with the mind and freed of all conditioning, / that is equal to the reflection on Brahman, is called meditation.

373.s:
dhyeyālambanasaṃsthasya sadṛśapratyayasya ca /
pratyāntaranirmuktaḥ pratyayo dhyānamucyate //
373.d:
ध्येयालम्बनसंस्थस्य सदृशप्रत्ययस्य च /
प्रत्यान्तरनिर्मुक्तः प्रत्ययो ध्यानमुच्यते //
373.m: A continuous cognition resting upon the object of meditation, consisting of similar thoughts / and free from any other cognition, is called meditation.

373.s:
dhyeyāvasthitacittasya pradeśe yatra kutricit /
dhyānametatsamuddiṣṭaṃ pratyayasyaikabhāvanā //
373.d:
ध्येयावस्थितचित्तस्य प्रदेशे यत्र कुत्रिचित् /
ध्यानमेतत्समुद्दिष्टं प्रत्ययस्यैकभावना //
373.m: For a mind fixed on the object of meditation in any place whatsoever, / this single concentration of cognition is taught as meditation.

373.s:
evaṃ dhyānasamāyuktaḥ khadehaṃ yaḥ parityajet /
kulaṃ svajanamitrāṇi samuddhṛtya harirbhavet //
373.d:
एवं ध्यानसमायुक्तः खदेहं यः परित्यजेत् /
कुलं स्वजनमित्राणि समुद्धृत्य हरिर्भवेत् //
373.m: One endowed with such meditation who abandons his body / delivers his family, kinsmen, and friends, and becomes Hari.

373.s:
evaṃ muhūrtamardhaṃ vā dhyāyed yaḥ śraddhayā hariṃ /
sopi yāṃ gatimāpnoti na tāṃ sarvair mahāmakhaiḥ //
:n
1 bhoganadyabhiveśeneti ña..
:p 320
373.d:
एवं मुहूर्तमर्धं वा ध्यायेद् यः श्रद्धया हरिं /
सोपि यां गतिमाप्नोति न तां सर्वैर् महामखैः //
:न्
1 भोगनद्यभिवेशेनेति ञ..
:प् 320
373.m:
One who meditates on Hari with faith in this way even for a muhūrta or half [a muhūrta] / attains a destination that cannot be reached by all the great sacrifices.
[Notes]
1. "bhoganadyabhiveśena" according to manuscript ña.
[Page 320]

373.s:
dhyātā dhyānaṃ tathā dhyeyaṃ yacca dhyānaprayojanaṃ /
etaccatuṣṭayaṃ jñātvā yogaṃ yuñjīta tattvavit //
373.d:
ध्याता ध्यानं तथा ध्येयं यच्च ध्यानप्रयोजनं /
एतच्चतुष्टयं ज्ञात्वा योगं युञ्जीत तत्त्ववित् //
373.m: The meditator, meditation, the object of meditation, and the purpose of meditation: / having known this tetrad, the knower of truth should practice yoga.

373.s:
yogābhyāsādbhavenmūktiraiśvaryañcāṣṭadhā mahat /
jñānavairāgyasampannaḥ śraddadhānaḥ kṣamānvitaḥ //
373.d:
योगाभ्यासाद्भवेन्मूक्तिरैश्वर्यञ्चाष्टधा महत् /
ज्ञानवैराग्यसम्पन्नः श्रद्दधानः क्षमान्वितः //
373.m: From the practice of yoga liberation arises, as well as great eightfold sovereignty. / Endowed with knowledge and detachment, faithful, patient,

373.s:
viṣṇubhaktaḥ sadotsāhī dhyātetthaṃ puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ /
mūrtāmūrtaṃ parambrahma harerdhyānaṃ hi cintanam //
373.d:
विष्णुभक्तः सदोत्साही ध्यातेत्थं पुरुषः स्मृतः /
मूर्तामूर्तं परम्ब्रह्म हरेर्ध्यानं हि चिन्तनम् //
373.m: devoted to Viṣṇu, and ever enthusiastic, such a person is remembered as the meditator. / The Supreme Brahman is both formed and formless; meditation on Hari is indeed reflection [upon it].

373.s:
sakalo niṣkalo jñeyaḥ sarvajñaḥ paramo hariḥ /
aṇimādiguṇaiśvaryaṃ muktirdhyānaprayojanam //
373.d:
सकलो निष्कलो ज्ञेयः सर्वज्ञः परमो हरिः /
अणिमादिगुणैश्वर्यं मुक्तिर्ध्यानप्रयोजनम् //
373.m: The supreme Hari is to be known as with parts and without parts, omniscient. / Sovereignty with the qualities such as atomicity (aṇimā), and liberation, are the purpose of meditation.

373.s:
phalena yojako viṣṇurato dhyāyet pareśvaraṃ /
gacchaṃstiṣṭhan svapan jāgradunmiṣan nimiṣannapi //
373.d:
फलेन योजको विष्णुरतो ध्यायेत् परेश्वरं /
गच्छंस्तिष्ठन् स्वपन् जाग्रदुन्मिषन् निमिषन्नपि //
373.m: Viṣṇu joins [one] with the fruit; therefore one should meditate on the Supreme Lord / while walking, standing, sleeping, waking, and opening or closing the eyes.

373.s:
śucirvāpyaśucirvāpi dhyāyet śatatamīśvaram /
svadehāyatanasyānte manasi sthāpya keśavam //
373.d:
शुचिर्वाप्यशुचिर्वापि ध्यायेत् शततमीश्वरम् /
स्वदेहायतनस्यान्ते मनसि स्थाप्य केशवम् //
373.m: Whether pure or impure, one should constantly meditate on the Lord, / establishing Keśava in the mind within the shrine of one's own body.

373.s:
hṛtpadmapīṭhikāmadhye dhyānayogena(1) pūjayet /
dhyānayajñaḥ paraḥ śuddhaḥ sarvadoṣavivarjitaḥ //
373.d:
हृत्पद्मपीठिकामध्ये ध्यानयोगेन(1) पूजयेत् /
ध्यानयज्ञः परः शुद्धः सर्वदोषविवर्जितः //
373.m: In the middle of the pedestal of the heart lotus, one should worship [him] through the yoga of meditation. / The sacrifice of meditation is supreme, pure, and devoid of all defects;

373.s:
teneṣṭvā muktimāpnoti vāhyaśuddhaiś ca nādhvaraiḥ /
hiṃsādoṣavimuktitvādviśuddhiścittasādhanaḥ //
373.d:
तेनेष्ट्वा मुक्तिमाप्नोति वाह्यशुद्धैश् च नाध्वरैः /
हिंसादोषविमुक्तित्वाद्विशुद्धिश्चित्तसाधनः //
373.m: having sacrificed with it, one attains liberation, and not by external sacrifices even if pure; / because it is free from the sin of violence, this purifier is accomplished by the mind.

373.s:
dhyānayajñaḥ parastasmādapavargaphalapradaḥ /
tasmādśuddhaṃ santyajya hy anityaṃ vāhyasādhanaṃ //
373.d:
ध्यानयज्ञः परस्तस्मादपवर्गफलप्रदः /
तस्माद्शुद्धं सन्त्यज्य ह्य् अनित्यं वाह्यसाधनं //
373.m: Therefore the sacrifice of meditation is supreme, bestowing the fruit of final liberation. / Therefore, having abandoned what is impure and impermanent, namely the external means,

373.s:
yajñādyaṃ karma santyajya yogamatyarthamabhyaset /
vikāramuktamavyaktaṃ bhogyabhogasamanvitaṃ //
373.d:
यज्ञाद्यं कर्म सन्त्यज्य योगमत्यर्थमभ्यसेत् /
विकारमुक्तमव्यक्तं भोग्यभोगसमन्वितं //
373.m: and having renounced action such as sacrifice, one should intensely practice yoga. / One should first reflect in the heart on the unmanifest, free from modification, / endowed with the enjoyer and objects of enjoyment, and initially upon the three guṇas in succession:

373.s:
cintayeddhṛdaye pūrvaṃ kramādādau guṇatrayaṃ /
tamaḥ pracchādya rajasā sattvena cchādayedrajaḥ //
:n
1 dhyānamārgeṇeti kha.. , ja.. ca
:p 321
373.d:
चिन्तयेद्धृदये पूर्वं क्रमादादौ गुणत्रयं /
तमः प्रच्छाद्य रजसा सत्त्वेन च्छादयेद्रजः //
:न्
1 ध्यानमार्गेणेति ख.. , ज.. च
:प् 321
373.m:
covering darkness (tamas) with passion (rajas), and covering passion with purity (sattva).
[Notes]
1. "dhyānamārgeṇa" according to manuscripts kha and ja.
[Page 321]

373.s:
dhyāyettrimaṇḍalaṃ pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ raktaṃ sitaṃ kramāt /
sattvopādhiguṇātītaḥ puruṣaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ(1) //
373.d:
ध्यायेत्त्रिमण्डलं पूर्वं कृष्णं रक्तं सितं क्रमात् /
सत्त्वोपाधिगुणातीतः पुरुषः पञ्चविंशकः(1) //
373.m: One should first meditate on the three circles, successively black, red, and white. / Beyond the quality of the conditioning of sattva is the Spirit (puruṣa), the twenty-fifth [principle].

373.s:
dhyeyametadaśuddhañca tyaktvā śuddhaṃ vicintayet /
aiśvaryaṃ paṅkajaṃ divyaṃ puruśopari saṃsthitaṃ //
373.d:
ध्येयमेतदशुद्धञ्च त्यक्त्वा शुद्धं विचिन्तयेत् /
ऐश्वर्यं पङ्कजं दिव्यं पुरुशोपरि संस्थितं //
373.m: Having abandoned this impure object of meditation, one should reflect on the pure: / the divine lotus of sovereignty situated above the Puruṣa,

373.s:
dvādaśāṅgulavistīrṇaṃ śuddhaṃ vikaśitaṃ sitaṃ /
nālamaṣṭāṅṇūlaṃ tasya nābhikandasamudbhavaṃ //
373.d:
द्वादशाङ्गुलविस्तीर्णं शुद्धं विकशितं सितं /
नालमष्टाङ्णूलं तस्य नाभिकन्दसमुद्भवं //
373.m: twelve finger-breadths wide, pure, blossoming, and white, / its stalk measuring eight finger-breadths, springing from the bulb of the navel.

373.s:
padmapatrāṣṭakaṃ jñeyamaṇimādiguṇāṣṭakam /
karṇikākeśaraṃ nālaṃ jñānavairāgyamuttamam //
373.d:
पद्मपत्राष्टकं ज्ञेयमणिमादिगुणाष्टकम् /
कर्णिकाकेशरं नालं ज्ञानवैराग्यमुत्तमम् //
373.m: The eight petals of the lotus are to be known as the eight qualities such as atomicity; / the pericarp, filaments, and stalk are supreme knowledge and detachment;

373.s:
viṣṇudharmaś ca tatkandamiti padmaṃ vicintayet /
taddharmajñānavairāgyaṃ śivaiśvaryamayaṃ paraṃ //
373.d:
विष्णुधर्मश् च तत्कन्दमिति पद्मं विचिन्तयेत् /
तद्धर्मज्ञानवैराग्यं शिवैश्वर्यमयं परं //
373.m: and Viṣṇu's righteousness is its bulb—thus one should visualize the lotus. / Its righteousness, knowledge, detachment, and supreme divine sovereignty,

373.s:
jñātvā padmāsanaṃ sarvaṃ sarvaduḥkhāntamāpnuyāt /
tatpadmakarṇikāmadhye śuddhadīpaśikhākṛtiṃ(2) //
373.d:
ज्ञात्वा पद्मासनं सर्वं सर्वदुःखान्तमाप्नुयात् /
तत्पद्मकर्णिकामध्ये शुद्धदीपशिखाकृतिं(2) //
373.m: knowing that lotus seat entirely, one reaches the end of all suffering. / In the middle of the pericarp of that lotus, having the form of a pure flame of a lamp,

373.s:
aṅguṣṭhamātramamalaṃ dhyāyedoṅkāramīśvaraṃ /
kadambagolakākāraṃ tāraṃ rūpamiva sthitaṃ //
373.d:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रममलं ध्यायेदोङ्कारमीश्वरं /
कदम्बगोलकाकारं तारं रूपमिव स्थितं //
373.m: the size of a thumb, stainless, one should meditate on the Lord as the syllable Oṃ, / shaped like a round kadamba blossom, standing like a radiant star.

373.s:
dhyāyedvā raśmijālena dīpyamānaṃ samantataḥ /
pradhānaṃ puruṣātītaṃ sthitaṃ padmasthamīśvaraṃ //
373.d:
ध्यायेद्वा रश्मिजालेन दीप्यमानं समन्ततः /
प्रधानं पुरुषातीतं स्थितं पद्मस्थमीश्वरं //
373.m: Or one should meditate on the Lord who is blazing on all sides with a mass of rays, / beyond Pradhāna and Puruṣa, seated upon the lotus.

373.s:
dhyāyejjapecca satatamoṅkāraṃ paramakṣaraṃ /
manaḥsthityarthamicchānti sthūladhyānamanukramāt //
373.d:
ध्यायेज्जपेच्च सततमोङ्कारं परमक्षरं /
मनःस्थित्यर्थमिच्छान्ति स्थूलध्यानमनुक्रमात् //
373.m: One should constantly meditate on and recite the syllable Oṃ, the supreme imperishable. / For the sake of steadying the mind, they desire gross meditation in progressive order.

373.s:
tadbhūtaṃ niś calībhūtaṃ labhet sūkṣme 'pi saṃsthitaṃ /
nābhikande sthitaṃ nālaṃ daśāṅgulasamāyataṃ //
373.d:
तद्भूतं निश् चलीभूतं लभेत् सूक्ष्मे ऽपि संस्थितं /
नाभिकन्दे स्थितं नालं दशाङ्गुलसमायतं //
373.m: When it has become steady there, one attains [absorption] even in the subtle. / The stalk situated in the bulb of the navel is ten finger-breadths in length;

373.s:
nālenāṣṭadalaṃ padmaṃ dvādaśāṅgulavistṛtaṃ /
:n
1 sattvopādhisamāyuktaḥ sadā dhyeyaś ca keśava iti kha..
2 labdhadīpaśikhākṛtimiti kha.. , ña.. ca
:p 322
sakarṇike kesarāle sūryasomāgnimaṇḍalaṃ //
373.d:
नालेनाष्टदलं पद्मं द्वादशाङ्गुलविस्तृतं /
:न्
1 सत्त्वोपाधिसमायुक्तः सदा ध्येयश् च केशव इति ख..
2 लब्धदीपशिखाकृतिमिति ख.. , ञ.. च
:प् 322
सकर्णिके केसराले सूर्यसोमाग्निमण्डलं //
373.m:
upon the stalk is an eight-petaled lotus, twelve finger-breadths wide;
[Notes]
1. "sattvopādhisamāyuktaḥ sadā dhyeyaś ca keśava" according to manuscript kha.
2. "labdhadīpaśikhākṛtim" according to manuscripts kha and ña.
[Page 322]
With a pericarp and filaments, [within] the maṇḍala of the sun, moon, and fire.

373.s:
agnimaṇḍalamadhyasthaḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
padmī caturbhujo viṣṇuratha vāṣṭabhujo hariḥ //
373.d:
अग्निमण्डलमध्यस्थः शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः /
पद्मी चतुर्भुजो विष्णुरथ वाष्टभुजो हरिः //
373.m: Situated in the middle of the fire-maṇḍala, holding a conch, discus, and mace, / Viṣṇu has four arms with a lotus, or else Hari has eight arms:

373.s:
śārṅgākṣavalayadharaḥ pāśāṅkuśadharaḥ paraḥ /
svarṇavarṇaḥ śvetavarṇaḥ saśrovatsaḥ sakaustubhaḥ //
373.d:
शार्ङ्गाक्षवलयधरः पाशाङ्कुशधरः परः /
स्वर्णवर्णः श्वेतवर्णः सश्रोवत्सः सकौस्तुभः //
373.m: The Supreme holds a bow and a rosary, holds a noose and a goad, / gold-coloured, white-coloured, possessing the Śrīvatsa mark and the Kaustubha gem,

373.s:
vanamālī svarṇahārī sphuranmakarakuṇḍalaḥ /
ratnojjvalakirīṭaś ca pītāmbaradharo mahān //
373.d:
वनमाली स्वर्णहारी स्फुरन्मकरकुण्डलः /
रत्नोज्ज्वलकिरीटश् च पीताम्बरधरो महान् //
373.m: wearing a garland of wild flowers, wearing a gold necklace, with glittering crocodile-shaped earrings, / crowned with a diadem radiant with jewels, wearing yellow garments, great,

373.s:
sarvābharaṇabhūṣāḍhyo vitastarvā yathecchayā /
ahaṃ brahma jyotirātmā vāudevo bimukta oṃ //
373.d:
सर्वाभरणभूषाढ्यो वितस्तर्वा यथेच्छया /
अहं ब्रह्म ज्योतिरात्मा वाउदेवो बिमुक्त ओं //
373.m: richly adorned with all ornaments, measuring a span or according to wish: / 'I am Brahman, the self of light, Vāsudeva, liberated. Oṃ.'

373.s:
dhyānācchrānto japenmantraṃ japācchrāntaś ca cintayet /
japadhyānādiyuktasya viṣṇuḥ śīghraṃ prasīdati //
373.d:
ध्यानाच्छ्रान्तो जपेन्मन्त्रं जपाच्छ्रान्तश् च चिन्तयेत् /
जपध्यानादियुक्तस्य विष्णुः शीघ्रं प्रसीदति //
373.m: Tired of meditation, one should recite the mantra; tired of recitation, one should contemplate. / Viṣṇu quickly becomes pleased with one engaged in recitation, meditation, and the like.

373.s:
japayajñasya vai yajñāḥ kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīṃ /
japinaṃ nopasarpanti vyādhayaścādhayo grahāḥ /
bhuktirmurktirmṛtyujayo japena prāpnuyāt phalaṃ(1) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dhyānaṃ nāma trisaptatyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 prāpnuyāddharimiti kha.. / prāpyate phalamiti ña..
:p 323
:ś atha catuḥsaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dhāraṇā
373.d:
जपयज्ञस्य वै यज्ञाः कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीं /
जपिनं नोपसर्पन्ति व्याधयश्चाधयो ग्रहाः /
भुक्तिर्मुर्क्तिर्मृत्युजयो जपेन प्राप्नुयात् फलं(1) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे ध्यानं नाम त्रिसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 प्राप्नुयाद्धरिमिति ख.. / प्राप्यते फलमिति ञ..
:प् 323
:श् अथ चतुःसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
धारणा
373.m:
Sacrifices are not worth a sixteenth part of the sacrifice of recitation. / Diseases, mental anxieties, and malevolent planets do not approach the practitioner of recitation; / through recitation one attains the fruit of worldly enjoyment, liberation, and conquest of death.
Thus ends the three hundred and seventy-third chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named Meditation.
[...]
1. "prāpnuyād dharim" in manuscript Kha. / "prāpyate phalam" in manuscript Ña.
[Page 323]
Now begins the three hundred and seventy-fourth chapter.
Fixation.

374.s:
agnir uvāca
dhāraṇā manasodhyeye saṃsthitirdhyānavaddvidhā /
mūrtāmūrtaharidhyānamanodhāraṇato hariḥ //
374.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
धारणा मनसोध्येये संस्थितिर्ध्यानवद्द्विधा /
मूर्तामूर्तहरिध्यानमनोधारणतो हरिः //
374.m: Agni said: / Fixation is the mind's steady abiding in the object of meditation; like meditation, it is twofold. / Hari [is attained] through meditation and mental fixation on Hari with form and without form.

374.s:
yadvāhyāvasthitaṃ lakṣayaṃ tasmānna calate manaḥ /
tāvat kālaṃ pradeśeṣu dhāraṇā manasi sthitiḥ //
374.d:
यद्वाह्यावस्थितं लक्षयं तस्मान्न चलते मनः /
तावत् कालं प्रदेशेषु धारणा मनसि स्थितिः //
374.m: When the mind does not waver from that object which is situated outside / for so long a time in [those] locations, that steadfastness in the mind is fixation.

374.s:
kālāvadhi paricchinnaṃ dehe saṃsthāpitaṃ manaḥ /
na pracyavati yallakṣyāddhāraṇā sābhidhīyate //
374.d:
कालावधि परिच्छिन्नं देहे संस्थापितं मनः /
न प्रच्यवति यल्लक्ष्याद्धारणा साभिधीयते //
374.m: When the mind, bounded by a duration of time, is established in the body / and does not deviate from the focus, that is called fixation.

374.s:
dhāraṇā dvādaśāyāmā dhyānaṃ dvadaśadhāraṇāḥ /
dhyānaṃ dvādaśakaṃ yāvatsamādhirabhidhīyate //
374.d:
धारणा द्वादशायामा ध्यानं द्वदशधारणाः /
ध्यानं द्वादशकं यावत्समाधिरभिधीयते //
374.m: Fixation lasts twelve breath-extensions; meditation is twelve fixations; / as long as twelve meditations [endures], it is called samādhi.

374.s:
dhāraṇābhyāsayuktātmā yadi prāṇair vimucyate /
kulaikaviṃśamuttārya svaryāti paramaṃ padaṃ(1) //
374.d:
धारणाभ्यासयुक्तात्मा यदि प्राणैर् विमुच्यते /
कुलैकविंशमुत्तार्य स्वर्याति परमं पदं(1) //
374.m: If a practitioner whose self is united with the practice of fixation is released from the vital breaths, / having delivered twenty-one generations of his lineage, he goes to heaven, to the supreme state.

374.s:
yasmin yasmin bhavedaṅge yogināṃ vyādhisambhavaḥ /
tattadaṅgaṃ dhiyā vyāpya dhārayettattvadhāraṇaṃ //
374.d:
यस्मिन् यस्मिन् भवेदङ्गे योगिनां व्याधिसम्भवः /
तत्तदङ्गं धिया व्याप्य धारयेत्तत्त्वधारणं //
374.m: In whichever limb of the yogis the arising of disease may occur, / pervading that limb with intellect, one should hold the fixation of the principles.

374.s:
āgneyī vāruṇī caiva aiśānī cāmṛtātmikā /
sāgniḥ śikhā phaḍantā ca viṣṇoḥ kāryā dvijottama //
374.d:
आग्नेयी वारुणी चैव ऐशानी चामृतात्मिका /
साग्निः शिखा फडन्ता च विष्णोः कार्या द्विजोत्तम //
374.m: Fiery, watery, belonging to Īśāna, and consisting of nectar: / [the flame] possessing fire and ending with 'phaṭ' should be performed for Viṣṇu, O best of the twice-born.

374.s:
nāḍībhirvikaṭaṃ divyaṃ śūlāgraṃ vedhayecchubham /
pādāṅguṣṭhāt kapālāntaṃ raśmimaṇḍalamāvṛtaṃ //
:n
1 svayaṃ yāti paraṃ padamiti kha..
:p 324
374.d:
नाडीभिर्विकटं दिव्यं शूलाग्रं वेधयेच्छुभम् /
पादाङ्गुष्ठात् कपालान्तं रश्मिमण्डलमावृतं //
:न्
1 स्वयं याति परं पदमिति ख..
:प् 324
374.m:
One should pierce the auspicious trident-point, fierce and divine, through the channels, / surrounded by a sphere of rays extending from the big toe of the foot to the skull.
[...]
1. "svayaṃ yāti paraṃ padam" in manuscript Kha.
[Page 324]

374.s:
tiryakcādhordhvabhāgebhyaḥ prayāntyo 'tīva tejasā(1) /
cintayet sādhakendrastaṃ yāvatsarvaṃ mahāmune //
374.d:
तिर्यक्चाधोर्ध्वभागेभ्यः प्रयान्त्यो ऽतीव तेजसा(1) /
चिन्तयेत् साधकेन्द्रस्तं यावत्सर्वं महामुने //
374.m: [Rays] shooting forth with intense radiance horizontally, downwards, and upwards: / the best of practitioners should contemplate it until everything, O great sage,

374.s:
bhasprībhūtaṃ śarīraṃ svantataś caivīpasaṃharet /
śītaśleṣmādayaḥ pāpaṃ vinaśyanti dvijātayaḥ //
374.d:
भस्प्रीभूतं शरीरं स्वन्ततश् चैवीपसंहरेत् /
शीतश्लेष्मादयः पापं विनश्यन्ति द्विजातयः //
374.m: has turned one's own body to ashes, and then one should withdraw it. / Cold, phlegm, and the like, along with sin, are destroyed, O twice-born.

374.s:
śiro dhīrañca(2) kārañca kaṇṭhaṃ cādhomukhe smaret /
dhyāyedacchinnacintātmā bhuyo bhūtena cātmanā //
374.d:
शिरो धीरञ्च(2) कारञ्च कण्ठं चाधोमुखे स्मरेत् /
ध्यायेदच्छिन्नचिन्तात्मा भुयो भूतेन चात्मना //
374.m: One should recall the head as resolute and acting, and the throat turned downwards; / with unsevered contemplation, one should meditate again and again with one's self identical with the elements.

374.s:
sphuracchīkarasaṃsmarśaprabhūte himagāmibhiḥ /
dhārābhirakhilaṃ viśvamāpūrya bhuvi cintayet //
374.d:
स्फुरच्छीकरसंस्मर्शप्रभूते हिमगामिभिः /
धाराभिरखिलं विश्वमापूर्य भुवि चिन्तयेत् //
374.m: Through streams born of the contact of shimmering sprays, moving with snow, / one should contemplate the entire universe filled upon the earth.

374.s:
brahmarandhrācca saṃkṣobhādyāvadādhāramaṇḍalag /
suṣumnāntargato bhūtvā saṃpūrṇendukṛtālayaṃ //
374.d:
ब्रह्मरन्ध्राच्च संक्षोभाद्यावदाधारमण्डलग् /
सुषुम्नान्तर्गतो भूत्वा संपूर्णेन्दुकृतालयं //
374.m: From the agitation at the aperture of Brahmā down to the mūlādhāra-maṇḍala, / having entered the central channel, [which has] become the abode of the full moon,

374.s:
saṃplāvya himasaṃsparśatoyenāmṛtamūrtinā /
kṣutpipāsākramaprāyasantāpaparipīḍitaḥ //
374.d:
संप्लाव्य हिमसंस्पर्शतोयेनामृतमूर्तिना /
क्षुत्पिपासाक्रमप्रायसन्तापपरिपीडितः //
374.m: inundating it with water of snow-like touch, consisting of nectar— / one afflicted by hunger, thirst, weakness, and torment,

374.s:
dhārayedvāruṇīṃ mantro tuṣṭyarthaṃ cāpyatantritaḥ /
vāruṇīdhāraṇā proktā aiśānīdhāraṇāṃ śṛṇu //
374.d:
धारयेद्वारुणीं मन्त्रो तुष्ट्यर्थं चाप्यतन्त्रितः /
वारुणीधारणा प्रोक्ता ऐशानीधारणां शृणु //
374.m: unwearied, should maintain the watery [fixation] for the sake of satisfaction with the mantra. / The watery fixation has been declared; hear the fixation belonging to Īśāna.

374.s:
vyomni brahmamaye padme prāṇāpāṇe kṣayaṅgate /
prasādaṃ cintayed viṣṇoryāvaccintā kṣayaṃ gatā //
374.d:
व्योम्नि ब्रह्ममये पद्मे प्राणापाणे क्षयङ्गते /
प्रसादं चिन्तयेद् विष्णोर्यावच्चिन्ता क्षयं गता //
374.m: When the ascending and descending breaths have dissolved in the sky, in the lotus consisting of Brahman, / one should contemplate the grace of Viṣṇu until thought has reached its end.

374.s:
mahābhāvañjapet sarvaṃ tato vyāpaka īśvaraḥ /
ardhenduṃ paramaṃ śāntaṃ nirābhāsannirañjanaṃ //
374.d:
महाभावञ्जपेत् सर्वं ततो व्यापक ईश्वरः /
अर्धेन्दुं परमं शान्तं निराभासन्निरञ्जनं //
374.m: One should recite all of the Great State; then the all-pervading Īśvara, / the crescent moon, supremely tranquil, free from appearances, spotless.

374.s:
asatyaṃ satyamābhāti tāvatsarvaṃ carācaraṃ /
yāvat svasyandarūpantu na dṛṣṭaṃ guruvaktrataḥ //
374.d:
असत्यं सत्यमाभाति तावत्सर्वं चराचरं /
यावत् स्वस्यन्दरूपन्तु न दृष्टं गुरुवक्त्रतः //
374.m: All that moves and is motionless appears real though unreal, / so long as one's own radiant nature is not seen from the mouth of the guru.

374.s:
dṛṣṭhe tasmin pare tattve ābrahma sacarācaraṃ /
:n
1 pāṭho 'yamādarśadoṣeṇa duṣṭaḥ
2 vīraśceti ña..
:p 325
pramātṛmānameyañca dhyānahṛtpadmakalpanaṃ //
374.d:
दृष्ठे तस्मिन् परे तत्त्वे आब्रह्म सचराचरं /
:न्
1 पाठो ऽयमादर्शदोषेण दुष्टः
2 वीरश्चेति ञ..
:प् 325
प्रमातृमानमेयञ्च ध्यानहृत्पद्मकल्पनं //
374.m:
When that supreme reality is seen, everything from Brahmā downward, moving and unmoving,
[...]
1. This reading is corrupt due to an error in the exemplar.
2. "vīraś ca" in manuscript Ña.
[Page 325]
the knower, the means of knowing, and the knowable, and the conceptualization of the heart-lotus in meditation,

374.s:
mātṛmodakavatsarvaṃ japahomārcanādikaṃ /
viṣṇumantreṇa vā kuryādamṛtāṃ dhāraṇāṃ vade //
374.d:
मातृमोदकवत्सर्वं जपहोमार्चनादिकं /
विष्णुमन्त्रेण वा कुर्यादमृतां धारणां वदे //
374.m: all recitation, fire oblations, worship, and the like, are like sweetmeats made by a mother. / Or one should perform it with the mantra of Viṣṇu; I will declare the nectar-like fixation.

374.s:
saṃpūrṇendunibhaṃ dhyāyet kamalaṃ tantrimuṣṭigam /
śiraḥsthaṃ cintayed yatnācchaśāṅkāyutavarcasaṃ //
374.d:
संपूर्णेन्दुनिभं ध्यायेत् कमलं तन्त्रिमुष्टिगम् /
शिरःस्थं चिन्तयेद् यत्नाच्छशाङ्कायुतवर्चसं //
374.m: One should meditate on the lotus resembling the full moon, situated within the fist of channels; / one should attentively contemplate [it] residing in the head, having the splendour of ten thousand moons,

374.s:
sampūrṇamaṇḍalaṃ vyomni śivakallolapūrṇitaṃ /
tathā hṛtkamale dhyāyettanmadhye svatanuṃ smaret /
sādhako vigatakleśo jāyate dhāraṇādihiḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dhāraṇā nāma
catuḥsaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcasaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
samādhiḥ
374.d:
सम्पूर्णमण्डलं व्योम्नि शिवकल्लोलपूर्णितं /
तथा हृत्कमले ध्यायेत्तन्मध्ये स्वतनुं स्मरेत् /
साधको विगतक्लेशो जायते धारणादिहिः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे धारणा नाम
चतुःसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
समाधिः
374.m:
a complete maṇḍala in the sky, filled with waves of auspiciousness. / Likewise, one should meditate in the heart-lotus, and recall one's own body in its middle; / by means of fixation and the rest, the practitioner becomes freed from affliction.
Thus ends the three hundred and seventy-fourth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named Fixation.
Now begins the three hundred and seventy-fifth chapter.
Samādhi.

375.s:
agnir uvāca
yadātmamātraṃ nirbhāsaṃ stimitodadhivat sthitaṃ /
caitanyarūpavaddhyānaṃ tat samādhirihocyate //
375.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
यदात्ममात्रं निर्भासं स्तिमितोदधिवत् स्थितं /
चैतन्यरूपवद्ध्यानं तत् समाधिरिहोच्यते //
375.m: Agni said: / Meditation when shining as the Self alone, motionless like a calmed ocean, / having the nature of pure consciousness, is here called samādhi.

375.s:
dhyāyanmanaḥ sanniveśya yastiṣṭhedacalasthiraḥ /
nirvātānalavadyogī samādhisthaḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
375.d:
ध्यायन्मनः सन्निवेश्य यस्तिष्ठेदचलस्थिरः /
निर्वातानलवद्योगी समाधिस्थः प्रकीर्तितः //
375.m: The yogi who stands motionless and steady, having fixed the mind while meditating, / like a fire in a windless place, is declared to be established in samādhi.

375.s:
na śṛṇoti na cāghrāti na paśyati na vamyati /
na ca sparśaṃ vijānāti na saṅkalpayate manaḥ //
375.d:
न शृणोति न चाघ्राति न पश्यति न वम्यति /
न च स्पर्शं विजानाति न सङ्कल्पयते मनः //
375.m: He does not hear, nor smell, nor see, nor speak; / he does not perceive touch, nor does the mind form volitions;

375.s:
na cābhimanyate kiñcinna ca budhyati kāṣṭhavat /
evamīśvarasaṃlīnaḥ samādhisthaḥ sa gīyate //
:p 326
375.d:
न चाभिमन्यते किञ्चिन्न च बुध्यति काष्ठवत् /
एवमीश्वरसंलीनः समाधिस्थः स गीयते //
:प् 326
375.m:
he does not conceive any egoism, nor is he conscious, like a piece of wood. / Thus merged in the Lord, he is said to be established in samādhi.
[Page 326]

375.s:
yathā dīpo nivātasyo neṅgate sopamā smṛtā /
dhyāyato viṣṇumātmānaṃ samādhistasya yoginaḥ //
375.d:
यथा दीपो निवातस्यो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता /
ध्यायतो विष्णुमात्मानं समाधिस्तस्य योगिनः //
375.m: Just as a lamp standing in a windless place does not flicker—that comparison is traditionally remembered / for the yogi established in samādhi, meditating on Viṣṇu as the Self.

375.s:
upasargāḥ pravartante divyāḥ siddhiprasūcakāḥ /
pātitaḥ śrāvaṇo dhāturdaśanasvāṅgavedanāḥ //
375.d:
उपसर्गाः प्रवर्तन्ते दिव्याः सिद्धिप्रसूचकाः /
पातितः श्रावणो धातुर्दशनस्वाङ्गवेदनाः //
375.m: Divine obstacles arise that indicate the [approach of] supernatural powers: / fallen condition, celestial hearing, elements, vision, and pains in one's own limbs.

375.s:
prārthayanti ca taṃ devā bhogair divyaiś ca yoginaṃ /
nṛpāś ca pṛthivīdānair dhanaiś ca sudhanādhipāḥ //
375.d:
प्रार्थयन्ति च तं देवा भोगैर् दिव्यैश् च योगिनं /
नृपाश् च पृथिवीदानैर् धनैश् च सुधनाधिपाः //
375.m: And the gods entreat that yogi with divine pleasures, / and kings with gifts of land, and lords of great wealth with treasures.

375.s:
vedādisarvaśāstrañca svayameva pravartate /
abhīṣṭachandoviṣayaṃ kāvyañcāsya pravartate //
375.d:
वेदादिसर्वशास्त्रञ्च स्वयमेव प्रवर्तते /
अभीष्टछन्दोविषयं काव्यञ्चास्य प्रवर्तते //
375.m: All sacred scriptures beginning with the Vedas reveal themselves spontaneously; / poetry concerning desired metres also proceeds from him.

375.s:
rasāyanāni divyāni divyāś cauṣadhayas tathā /
samastāni ca śilpāni kalāḥ sarvāś ca vindati //
375.d:
रसायनानि दिव्यानि दिव्याश् चौषधयस् तथा /
समस्तानि च शिल्पानि कलाः सर्वाश् च विन्दति //
375.m: He obtains divine elixirs and divine medicinal herbs, / all the crafts, and all the arts.

375.s:
surendrakanyā ity ādyā guṇāś ca pratibhādayaḥ /
tṛṇavattāntyajed yastu tasya viṣṇuḥ prasīdati //
375.d:
सुरेन्द्रकन्या इत्य् आद्या गुणाश् च प्रतिभादयः /
तृणवत्तान्त्यजेद् यस्तु तस्य विष्णुः प्रसीदति //
375.m: Daughters of Indra and the like, and qualities beginning with intuitive brilliance: / whoever casts them aside like a piece of straw, with him Viṣṇu is pleased.

375.s:
aṇimādiguṇaiśvaryaḥ śiṣye jñānaṃ prakāśya ca /
bhuktvā bhogān yathecchātastanuntyaktvālayāttataḥ //
375.d:
अणिमादिगुणैश्वर्यः शिष्ये ज्ञानं प्रकाश्य च /
भुक्त्वा भोगान् यथेच्छातस्तनुन्त्यक्त्वालयात्ततः //
375.m: Possessing sovereignty with qualities like atomicity, having revealed knowledge to his disciple, / having enjoyed pleasures at will, and then having abandoned the body from its abode,

375.s:
tiṣṭhet svātmani vijñāna ānande brahmaṇīśvare/
malino hi yathādarśa ātmajñānāya na kṣamaḥ //
375.d:
तिष्ठेत् स्वात्मनि विज्ञान आनन्दे ब्रह्मणीश्वरे/
मलिनो हि यथादर्श आत्मज्ञानाय न क्षमः //
375.m: he would remain in his own self, in consciousness, in bliss, in Brahman, the Lord. / For just as a soiled mirror is incapable of [reflecting] self-knowledge,

375.s:
sarvāśrayannije dehe dehī vindati vedanāṃ /
yogayuktastu sarveṣāṃ yogānnāpnoti vedanāṃ //
375.d:
सर्वाश्रयन्निजे देहे देही विन्दति वेदनां /
योगयुक्तस्तु सर्वेषां योगान्नाप्नोति वेदनां //
375.m: The embodied soul experiences sensation in its own body, which is the receptacle of all. / But one endowed with yoga does not experience the pain of all on account of yoga.

375.s:
ākāśamekaṃ hi yathā ghaṭādiṣu pṛthag bhavet /
tathātmaiko hy anekeṣu jalādhāreṣvivāṃśumān //
375.d:
आकाशमेकं हि यथा घटादिषु पृथग् भवेत् /
तथात्मैको ह्य् अनेकेषु जलाधारेष्विवांशुमान् //
375.m: Just as space, though one, becomes distinct in pots and the like, / so the single Self is [present] in many [bodies], like the sun in vessels of water.

375.s:
brahmakhānilatejāṃsi jalabhūkṣitidhātavaḥ /
ime lokā eṣa cātmā tasmācca sacarācaraṃ //
:p 327
375.d:
ब्रह्मखानिलतेजांसि जलभूक्षितिधातवः /
इमे लोका एष चात्मा तस्माच्च सचराचरं //
:प् 327
375.m:
Brahman, space, wind, fire, water, and the elements of the earth— / these worlds, and this Self; and from that [proceeds] all that moves and is still.
[Page 327]

375.s:
gṛddaṇdacakrasaṃyogāt kumbhakāro yathā ghaṭaṃ /
karoti tṛṇamṛtkāṣṭhair gṛhaṃ vā gṛhakārakaḥ //
375.d:
गृद्दण्दचक्रसंयोगात् कुम्भकारो यथा घटं /
करोति तृणमृत्काष्ठैर् गृहं वा गृहकारकः //
375.m: Just as a potter makes a pot by the union of clay, stick, and wheel, / or a builder builds a house with grass, mud, and timber,

375.s:
karaṇānyevamādāya tāsu tāsviha yoniṣu /
mṛjatyātmānamātmaivaṃ sambhūya karaṇāni ca //
375.d:
करणान्येवमादाय तासु तास्विह योनिषु /
मृजत्यात्मानमात्मैवं सम्भूय करणानि च //
375.m: so taking the organs and combining with the organs in these various wombs here, / the Self creates itself in this way.

375.s:
karmaṇā doṣamohābhyāmicchayaiva sa badhyate /
jñānādvimucyate jīvo dharmād yogī na rogabhāk //
375.d:
कर्मणा दोषमोहाभ्यामिच्छयैव स बध्यते /
ज्ञानाद्विमुच्यते जीवो धर्माद् योगी न रोगभाक् //
375.m: It is bound by action, by defect and delusion, and by desire alone; / through knowledge the individual soul is liberated, through dharma a yogin is free from affliction.

375.s:
vartyādhārasnehayogād yathā dīpasya saṃsthitiḥ /
vikriyāpi ca dṛṣṭvaivamakāle prāṇasaṃkṣayaḥ //
375.d:
वर्त्याधारस्नेहयोगाद् यथा दीपस्य संस्थितिः /
विक्रियापि च दृष्ट्वैवमकाले प्राणसंक्षयः //
375.m: Just as a lamp endures by the combination of wick, container, and oil, / yet an alteration [leads to its going out], so too is the premature destruction of life seen.

375.s:
anantā raśmayastasya dīpavad yaḥ sthito hṛdi /
sitāsitāḥ kadrunīlāḥ kapilāḥ pītalohitāḥ //
375.d:
अनन्ता रश्मयस्तस्य दीपवद् यः स्थितो हृदि /
सितासिताः कद्रुनीलाः कपिलाः पीतलोहिताः //
375.m: Endless are the rays of that which is situated like a lamp in the heart: / white and black, brown, blue, tawny, yellow, and red.

375.s:
ūrdhvamekaḥ sthitasteṣāṃ yo bhittvā sūryamaṇḍalaṃ /
brahmalokamatikramya tena yāti parāṅgatiṃ //
375.d:
ऊर्ध्वमेकः स्थितस्तेषां यो भित्त्वा सूर्यमण्डलं /
ब्रह्मलोकमतिक्रम्य तेन याति पराङ्गतिं //
375.m: One of them is situated upward, which, having pierced the disc of the sun / and passed beyond the world of Brahmā, goes by that to the supreme state.

375.s:
yadasyānyadraśmiśatamūrdhvameva vyavasthitaṃ /
tena devanikāyāni dhāmāni pratipadyate //
375.d:
यदस्यान्यद्रश्मिशतमूर्ध्वमेव व्यवस्थितं /
तेन देवनिकायानि धामानि प्रतिपद्यते //
375.m: The other hundred rays of it that are situated upwards— / by that one attains the realms that are assemblies of the gods.

375.s:
ye naikarūpāścādhastādraśmayo 'sya mṛduprabhāḥ /
iha karmopabhogāya taiś ca sañcarate hi saḥ //
375.d:
ये नैकरूपाश्चाधस्ताद्रश्मयो ऽस्य मृदुप्रभाः /
इह कर्मोपभोगाय तैश् च सञ्चरते हि सः //
375.m: Those multiform rays of it below, which are soft in lustre— / through those it wanders here for the sake of experiencing [the fruit of] action.

375.s:
buddhīndriyāṇi sarvāṇi manaḥ karmendriyāṇi ca /
ahaṅkāraś ca buddhiś ca pṛthivyādīni caiva hi //
375.d:
बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि सर्वाणि मनः कर्मेन्द्रियाणि च /
अहङ्कारश् च बुद्धिश् च पृथिव्यादीनि चैव हि //
375.m: All the senses of cognition, the mind, and the organs of action, / ego and intellect, and earth and the other [elements]—

375.s:
avyakta ātmā kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetrastyāsya nigadyate /
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtasya sannasan sadasacca saḥ //
375.d:
अव्यक्त आत्मा क्षेत्रज्ञः क्षेत्रस्त्यास्य निगद्यते /
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतस्य सन्नसन् सदसच्च सः //
375.m: the unmanifest Self, the knower of the field, is declared to be the master of this field; / it is the ruler of every being, being and non-being, and both being and non-being.

375.s:
buddherutpattiravyaktā tato 'haṅkārasambhavaḥ /
tasmāt khādīni jāyante ekottaraguṇāni tu //
:p 328
375.d:
बुद्धेरुत्पत्तिरव्यक्ता ततो ऽहङ्कारसम्भवः /
तस्मात् खादीनि जायन्ते एकोत्तरगुणानि तु //
:प् 328
375.m:
The arising of the intellect is from the unmanifest; from that arises ego; / from that are born space and the other [elements], possessing qualities that increase by one.
[Page 328]

375.s:
śabdaḥ sparśaś ca rūpañca raso gandhaś ca tadguṇāḥ /
yo yasminnāśritaś caiṣāṃ sa tasminneva līyate //
375.d:
शब्दः स्पर्शश् च रूपञ्च रसो गन्धश् च तद्गुणाः /
यो यस्मिन्नाश्रितश् चैषां स तस्मिन्नेव लीयते //
375.m: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are their qualities; / whichever [element] rests in whichever [quality], it dissolves back into that very one.

375.s:
sattvaṃ rajastamaś caiva guṇāstasyaiva kīrtitāḥ /
rajastamobhyāmāviṣṭaś cakravadbhrābhyate hi saḥ //
375.d:
सत्त्वं रजस्तमश् चैव गुणास्तस्यैव कीर्तिताः /
रजस्तमोभ्यामाविष्टश् चक्रवद्भ्राभ्यते हि सः //
375.m: Sattva, rajas, and tamas are declared to be its qualities; / seized by rajas and tamas, it is spun around like a wheel.

375.s:
anādirādimān yaś ca sa eva puruṣaḥ paraḥ /
liṅgendriyair upagrāhyāḥ sa vikāra udāhṛtaḥ //
375.d:
अनादिरादिमान् यश् च स एव पुरुषः परः /
लिङ्गेन्द्रियैर् उपग्राह्याः स विकार उदाहृतः //
375.m: He who is without beginning and has a beginning, he alone is the supreme Puruṣa; / what can be grasped by the indicative senses is declared to be change.

375.s:
yato devāḥ purāṇāni vidyopaniṣadas tathā /
ślokāḥ sūtrāṇi bhāṣyāṇi yaccānyadmāṅbhayaṃ bhavet //
375.d:
यतो देवाः पुराणानि विद्योपनिषदस् तथा /
श्लोकाः सूत्राणि भाष्याणि यच्चान्यद्माङ्भयं भवेत् //
375.m: From which [proceed] the gods, the Purāṇas, knowledge, and the Upaniṣads, / verses, aphorisms, commentaries, and whatever other speech there may be.

375.s:
pitṛyānopavīthyāś ca yadagastyasya cāntaraṃ /
tenāgnihotriṇo yānti prajākāmā divaṃ prati //
375.d:
पितृयानोपवीथ्याश् च यदगस्त्यस्य चान्तरं /
तेनाग्निहोत्रिणो यान्ति प्रजाकामा दिवं प्रति //
375.m: The space between the lane of the Path of the Ancestors and the Agastya constellation— / along that, the maintainers of the sacred fire, desirous of offspring, travel towards heaven.

375.s:
ye ca dānaparāḥ samyagaṣṭābhiś ca guṇair yutāḥ /
aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi munayo gṛhamedhinaḥ //
375.d:
ये च दानपराः सम्यगष्टाभिश् च गुणैर् युताः /
अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि मुनयो गृहमेधिनः //
375.m: And eighty-eight thousand householder sages / who are dedicated to gifting and properly endowed with the eight virtues,

375.s:
punarāvartane vījabhūtā dharmapravartakāḥ /
saptarṣināgvīthyāś ca devalokaṃ samāśritāḥ //
375.d:
पुनरावर्तने वीजभूता धर्मप्रवर्तकाः /
सप्तर्षिनाग्वीथ्याश् च देवलोकं समाश्रिताः //
375.m: becoming the seeds for return, promoters of dharma, / have resorted to the world of the gods by the serpent lane of the Seven Sages.

375.s:
tāvanta eva munayaḥ sarvārambhavivarjitāḥ /
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa saṅgatyāgena medhayā //
375.d:
तावन्त एव मुनयः सर्वारम्भविवर्जिताः /
तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण सङ्गत्यागेन मेधया //
375.m: Just as many sages, free from all undertakings, / through ascetic austerity, celibacy, renunciation of company, and intellect,

375.s:
yatra yatrāvatiṣṭhante yāvadāhūtasaṃplavaṃ /
vedānuvacanaṃ yajñā brahmacaryaṃ tapo damaḥ //
375.d:
यत्र यत्रावतिष्ठन्ते यावदाहूतसंप्लवं /
वेदानुवचनं यज्ञा ब्रह्मचर्यं तपो दमः //
375.m: remain wherever they are until the dissolution of the summoned. / Vedic recitation, sacrifices, celibacy, ascetic austerity, self-restraint,

375.s:
śraddhopavāsaḥ satyatvamātmano jñānahetavaḥ /
sa tvāśramair nididhyāsyaḥ samastair evameva tu //
375.d:
श्रद्धोपवासः सत्यत्वमात्मनो ज्ञानहेतवः /
स त्वाश्रमैर् निदिध्यास्यः समस्तैर् एवमेव तु //
375.m: faith, fasting, and truthfulness are the causes of knowledge of the Self; / but that [Self] is to be meditated upon in this very manner by all the stages of life.

375.s:
draṣṭavyastvatha mantavyaḥ śrotavyaś ca dvijātibhiḥ /
ya evamenaṃ vindanti ye cāraṇyakamāśritāḥ //
375.d:
द्रष्टव्यस्त्वथ मन्तव्यः श्रोतव्यश् च द्विजातिभिः /
य एवमेनं विन्दन्ति ये चारण्यकमाश्रिताः //
375.m: It is to be seen, pondered, and heard by the twice-born. / Those who know this in this manner, and those who have taken to forest life,

375.s:
upāsate dvijāḥ satyaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ /
:p 329
kramātte sambhavantyarcirahaḥ śuklaṃ tathottaraṃ //
375.d:
उपासते द्विजाः सत्यं श्रद्धया परया युताः /
:प् 329
क्रमात्ते सम्भवन्त्यर्चिरहः शुक्लं तथोत्तरं //
375.m:
the twice-born worship the truth endowed with supreme faith.
[Page 329]
In succession, they attain the flame, the day, the bright [fortnight], and the northern

375.s:
ayanandevalokañca savitāraṃ savidyutaṃ /
tatastān puruṣo 'bhyetya mānaso brahmalaukikān //
375.d:
अयनन्देवलोकञ्च सवितारं सविद्युतं /
ततस्तान् पुरुषो ऽभ्येत्य मानसो ब्रह्मलौकिकान् //
375.m: solstice, the world of the gods, the sun, and the realm of lightning; / then a mental person, approaching them, makes them

375.s:
karoti punarāvṛttisteṣāmiha na vidyate /
yajñena tapasā dānair ye hi svargajito janāḥ //
375.d:
करोति पुनरावृत्तिस्तेषामिह न विद्यते /
यज्ञेन तपसा दानैर् ये हि स्वर्गजितो जनाः //
375.m: dwellers in the world of Brahmā; for them there is no return here. / But the people who have conquered heaven by sacrifice, ascetic austerity, and gifts

375.s:
dhūmaṃ niśāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣaṃ dakṣiṇāyanameva ca /
pitṛlokaṃ candramasaṃ nabho vāyuṃ jalaṃ mahīṃ //
375.d:
धूमं निशां कृष्णपक्षं दक्षिणायनमेव च /
पितृलोकं चन्द्रमसं नभो वायुं जलं महीं //
375.m: [reach] smoke, the night, the dark fortnight, the southern solstice, / the realm of the ancestors, the moon, the sky, the wind, the water, and the earth;

375.s:
kramātte sambhavantīha punareva vrajanti ca /
etadyo na vijānāti mārgadvitayamātmanaḥ //
375.d:
क्रमात्ते सम्भवन्तीह पुनरेव व्रजन्ति च /
एतद्यो न विजानाति मार्गद्वितयमात्मनः //
375.m: in succession they arise here and depart again. / He who does not know this pair of paths for the soul

375.s:
dandaśūkaḥ pataṅgo vā bhavedkīṭo 'thavā kṛmiḥ /
hṛdaye dīpavadbrahma dhyānājjivo mṛto bhavet //
375.d:
दन्दशूकः पतङ्गो वा भवेद्कीटो ऽथवा कृमिः /
हृदये दीपवद्ब्रह्म ध्यानाज्जिवो मृतो भवेत् //
375.m: becomes a serpent, a moth, or an insect or worm. / Through meditation on Brahman like a lamp in the heart, the individual soul becomes as dead [to the world].

375.s:
nyāyāgatadhanastattvajñānaniṣṭho 'tithipriyaḥ /
śrāddhakṛtsatyavādī ca gṛhastho 'pi vimucyate //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe samādhirnāma pañcasaptatyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ
:p 330
:ś atha ṣaṭsaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
brahmajñānaṃ
375.d:
न्यायागतधनस्तत्त्वज्ञाननिष्ठो ऽतिथिप्रियः /
श्राद्धकृत्सत्यवादी च गृहस्थो ऽपि विमुच्यते //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे समाधिर्नाम पञ्चसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः
:प् 330
:श् अथ षट्सप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
ब्रह्मज्ञानं
375.m:
Whose wealth is lawfully acquired, who is established in knowledge of truth, fond of guests, / a performer of ancestral rites, and truthful in speech—even a householder is liberated.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the three hundred and seventy-fifth chapter, named Samādhi.
[Page 330]
Now the three hundred and seventy-sixth chapter.
The Knowledge of Brahman

376.s:
agnir uvāca
brahmajñānaṃ pravakṣyāmi saṃsārājñānamuktaye /
ayamātmā parṃ brahma ahamasmīti mucyate //
376.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ब्रह्मज्ञानं प्रवक्ष्यामि संसाराज्ञानमुक्तये /
अयमात्मा पर्ं ब्रह्म अहमस्मीति मुच्यते //
376.m:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim the knowledge of Brahman for the sake of release from the ignorance of worldly existence: / 'This Self is the supreme Brahman; I am [He]'—having known this, one is liberated.

376.s:
deha ātmā na bhavati dṛsyatvācca ghaṭādivat /
prasapte maraṇe dehādātmānyo jñāyate dhruvaṃ //
376.d:
देह आत्मा न भवति दृस्यत्वाच्च घटादिवत् /
प्रसप्ते मरणे देहादात्मान्यो ज्ञायते ध्रुवं //
376.m: The body is not the Self, because it is visible, like a pot and the like. / In deep sleep and in death, the Self is surely known to be distinct from the body.

376.s:
dehaḥ sa cedavyavaharedvikāryādisannibhaḥ /
cakṣurādīnīndriyāṇi nātmā vai karaṇaṃ tvataḥ //
376.d:
देहः स चेदव्यवहरेद्विकार्यादिसन्निभः /
चक्षुरादीनीन्द्रियाणि नात्मा वै करणं त्वतः //
376.m: If that body acted, it would be similar to an object undergoing change and the like. / The senses such as the eye are not the Self; on the contrary, they are instruments.

376.s:
mano dhīrapi ātmā na dīpavat karaṇaṃ tvataḥ /
prāṇo 'pyātmā na bhavati suṣupte citprabhāvataḥ //
376.d:
मनो धीरपि आत्मा न दीपवत् करणं त्वतः /
प्राणो ऽप्यात्मा न भवति सुषुप्ते चित्प्रभावतः //
376.m:
The mind and intellect are also not the Self, for, like a lamp, they are instruments.
The vital breath also is not the Self, because of the power of consciousness in deep sleep.

376.s:
jāgratsvapne ca caitanyaṃ saṅkīrṇatvānna budhyate /
vijñānarahitaḥ prāṇaḥ suṣupte jñāyate yataḥ //
376.d:
जाग्रत्स्वप्ने च चैतन्यं सङ्कीर्णत्वान्न बुध्यते /
विज्ञानरहितः प्राणः सुषुप्ते ज्ञायते यतः //
376.m:
And in waking and dream, consciousness is not perceived owing to commingling,
since in deep sleep the vital breath is known to be devoid of cognition.

376.s:
ato nātmendriyaṃ tasmādintriyādikamātmanaḥ /
ahaṅkāro 'pi naivātmā dehavadvyabhicārataḥ //
376.d:
अतो नात्मेन्द्रियं तस्मादिन्त्रियादिकमात्मनः /
अहङ्कारो ऽपि नैवात्मा देहवद्व्यभिचारतः //
376.m:
Therefore the Self is not a sense organ; hence the sense organs and the like belong to the Self.
Ego is also not the Self at all, because of its variability, just like the body.

376.s:
uktebhyo vyatirikto 'yamātmā sarvahṛdi sthitaḥ /
sarvadraṣṭā ca bhoktā ca naktamujjvaladīpavat //
376.d:
उक्तेभ्यो व्यतिरिक्तो ऽयमात्मा सर्वहृदि स्थितः /
सर्वद्रष्टा च भोक्ता च नक्तमुज्ज्वलदीपवत् //
376.m:
Distinct from these mentioned [principles], this Self is situated in the heart of all,
the seer of all and the experiencer [of all], like a blazing lamp at night.

376.s:
samādhyārambhakāle ca evaṃ sañcintayenmuniḥ /
yato brahmaṇa ākāśaṃ khādvāyurvāyuto 'nalaḥ //
376.d:
समाध्यारम्भकाले च एवं सञ्चिन्तयेन्मुनिः /
यतो ब्रह्मण आकाशं खाद्वायुर्वायुतो ऽनलः //
376.m:
And at the time of beginning absorption, the sage should contemplate thus:
that from Brahman [came] space; from space, wind; from wind, fire;

376.s:
agnerāpo jalātpṛthvī tataḥ sūkṣmaṃ śarīrakaṃ /
apañcīkṛtabhūtebhya āsan pañcīkṛtānyataḥ //
:p 331
376.d:
अग्नेरापो जलात्पृथ्वी ततः सूक्ष्मं शरीरकं /
अपञ्चीकृतभूतेभ्य आसन् पञ्चीकृतान्यतः //
:प् 331

376.s:
sthūlaṃ śarīraṃ dhyātvāsmāllayaṃ brahmaṇi cintayet /
pañcīkṛtāni bhūtāni tatkāryañca virāṭsmṛtam //
376.d:
स्थूलं शरीरं ध्यात्वास्माल्लयं ब्रह्मणि चिन्तयेत् /
पञ्चीकृतानि भूतानि तत्कार्यञ्च विराट्स्मृतम् //
376.m:
having meditated on the gross body, one should contemplate its dissolution into Brahman from this.
The compounded elements and their effect are known as Virāj.

376.s:
etat sthūlaṃ śarīraṃ hi ātmano jñānakalpitaṃ /
indriyair atha vijñānaṃ dhīrā jāgaritaṃ viduḥ //
376.d:
एतत् स्थूलं शरीरं हि आत्मनो ज्ञानकल्पितं /
इन्द्रियैर् अथ विज्ञानं धीरा जागरितं विदुः //
376.m:
This gross body indeed is conceptualized through knowledge of the Self.
The wise know waking as cognition through the sense organs.

376.s:
viśvastadabhimānī syāt trayametadakārakaṃ /
apañcīkṛtabhūtāni tatkāryaṃ liṅgamucyate //
376.d:
विश्वस्तदभिमानी स्यात् त्रयमेतदकारकं /
अपञ्चीकृतभूतानि तत्कार्यं लिङ्गमुच्यते //
376.m:
Viśva is its identifier; this triad is the letter ‘A’.
The uncompounded elements and their effect are called the subtle body.

376.s:
