saṃyuktaṃ saptadaśabhirhiraṇyagarbhasaṃjñitaṃ /
śarīramātmanaḥ sūkṣmaṃ liṅgamityabhidhīyate //
376.d:
संयुक्तं सप्तदशभिर्हिरण्यगर्भसंज्ञितं /
शरीरमात्मनः सूक्ष्मं लिङ्गमित्यभिधीयते //
376.m:
Endowed with the seventeen [components], termed Hiraṇyagarbha,
the subtle body of the Self is called the subtle body.

376.s:
jāgratsaṃskārajaḥ svapnaḥ pratyayo viṣayātmakaḥ /
ātmā tadupamānī styāttaijaso hy aprapañcataḥ //
376.d:
जाग्रत्संस्कारजः स्वप्नः प्रत्ययो विषयात्मकः /
आत्मा तदुपमानी स्त्यात्तैजसो ह्य् अप्रपञ्चतः //
376.m:
Dream is an awareness consisting of objects, born of waking impressions.
The Self that identifies with it is Taijasa, free from the gross world.

376.s:
sthūlasūkṣmaśarīrākhyadvayasyaikaṃ hi kāraṇaṃ /
ātmā jñānañca sābhāsaṃ tadadhyāhṛtamucyate //
376.d:
स्थूलसूक्ष्मशरीराख्यद्वयस्यैकं हि कारणं /
आत्मा ज्ञानञ्च साभासं तदध्याहृतमुच्यते //
376.m:
For the pair named the gross and subtle bodies, there is indeed one cause.
The Self and consciousness with its reflection are said to be superadded to that.

376.s:
na sannāsanna sadasadetatsāvayavaṃ na tat /
nirgatāvayavaṃ neti nābhinnaṃ bhinnameva ca //
376.d:
न सन्नासन्न सदसदेतत्सावयवं न तत् /
निर्गतावयवं नेति नाभिन्नं भिन्नमेव च //
376.m:
It is neither existent nor non-existent nor both existent and non-existent; it is not with parts,
nor without parts; it is not undifferentiated, nor is it differentiated;

376.s:
bhinnābhinnaṃ hy anirvācyaṃ bandhasaṃsārakārakaṃ /
ekaṃ sa brahma vijñānāt prāptaṃ naiva ca karmabhiḥ //
376.d:
भिन्नाभिन्नं ह्य् अनिर्वाच्यं बन्धसंसारकारकं /
एकं स ब्रह्म विज्ञानात् प्राप्तं नैव च कर्मभिः //
376.m:
it is indeed differentiated-and-undifferentiated, inexpressible, the cause of worldly bondage.
That Brahman is one, attained through knowledge and not at all through actions.

376.s:
sarvātmanā hīndriyāṇāṃ saṃhāraḥ kāraṇātmanāṃ /
buddheḥ sthānaṃ suṣuptaṃ syāttaddvayasyābhimānavān //
376.d:
सर्वात्मना हीन्द्रियाणां संहारः कारणात्मनां /
बुद्धेः स्थानं सुषुप्तं स्यात्तद्द्वयस्याभिमानवान् //
376.m:
When there is complete dissolution of the sense organs having the nature of the cause,
deep sleep is the locus of the intellect; identifying with both of these

376.s:
prājña ātmā trayañcaitat makāraḥ praṇavaḥ smṛtaḥ /
akāraś ca ukāro 'sau makāro hy ayameva ca //
376.d:
प्राज्ञ आत्मा त्रयञ्चैतत् मकारः प्रणवः स्मृतः /
अकारश् च उकारो ऽसौ मकारो ह्य् अयमेव च //
376.m:
is Prājña, the Self. This triad is remembered as the letter ‘M’, the Praṇava;
and the letter ‘A’ and this letter ‘U’ are indeed just this letter ‘M’.

376.s:
ahaṃ sākṣī ca cinmātro jāgratsvapnādikasya ca /
nājñānañcaiva tatkāryaṃ saṃsārādikabandhanaṃ //
376.d:
अहं साक्षी च चिन्मात्रो जाग्रत्स्वप्नादिकस्य च /
नाज्ञानञ्चैव तत्कार्यं संसारादिकबन्धनं //
376.m:
I am the witness and pure consciousness of waking, dream, and the like;
neither ignorance nor its effect, the bondage of worldly existence and the like, [is mine].

376.s:
nityaśuddhabandhamuktasatyamānandamadvayaṃ /
:p 332
brahmāhamasmyahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirvimukta oṃ //
376.d:
नित्यशुद्धबन्धमुक्तसत्यमानन्दमद्वयं /
:प् 332
ब्रह्माहमस्म्यहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्विमुक्त ओं //
376.m:
Eternally pure, free from bondage, truth, bliss, non-dual—
[page 332]
I am Brahman; I am Brahman, the supreme light, liberated. Oṃ.

376.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jñānaṃ samādhirbandhaghātakaḥ /
ciramānandakaṃ brahma satyaṃ jñānamanantakaṃ //
376.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्ञानं समाधिर्बन्धघातकः /
चिरमानन्दकं ब्रह्म सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तकं //
376.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme knowledge; absorption is the destroyer of bondage.
Brahman is eternal bliss, truth, knowledge, infinite.

376.s:
ayamātmā parambrahma tad brahma tvamasīti ca /
guruṇā bodhito jīvo hy ahaṃ brahmāsmi vāhyataḥ //
376.d:
अयमात्मा परम्ब्रह्म तद् ब्रह्म त्वमसीति च /
गुरुणा बोधितो जीवो ह्य् अहं ब्रह्मास्मि वाह्यतः //
376.m:
‘This Self is supreme Brahman,’ and ‘You are that Brahman.’
Awakened by the guru, the individual self [realizes], ‘I am indeed Brahman externally.’

376.s:
so 'sāvādityapuruṣaḥ so 'sāvahamakhaṇḍa oṃ /
mucyate 'sārasaṃsārādbrahmajño brahma tadbhavet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe brahmajñānaṃ nāma
ṣaṭsaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha saptasaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
brahmajñānaṃ
376.d:
सो ऽसावादित्यपुरुषः सो ऽसावहमखण्ड ओं /
मुच्यते ऽसारसंसाराद्ब्रह्मज्ञो ब्रह्म तद्भवेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे ब्रह्मज्ञानं नाम
षट्सप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ सप्तसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
ब्रह्मज्ञानं
376.m:
He is that person in the sun; he is that indivisible I. Oṃ.
The knower of Brahman is freed from worthless worldly existence and becomes that Brahman.
Thus in the great Purāṇa composed by Agni, the three hundred and seventy-sixth chapter, named ‘Knowledge of Brahman.’
Now the three hundred and seventy-seventh chapter.
Knowledge of Brahman

377.s:
agnir uvāca
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ pṛthivyavanalojjhitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirvāyvākāśavivarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः पृथिव्यवनलोज्झितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्वाय्वाकाशविवर्जितं //
377.m:
Agni said:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free from earth, water, and fire.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of wind and space.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirādikāryavivarjitam /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirvirāḍātmavivarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिरादिकार्यविवर्जितम् /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्विराडात्मविवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of primary effects.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the Virāj self.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirjāgratsthānavivarjitam /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirviśvabhāvavivarjitam //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्जाग्रत्स्थानविवर्जितम् /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्विश्वभावविवर्जितम् //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the waking state.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the nature of Viśva.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirākārākṣaravarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirvākpāṇyaṅghrivivarjitam //
:p 333
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिराकाराक्षरवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्वाक्पाण्यङ्घ्रिविवर्जितम् //
:प् 333
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the syllable ‘A’.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of speech, hands, and feet.
[page 333]

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ pāyūpasthavivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ śrotratvakcakṣurujjhitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः पायूपस्थविवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः श्रोत्रत्वक्चक्षुरुज्झितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the anus and genitals.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, free from ears, skin, and eyes.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotīrasarūpavivarjitam /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ sarvagandhavivarjitam //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतीरसरूपविवर्जितम् /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः सर्वगन्धविवर्जितम् //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of taste and form.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of all smell.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirjihvāghrāṇavivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ sparśaśabdavivarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्जिह्वाघ्राणविवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः स्पर्शशब्दविवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of tongue and nose.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of touch and sound.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirmanobuddhivivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiścittāhaṅkāravarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्मनोबुद्धिविवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिश्चित्ताहङ्कारवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of mind and intellect.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of thought and ego.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ prāṇāpānavivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirvyānodānavivarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः प्राणापानविवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्व्यानोदानविवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the prāṇa and apāna breaths.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the vyāna and udāna breaths.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ samānaparivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirjarāmaraṇavarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः समानपरिवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्जरामरणवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the samāna breath.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of old age and death.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ śokamohavivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ kṣutpipāsāvivarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः शोकमोहविवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः क्षुत्पिपासाविवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of grief and delusion.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of hunger and thirst.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ śabdodbhūtādivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirhiraṇyagarbhavarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः शब्दोद्भूतादिवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्हिरण्यगर्भवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of what arises from sound and the like.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of Hiraṇyagarbha.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ svapnāvasthāvivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotistaijasādivivarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः स्वप्नावस्थाविवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिस्तैजसादिविवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the dream state.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of Taijasa and the like.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirapakārādivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ sabhājñānavivarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिरपकारादिवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः सभाज्ञानविवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of injury and the like.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the knowledge of an assembly.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiradhyāhṛtavivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ sattvādiguṇavarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिरध्याहृतविवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः सत्त्वादिगुणवर्जितं //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of superimposition.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the qualities such as sattva.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ sadasadbhāvavarjitaṃ /
:p 334
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ sarvāvayavavarjitaṃ //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः सदसद्भाववर्जितं /
:प् 334
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः सर्वावयववर्जितं //

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirbhedābhedavivarjitaṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ suṣuptisthānavarjitam //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्भेदाभेदविवर्जितं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः सुषुप्तिस्थानवर्जितम् //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of difference and non-difference.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the deep sleep state.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ prājñabhāvavivarjitam /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirmakārādivivarjitam //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः प्राज्ञभावविवर्जितम् /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्मकारादिविवर्जितम् //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the nature of Prājña.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the letter ‘M’ and the rest.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirmānameyavivarjitam /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotirmitimāhṛvivarjitam //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्मानमेयविवर्जितम् /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिर्मितिमाहृविवर्जितम् //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of the means of knowledge and the object of knowledge.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of cognition and the knower.

377.s:
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ sākṣitvādivivarjitam /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ kāryakāraṇavarjitam //
377.d:
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः साक्षित्वादिविवर्जितम् /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः कार्यकारणवर्जितम् //
377.m:
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of witnesshood and the like.
I am Brahman, the supreme light, devoid of effect and cause.

377.s:
dehendriyamanobuddhiprāṇāhaṅkāravarjitaṃ /
jāgrat sapnasuṣuptyādimuktaṃ brahma turīyakaṃ //
377.d:
देहेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिप्राणाहङ्कारवर्जितं /
जाग्रत् सप्नसुषुप्त्यादिमुक्तं ब्रह्म तुरीयकं //
377.m:
Devoid of the body, sense organs, mind, intellect, vital breath, and ego,
freed from waking, dream, deep sleep, and the like, Brahman is the fourth.

377.s:
nityaśuddhabuddhamuktaṃ satyamānandamadvayam /
brahmāhamasmyahaṃ brahma savijñānaṃ vimukta oṃ /
ahaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ samādhirmokṣadaḥ paraḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe samādhirnāma saptasaptatyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 335
:ś athāṣṭasaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
brahmajñānaṃ
377.d:
नित्यशुद्धबुद्धमुक्तं सत्यमानन्दमद्वयम् /
ब्रह्माहमस्म्यहं ब्रह्म सविज्ञानं विमुक्त ओं /
अहं ब्रह्म परं ज्योतिः समाधिर्मोक्षदः परः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे समाधिर्नाम सप्तसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 335
:श् अथाष्टसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
ब्रह्मज्ञानं
377.m:
Eternally pure, awakened, liberated, truth, bliss, non-dual,
I am Brahman, I am Brahman with full realization, liberated. Oṃ.
I am Brahman, the supreme light; absorption is the supreme giver of liberation.
Thus in the great Purāṇa composed by Agni, the three hundred and seventy-seventh chapter, named ‘Absorption.’
[page 335]
Now the three hundred and seventy-eighth chapter.
Knowledge of Brahman

378.s:
agnir uvāca
yajñaiś ca devānāpnoti vairājaṃ tapasā padaṃ /
brahmaṇaḥ karmasannyāsādvairāgyāt prakṛtau layaṃ //
378.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
यज्ञैश् च देवानाप्नोति वैराजं तपसा पदं /
ब्रह्मणः कर्मसन्न्यासाद्वैराग्यात् प्रकृतौ लयं //
378.m:
Agni said:
By sacrifices one attains the gods; by ascetic austerity, the station of the Virāj; / through the renunciation of actions, [the realm] of Brahmā; through dispassion, dissolution in Prakṛti;

378.s:
jñānāt prāpnoti kaivalyaṃ pañcaitā gatayaḥsmṛtāḥ /
prītitāpaviṣādādervinivṛttirviraktatā //
378.d:
ज्ञानात् प्राप्नोति कैवल्यं पञ्चैता गतयःस्मृताः /
प्रीतितापविषादादेर्विनिवृत्तिर्विरक्तता //
378.m: through knowledge one attains absolute liberation: these five destinations are recalled. / Dispassion is the cessation of pleasure, suffering, dejection, and the like.

378.s:
sannyāsaḥ karmaṇāntyāgaḥ kṛtānāmakṛtaiḥ saha /
avyaktādau viśeṣānte vikāro 'sminnivartate //
378.d:
सन्न्यासः कर्मणान्त्यागः कृतानामकृतैः सह /
अव्यक्तादौ विशेषान्ते विकारो ऽस्मिन्निवर्तते //
378.m: Renunciation is the abandonment of actions, those performed along with those unperformed. / In this [state], change from the unmanifest onwards up to the specific [elements] ceases.

378.s:
cetanācetanānyatvajñānena jñānamucyate /
paramātmā ca sarveṣāmādhāraḥ parameśvaraḥ //
378.d:
चेतनाचेतनान्यत्वज्ञानेन ज्ञानमुच्यते /
परमात्मा च सर्वेषामाधारः परमेश्वरः //
378.m: By the knowledge of the distinction between the conscious and the unconscious, it is called knowledge. / And the supreme Self is the support of all, the supreme Lord;

378.s:
viṣṇunāmnā ca deveṣu vedānteṣu ca gīyate /
yajñeśvaro yajñapumān pravṛttair ijyate hy asau //
378.d:
विष्णुनाम्ना च देवेषु वेदान्तेषु च गीयते /
यज्ञेश्वरो यज्ञपुमान् प्रवृत्तैर् इज्यते ह्य् असौ //
378.m: and by the name Viṣṇu he is sung among the gods and in the Vedāntas. / He, the Lord of sacrifice and the Sacrificial Person, is indeed worshipped by those devoted to active life;

378.s:
nivṛttair jñānayogena jñānamūrtiḥ sa cekṣyate /
hrasvadīrghaplutādyantu vacastatpuruṣottamaḥ //
378.d:
निवृत्तैर् ज्ञानयोगेन ज्ञानमूर्तिः स चेक्ष्यते /
ह्रस्वदीर्घप्लुताद्यन्तु वचस्तत्पुरुषोत्तमः //
378.m: by those devoted to cessation, he is beheld through the yoga of knowledge as the embodiment of knowledge. / And speech—short, long, protracted, and so forth—that is Puruṣottama.

378.s:
tatprāptiheturjñānañca karma coktaṃ mahāmune /
āgamoktaṃ vivekācca dvidhā jñānaṃ tathocyate //
378.d:
तत्प्राप्तिहेतुर्ज्ञानञ्च कर्म चोक्तं महामुने /
आगमोक्तं विवेकाच्च द्विधा ज्ञानं तथोच्यते //
378.m: Knowledge and action have been declared to be the cause of attaining him, O great sage. / And knowledge is likewise declared to be twofold: stated in scripture and born of discernment.

378.s:
śabdabrahmāgamamayaṃ paraṃ brahma vivekajam /
dve brahmaṇī veditavye brahmaśabdaparañca yat //
378.d:
शब्दब्रह्मागममयं परं ब्रह्म विवेकजम् /
द्वे ब्रह्मणी वेदितव्ये ब्रह्मशब्दपरञ्च यत् //
378.m: The sound-Brahman consists of scripture, while the supreme Brahman is born of discernment. / Two Brahmans are to be known: that which is the sound-Brahman, and that which is beyond.

378.s:
vedādividyā hy aparamakṣaraṃ brahmasatparam /
tadetadbhagavadvācyamupacāre 'rcane 'nyataḥ //
378.d:
वेदादिविद्या ह्य् अपरमक्षरं ब्रह्मसत्परम् /
तदेतद्भगवद्वाच्यमुपचारे ऽर्चने ऽन्यतः //
378.m: The lower [Brahman] is the knowledge of the Vedas and the like; the imperishable, supreme Brahman is true existence. / That word 'Bhagavat' designates this [Brahman], used metaphorically in worshipping another.

378.s:
sambharteti tathā bhartā bhakāro 'rthadvayānvitaḥ /
netā gamayitā sraṣṭā gakāro 'yaṃ mahamune //
:p 336
378.d:
सम्भर्तेति तथा भर्ता भकारो ऽर्थद्वयान्वितः /
नेता गमयिता स्रष्टा गकारो ऽयं महमुने //
:प् 336
378.m:
The syllable 'bha' has two meanings: 'sustainer' and likewise 'supporter'. / The syllable 'ga', O great sage, means 'leader', 'conveyor', and 'creator'.
[Page 336]

378.s:
aiśvaryasya samagrasya vīryasya yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ /
jñānavairāgyayoś caiva ṣaṇāṃ bhaga itīṅganā //
378.d:
ऐश्वर्यस्य समग्रस्य वीर्यस्य यशसः श्रियः /
ज्ञानवैराग्ययोश् चैव षणां भग इतीङ्गना //
378.m: All majesty, power, glory, and splendour, / and both knowledge and dispassion—the designation for these six is 'bhaga'.

378.s:
vasanti viṣṇau bhutāni sa ca dhātustridhātmakaḥ /
evaṃ harau hi bhagavān śabdo 'nyatropacārataḥ //
378.d:
वसन्ति विष्णौ भुतानि स च धातुस्त्रिधात्मकः /
एवं हरौ हि भगवान् शब्दो ऽन्यत्रोपचारतः //
378.m: Beings reside in Viṣṇu, and that verbal root has a threefold nature; / thus the word *bhagavān* truly applies to Hari, but elsewhere only metaphorically.

378.s:
utpattiṃ pralayaś caiva bhūtānāmagatiṃ gatiṃ /
vetti vidyāmavidyāñca sa vācyo bhagavāniti //
378.d:
उत्पत्तिं प्रलयश् चैव भूतानामगतिं गतिं /
वेत्ति विद्यामविद्याञ्च स वाच्यो भगवानिति //
378.m: He who knows the origin and dissolution, the coming and going of beings, / and knowledge and ignorance, is properly denoted by the word *bhagavān*.

378.s:
jñānaśaktiḥ paraiśvaryaṃ vīryaṃ tejāṃsyaśeṣataḥ /
bhagavacchabdavācyāni vinā heyair guṇādibhiḥ //
378.d:
ज्ञानशक्तिः परैश्वर्यं वीर्यं तेजांस्यशेषतः /
भगवच्छब्दवाच्यानि विना हेयैर् गुणादिभिः //
378.m: Power of knowledge, supreme sovereignty, prowess, and energy without remainder / are what is denoted by the word *bhagavān*, free from base qualities and the like.

378.s:
khāṇḍikyajanakāyāha yogaṃ keśidhvajaḥ purā /
anātmanyātmabuddhiryā ātmasvamiti yā matiḥ //
378.d:
खाण्डिक्यजनकायाह योगं केशिध्वजः पुरा /
अनात्मन्यात्मबुद्धिर्या आत्मस्वमिति या मतिः //
378.m: Keśidhvaja of old taught yoga to Khāṇḍikya Janaka: / that notion of self in what is not the self, that thought that something belongs to the self,

378.s:
avidyābhavambhūtirvījametaddvidhā sthiram /
pañcabhūtātmake dehe dehī mohatamāśritaḥ //
378.d:
अविद्याभवम्भूतिर्वीजमेतद्द्विधा स्थिरम् /
पञ्चभूतात्मके देहे देही मोहतमाश्रितः //
378.m: is the firm, twofold seed that produces worldly existence through ignorance. / In the body composed of the five elements, the embodied self, resorting to the darkness of delusion,

378.s:
ahametaditītyuccaiḥ kurute kumatirmatiṃ /
itthañca putrapautreṣu taddehotpātiteṣu ca //
378.d:
अहमेतदितीत्युच्चैः कुरुते कुमतिर्मतिं /
इत्थञ्च पुत्रपौत्रेषु तद्देहोत्पातितेषु च //
378.m: the fool, constantly forms the notion: 'I am this.' / And likewise, regarding sons, grandsons, and those born of their bodies,

378.s:
karoti paṇḍitaḥ sāmyamanātmani kalevare /
sarvadehopakārāya kurute karma mānavaḥ //
378.d:
करोति पण्डितः साम्यमनात्मनि कलेवरे /
सर्वदेहोपकाराय कुरुते कर्म मानवः //
378.m: the wise man forms an equal view [of identity] with the body which is not the self; / a person performs action for the benefit of the whole body.

378.s:
dehaścānyo yadā puṃsastadā bandhāya tatparaṃ /
nirvāṇamaya evāyamātmā jñānamayo 'malaḥ //
378.d:
देहश्चान्यो यदा पुंसस्तदा बन्धाय तत्परं /
निर्वाणमय एवायमात्मा ज्ञानमयो ऽमलः //
378.m: Since the body is distinct from the person, it then leads to bondage; / this self is entirely of the nature of nirvāṇa, of knowledge, and spotless.

378.s:
duḥkhajñānamayo 'dharmaḥ prakṛteḥ sa tu nātmanaḥ /
jalasya nāgninā saṅgaḥ sthālīsaṅgāttathāpi hi //
378.d:
दुःखज्ञानमयो ऽधर्मः प्रकृतेः स तु नात्मनः /
जलस्य नाग्निना सङ्गः स्थालीसङ्गात्तथापि हि //
378.m: What consists of misery and ignorance is unrighteousness; that belongs to nature, but not to the self. / Water has no contact with fire, yet through contact with the pot [it is heated];

378.s:
śabdāste kādikā dharmāstat kṛtā vai mahāmune /
tathātmā prakṛtau saṅgādahaṃmānādibhūṣitaḥ //
378.d:
शब्दास्ते कादिका धर्मास्तत् कृता वै महामुने /
तथात्मा प्रकृतौ सङ्गादहंमानादिभूषितः //
378.m: the sounds beginning with *ka* are qualities produced by that, O great sage. / In the same way, the self, through contact with nature, adorned with ego and the like,

378.s:
bhajate prākṛtāndharmān anyastebhyo hi so 'vyayaḥ /
:p 337
vandhāya viṣayāsaṅgaṃ mano nirviṣayaṃ dhiye //
378.d:
भजते प्राकृतान्धर्मान् अन्यस्तेभ्यो हि सो ऽव्ययः /
:प् 337
वन्धाय विषयासङ्गं मनो निर्विषयं धिये //
378.m:
experiences the qualities of nature, though it is distinct from them and imperishable.
[page 337]
Attachment to sense objects leads to bondage; a mind free of sense objects leads to knowledge.

378.s:
viṣayāttatsamākṛṣya brahmabhūtaṃ hariṃ smaret /
ātmabhāvaṃ nayatyenaṃ tadbrahmadhyāyinaṃ mune //
378.d:
विषयात्तत्समाकृष्य ब्रह्मभूतं हरिं स्मरेत् /
आत्मभावं नयत्येनं तद्ब्रह्मध्यायिनं मुने //
378.m: Having withdrawn it from sense objects, one should remember Hari, who has become Brahman; / he leads that meditator on Brahman into his own essential nature, O sage,

378.s:
vicārya svātmanaḥ śaktyā lauhamākarṣako yathā /
ātmaprayatnasāpekṣā viśiṣṭā yā manogatiḥ //
378.d:
विचार्य स्वात्मनः शक्त्या लौहमाकर्षको यथा /
आत्मप्रयत्नसापेक्षा विशिष्टा या मनोगतिः //
378.m: deliberating by the power of his own self, just as a magnet attracts iron. / That distinct movement of the mind which is dependent upon personal effort,

378.s:
tasyā brahmaṇi saṃyogo yoga ity abhidhīyate /
viniṣpandaḥ samādhisthaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati //
378.d:
तस्या ब्रह्मणि संयोगो योग इत्य् अभिधीयते /
विनिष्पन्दः समाधिस्थः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति //
378.m: its union with Brahman is termed yoga; / motionless, established in samādhi, one attains the supreme Brahman.

378.s:
yamaiḥ sanniyamaiḥ sthityā pratyāhṛtyā marujjayaiḥ /
prāṇāyāmena pavanaiḥ pratyāhāreṇa cendriyaiḥ //
378.d:
यमैः सन्नियमैः स्थित्या प्रत्याहृत्या मरुज्जयैः /
प्राणायामेन पवनैः प्रत्याहारेण चेन्द्रियैः //
378.m: By restraints, proper observances, posture, breath control, conquering the winds, / by regulation of breath, by the winds, and through withdrawal with the sense organs,

378.s:
vaśīkṛtaistataḥ kuryāt sthitaṃ cetaḥ śubhāśraye /
āśrayaścetaso brahma mūrtañcāmūrtakaṃ dvidhā //
378.d:
वशीकृतैस्ततः कुर्यात् स्थितं चेतः शुभाश्रये /
आश्रयश्चेतसो ब्रह्म मूर्तञ्चामूर्तकं द्विधा //
378.m: brought under control, one should then fix the steady mind on an auspicious support; / the support of the mind is Brahman, twofold: with form and formless.

378.s:
sanandanādayo brahmabhāvabhāvanayā yutāḥ /
karmabhāvanayā cānye devādyāḥ sthāvarāntakāḥ //
378.d:
सनन्दनादयो ब्रह्मभावभावनया युताः /
कर्मभावनया चान्ये देवाद्याः स्थावरान्तकाः //
378.m: Sanandana and others are endowed with meditation on the state of Brahman, / while others, from the gods down to immovable things, are endowed with meditation on action.

378.s:
hiraṇyagarbhādiṣu ca jñānakarmātmikā dvidhā /
trividhā bhāvanā proktā viśvaṃ brahma upāsyate //
378.d:
हिरण्यगर्भादिषु च ज्ञानकर्मात्मिका द्विधा /
त्रिविधा भावना प्रोक्ता विश्वं ब्रह्म उपास्यते //
378.m: And in Hiraṇyagarbha and others, it is twofold, consisting of knowledge and action. / Meditation is taught to be threefold; Brahman is worshipped as the universe.

378.s:
pratyastamitabhedaṃ yat sattāmātramagocaraṃ /
vacasāmātmasaṃvedyaṃ tajjñānaṃ brahma saṃjñitam //
378.d:
प्रत्यस्तमितभेदं यत् सत्तामात्रमगोचरं /
वचसामात्मसंवेद्यं तज्ज्ञानं ब्रह्म संज्ञितम् //
378.m: That in which differentiation has ceased, which is pure existence, beyond the range / of words, knowable only in oneself—that knowledge is designated as Brahman.

378.s:
tacca viṣṇoḥ paraṃ rūpamarūpasyājamakṣaraṃ /
aśakyaṃ prathamaṃ dhyātumato mūrtādi cintayet //
378.d:
तच्च विष्णोः परं रूपमरूपस्याजमक्षरं /
अशक्यं प्रथमं ध्यातुमतो मूर्तादि चिन्तयेत् //
378.m: And that is the supreme form of Viṣṇu, who is formless, unborn, and imperishable; / it is impossible to meditate upon it at first, therefore one should contemplate [him] as possessing form, etc.

378.s:
sadbhāvabhāvamāpannastato 'sau paramātmanā /
bhavatyabhedī bhedaś ca tasyājñānakṛto bhavet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe brahmajñānaṃ
nāmāṣṭasaptatyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 338
:ś athonāśītyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
advaitabrahmavijñānaṃ
378.d:
सद्भावभावमापन्नस्ततो ऽसौ परमात्मना /
भवत्यभेदी भेदश् च तस्याज्ञानकृतो भवेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे ब्रह्मज्ञानं
नामाष्टसप्तत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 338
:श् अथोनाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
अद्वैतब्रह्मविज्ञानं
378.m:
Having attained the state of true being, he then / becomes non-different from the Supreme Self, and difference is produced only by ignorance.
Thus, in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, the three hundred seventy-eighth chapter, entitled 'The Knowledge of Brahman'.
[page 338]
Now, the three hundred seventy-ninth chapter:
The Discernment of Non-dual Brahman.

379.s:
agnir uvāca
advaitabrahmavijñānaṃ vakṣye yadbhavato 'gadat /
śālagrāne tapaś cakre vāsudevārcanādikṛt //
379.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
अद्वैतब्रह्मविज्ञानं वक्ष्ये यद्भवतो ऽगदत् /
शालग्राने तपश् चक्रे वासुदेवार्चनादिकृत् //
379.m: Agni said: / I shall declare the discernment of non-dual Brahman, which he spoke to you. / He performed ascetic austerity in Śālagrāma, performing worship and the like of Vāsudeva.

379.s:
mṛgasaṅgāmmṛgo bhūtvā hy antakāle smaran mṛgaṃ /
jātismaro mṛgastyaktvā dehaṃ yogātsvato 'bhavat //
379.d:
मृगसङ्गाम्मृगो भूत्वा ह्य् अन्तकाले स्मरन् मृगं /
जातिस्मरो मृगस्त्यक्त्वा देहं योगात्स्वतो ऽभवत् //
379.m: Having become a deer due to association with a deer, remembering the deer at the time of death, / remembering his previous births, the deer shed its body and, through yoga, became himself.

379.s:
advaitabrahmabhūtaś ca jaḍavallokamācarat /
kṣattāsau vīrarājasya viṣṭiyogamamanyata //
379.d:
अद्वैतब्रह्मभूतश् च जडवल्लोकमाचरत् /
क्षत्तासौ वीरराजस्य विष्टियोगममन्यत //
379.m: And having become non-dual Brahman, he moved among people like an idiot. / A chamberlain of the valorous king considered him fit for forced labor.

379.s:
uvāha śivikrāmasya kṣatturvacanacoditaḥ /
gṛhīto viṣṭinā jñānī uvāhātmakṣayāya taṃ //
379.d:
उवाह शिविक्रामस्य क्षत्तुर्वचनचोदितः /
गृहीतो विष्टिना ज्ञानी उवाहात्मक्षयाय तं //
379.m: Urged by the chamberlain's word, he carried the palanquin of him; / seized for forced labor, the knower carried him for the destruction of his own [past karma].

379.s:
yayau jaḍagatiḥ paścāt ye tvanye tvaritaṃ yayuḥ /
śīghrān śīghragatīn dṛṣṭvā aśīghraṃ taṃ nṛpo'bravīt //
rājovāca
379.d:
ययौ जडगतिः पश्चात् ये त्वन्ये त्वरितं ययुः /
शीघ्रान् शीघ्रगतीन् दृष्ट्वा अशीघ्रं तं नृपोऽब्रवीत् //
राजोवाच
379.m:
He went with sluggish pace behind, while the others went swiftly; / seeing the swift moving quickly, the king said to him who was not swift:
The king said:

379.s:
kiṃ śrānto 'syalpamadhvānaṃ tvayoḍhā śivikā mama /
kimāyāsasaho na tvaṃ pīvānasi nirīkṣyase //
379.d:
किं श्रान्तो ऽस्यल्पमध्वानं त्वयोढा शिविका मम /
किमायाससहो न त्वं पीवानसि निरीक्ष्यसे //
379.m: "Are you tired? My palanquin has been carried by you for only a short distance. / Can you not endure exertion? You are observed to be stout."

379.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
nāhaṃ pīvānna vaiṣoḍhā śivikā bhavato mayā /
na śrānto 'smi na vāyāso voḍhavyo 'si mahīpate //
379.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
नाहं पीवान्न वैषोढा शिविका भवतो मया /
न श्रान्तो ऽस्मि न वायासो वोढव्यो ऽसि महीपते //
379.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / "I am not stout, nor indeed has this palanquin of yours been carried by me; / I am not tired, nor is exertion to be endured by me, O ruler of the earth.

379.s:
bhūmau pādayugantasthau jaṅghe pādadvaye sthite /
urū jaṅghādvayāvasthau tadādhāraṃ tathodaram //
379.d:
भूमौ पादयुगन्तस्थौ जङ्घे पादद्वये स्थिते /
उरू जङ्घाद्वयावस्थौ तदाधारं तथोदरम् //
379.m: The pair of feet rests on the earth, the shanks rest on the pair of feet, / the thighs rest on the pair of shanks, and the abdomen has them as its base;

379.s:
vakṣaḥsthalaṃ tathā vāhū skandhau codarasaṃsthitau /
skandhasthiteyaṃ śivikā mama bhāvo 'tra kiṃ kṛtaḥ //
:p 339
379.d:
वक्षःस्थलं तथा वाहू स्कन्धौ चोदरसंस्थितौ /
स्कन्धस्थितेयं शिविका मम भावो ऽत्र किं कृतः //
:प् 339
379.m:
likewise the chest, the arms, and the shoulders rest on the abdomen; / this palanquin rests on the shoulder: where is any sense of 'mine' produced here?
[page 339]

379.s:
śivikāyāṃ sthitañcedaṃ dehaṃ tvadupalakṣitaṃ /
tatra tvamahamapyatra procyate cedamanyathā //
379.d:
शिविकायां स्थितञ्चेदं देहं त्वदुपलक्षितं /
तत्र त्वमहमप्यत्र प्रोच्यते चेदमन्यथा //
379.m: And this body, indicated as 'you', is situated in the palanquin; / there 'you', and also 'I' here, are spoken of, but it is otherwise.

379.s:
ahaṃ tvañca tathānye ca bhūtairuhyāma(1) pārthiva /
guṇapravāhapatito guṇavargo hi yātyayaṃ //
379.d:
अहं त्वञ्च तथान्ये च भूतैरुह्याम(1) पार्थिव /
गुणप्रवाहपतितो गुणवर्गो हि यात्ययं //
379.m: I, and you, and likewise others, are carried by the material elements, O king; / fallen into the stream of the qualities, this collection of qualities indeed moves along.

379.s:
karmavaśyā guṇāś caite sattvādyāḥ pṛthivīpate /
avidyāsañcitaṃ karma taccāśeṣeṣu jantuṣu //
379.d:
कर्मवश्या गुणाश् चैते सत्त्वाद्याः पृथिवीपते /
अविद्यासञ्चितं कर्म तच्चाशेषेषु जन्तुषु //
379.m: And these qualities, sattva and the rest, are subject to karma, O lord of the earth; / and karma is accumulated through ignorance in all living beings.

379.s:
ātmā śuddho 'kṣaraḥ śānto nirguṇaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ /
pravṛddhyapacayau nāsya ekasyākhilajantuṣu //
379.d:
आत्मा शुद्धो ऽक्षरः शान्तो निर्गुणः प्रकृतेः परः /
प्रवृद्ध्यपचयौ नास्य एकस्याखिलजन्तुषु //
379.m: The self is pure, imperishable, tranquil, devoid of qualities, higher than nature; / it has neither increase nor decrease, being one in all living beings.

379.s:
yadā nopacayastasya yadā nāpacayo nṛpa /
tadā pīvānasīti tvaṃ kayā yuktyā tvayeritaṃ //
379.d:
यदा नोपचयस्तस्य यदा नापचयो नृप /
तदा पीवानसीति त्वं कया युक्त्या त्वयेरितं //
379.m: Since it has no increase, and since it has no decrease, O king, / then by what reasoning was it said by you: 'You are stout'?

379.s:
bhūjaṅghāpādakaṭyūrujaṭharādiṣu saṃsthitā /
śivikeyaṃ tathā skandhe tadā bhāvaḥsamastvayā //
379.d:
भूजङ्घापादकट्यूरुजठरादिषु संस्थिता /
शिविकेयं तथा स्कन्धे तदा भावःसमस्त्वया //
379.m: Resting upon the ground, shanks, feet, waist, thighs, belly, and so forth, / this palanquin is likewise on the shoulder; then the state is equal with you.

379.s:
tadanyajantubhirbhūpa śivikotthānakarmaṇā /
śailadravyagṛhotthopi pṛthivīsambhavopi vā //
379.d:
तदन्यजन्तुभिर्भूप शिविकोत्थानकर्मणा /
शैलद्रव्यगृहोत्थोपि पृथिवीसम्भवोपि वा //
379.m: By other creatures, O king, through the act of lifting the palanquin, / whether produced from the material of a mountain, a house, or born of the earth,

379.s:
yathā puṃsaḥ pṛthagbhāvaḥ prākṛtaiḥ karaṇair nṛpa /
soḍhavyaḥ sa mahābhāraḥ kataro nṛpate mayā //
379.d:
यथा पुंसः पृथग्भावः प्राकृतैः करणैर् नृप /
सोढव्यः स महाभारः कतरो नृपते मया //
379.m: just as there is a distinct state of the person from the material instruments, O king, / which great burden is to be endured, O king, by me?

379.s:
yaddravyā śivikā ceyaṃ taddravyo bhūtasaṃgrahaḥ /
bhavato me 'khilasyāsya samatvenopavṛṃhitaḥ //
379.d:
यद्द्रव्या शिविका चेयं तद्द्रव्यो भूतसंग्रहः /
भवतो मे ऽखिलस्यास्य समत्वेनोपवृंहितः //
379.m: Of whatever material this palanquin is, of that material is this assemblage of elements / of yours and of mine; it is expanded through equality of all this."

379.s:
tacchrutvovāca rājā taṃ gṛhītvāṅghrī kṣamāpya ca /
prasādaṃ kuru tyaktvemāṃ śivikāṃ brūhi śṛṇvate /
yo bhavān yannimittaṃ vā yadāgamanakāraṇam //
379.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वोवाच राजा तं गृहीत्वाङ्घ्री क्षमाप्य च /
प्रसादं कुरु त्यक्त्वेमां शिविकां ब्रूहि शृण्वते /
यो भवान् यन्निमित्तं वा यदागमनकारणम् //
379.m: Hearing that, the king seized his feet, asked for pardon, and said to him: / "Grant your favor! Leaving this palanquin, tell me who listens: / who are you, or for what purpose, or what is the reason for your coming?"

379.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
śrūyatāṃ kohamityetadvaktuṃ naiva ca śakyate /
:n
1 pāṭho 'yaṃ na samīcīnaḥ
:p 340
upabhoganimittañca sarvatrāgamanakriyā //
379.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
श्रूयतां कोहमित्येतद्वक्तुं नैव च शक्यते /
:न्
1 पाठो ऽयं न समीचीनः
:प् 340
उपभोगनिमित्तञ्च सर्वत्रागमनक्रिया //
379.m:
The brāhmaṇa said: / "Listen: 'Who am I?'—this cannot possibly be said.
[...]
1 This reading is not correct. / [page 340]
And the act of coming everywhere has experiencing as its purpose.

379.s:
sukhaduḥkhopabhogau tu tau deśādyupapādakau /
dharmādharmodbhavau bhoktuṃ janturdeśādimṛcchati //
rajovāca
379.d:
सुखदुःखोपभोगौ तु तौ देशाद्युपपादकौ /
धर्माधर्मोद्भवौ भोक्तुं जन्तुर्देशादिमृच्छति //
रजोवाच
379.m:
For the experiences of pleasure and pain, they bring about [birth in] a region and the like; / to experience [fruits] arisen from virtue and vice, a creature goes to a region and the like."
The king said:

379.s:
yo 'sti sohamiti brahman kathaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyate /
ātmanyeṣu na doṣāya śabdohamiti yo dvija //
379.d:
यो ऽस्ति सोहमिति ब्रह्मन् कथं वक्तुं न शक्यते /
आत्मन्येषु न दोषाय शब्दोहमिति यो द्विज //
379.m: "He who exists is 'I'—why can this not be said, O holy one? / The word 'I', O twice-born, does not bring fault when applied to these selves."

379.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
śabdohamiti doṣāya nātmanyeṣa tathaiva tat /
anātmanyātmavijñānaṃ śabdo vā bhrāntilakṣaṇaḥ //
379.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
शब्दोहमिति दोषाय नात्मन्येष तथैव तत् /
अनात्मन्यात्मविज्ञानं शब्दो वा भ्रान्तिलक्षणः //
379.m: The brāhmaṇa said: / "The word 'I' does not bring fault with respect to the self; that is indeed true. / The notion of self in what is not the self, or the word, has the mark of delusion."

379.s:
yadā samastadeheṣu pumāneko vyavasthitaḥ /
tadā hi ko bhavān kohamityetadviphalaṃ vacaḥ //
379.d:
यदा समस्तदेहेषु पुमानेको व्यवस्थितः /
तदा हि को भवान् कोहमित्येतद्विफलं वचः //
379.m: When a single person dwells in all bodies, / then indeed the words 'Who are you?' and 'Who am I?' are pointless.

379.s:
tvaṃ rājā śivikā ceyaṃ vayaṃ vāhāḥ puraḥsarāḥ /
ayañca bhavato loko na sadetannṛpocyate //
379.d:
त्वं राजा शिविका चेयं वयं वाहाः पुरःसराः /
अयञ्च भवतो लोको न सदेतन्नृपोच्यते //
379.m: You are the king, this is a palanquin, we are the bearers running ahead, / and this is your retinue—O king, this is not said to be real.

379.s:
vṛkṣāddāru tataśceyaṃ śivikā tvadadhiṣṭhitā /
kā vṛkṣasaṃjñā jātasya dārusaṃjñātha vā nṛpa //
379.d:
वृक्षाद्दारु ततश्चेयं शिविका त्वदधिष्ठिता /
का वृक्षसंज्ञा जातस्य दारुसंज्ञाथ वा नृप //
379.m: From a tree comes wood, and from that this palanquin which you occupy; / what is the designation 'tree', or the designation 'wood', of that which has been made, O king?

379.s:
vṛkṣārūḍho mahārājo nāyaṃ vadati cetanaḥ /
na ca dāruṇi sarvastvāṃ bravīti śivikāgataṃ //
379.d:
वृक्षारूढो महाराजो नायं वदति चेतनः /
न च दारुणि सर्वस्त्वां ब्रवीति शिविकागतं //
379.m: No conscious person says, 'The great king has mounted a tree,' / nor does everyone say to you sitting in the palanquin, '[You are mounted] upon wood.'

379.s:
śivikādārusaṅghāto racanāsthitisaṃsthitaḥ /
anviṣyatāṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha tadbhede śivikā tvayā //
379.d:
शिविकादारुसङ्घातो रचनास्थितिसंस्थितः /
अन्विष्यतां नृपश्रेष्ठ तद्भेदे शिविका त्वया //
379.m: A palanquin is an aggregate of pieces of wood arranged in a specific structure; / if that is taken apart, O best of kings, search for the palanquin!

379.s:
pumān strī gaurayaṃ vājī kuñcaro vihagastaruḥ /
deheṣu lokasaṃjñeyaṃ vijñeyā karmahetuṣu //
379.d:
पुमान् स्त्री गौरयं वाजी कुञ्चरो विहगस्तरुः /
देहेषु लोकसंज्ञेयं विज्ञेया कर्महेतुषु //
379.m: 'Man', 'woman', 'this is an ox', 'horse', 'elephant', 'bird', 'tree'— / this conventional worldly designation is to be understood as applied to bodies produced by karma.

379.s:
jihvā bravītyahamiti dantauṣṭhau tālukaṃ nṛpa /
ete nāhaṃ yataḥ sarve vāṅnipādanahetavaḥ //
379.d:
जिह्वा ब्रवीत्यहमिति दन्तौष्ठौ तालुकं नृप /
एते नाहं यतः सर्वे वाङ्निपादनहेतवः //
379.m: The tongue says 'I', as do the teeth, the lips, and the palate, O king; / these are not 'I', since all of them are merely the causes that produce speech.

379.s:
kiṃ hetubhirvadatyeṣā vāgevāhamiti svayaṃ /
tathāpi vāṅnāhametaduktaṃ mithyā na yujyate //
:p 341
379.d:
किं हेतुभिर्वदत्येषा वागेवाहमिति स्वयं /
तथापि वाङ्नाहमेतदुक्तं मिथ्या न युज्यते //
:प् 341
379.m:
Does speech itself speak 'I' through these causes? / Even then, speech is not 'I'; this statement cannot be false.
[p. 341]

379.s:
piṇḍaḥ pṛthag yataḥ puṃsaḥ śiraḥpāyvādilakṣaṇaḥ /
tato 'hamiti kutraitāṃ saṃjñāṃ rājan karomyahaṃ //
379.d:
पिण्डः पृथग् यतः पुंसः शिरःपाय्वादिलक्षणः /
ततो ऽहमिति कुत्रैतां संज्ञां राजन् करोम्यहं //
379.m: Since the physical body, characterized by the head, anus, and other parts, is distinct from the person, / where, then, O king, am I to apply this designation 'I'?

379.s:
yadanyo 'sti paraḥ kopi mattaḥ pārthivasattama /
tadeṣohamayaṃ cānyo vaktum evamapīṣyate //
379.d:
यदन्यो ऽस्ति परः कोपि मत्तः पार्थिवसत्तम /
तदेषोहमयं चान्यो वक्तुम् एवमपीष्यते //
379.m: If there were another person supreme and distinct from me, O best of kings, / then it would be appropriate to say, 'This is I, and that is another.'

379.s:
paramārthabhedo na nago na paśurnaca pādapaḥ /
śarīrāś ca vibhedāś ca ya ete karmayonayaḥ //
379.d:
परमार्थभेदो न नगो न पशुर्नच पादपः /
शरीराश् च विभेदाश् च य एते कर्मयोनयः //
379.m: In the ultimate sense there is no mountain, no beast, and no tree; / and the diverse bodies are merely those born of karma.

379.s:
yastu rājeti yalloke yacca rājabhaṭātmakam /
taccānyacca nṛpetthantu na sat samyaganāmayaṃ //
379.d:
यस्तु राजेति यल्लोके यच्च राजभटात्मकम् /
तच्चान्यच्च नृपेत्थन्तु न सत् सम्यगनामयं //
379.m: That which in the world is called 'king', and that which consists of a king's soldiers— / that and the other things, O king, are in this manner not truly real or free from affliction.

379.s:
tvaṃ rājā sarvalokasya pituḥ putro riporipuḥ/
patnyāḥ patiḥ pitā sūnoḥ kastvāṃ bhūpa vadāmyahaṃ //
379.d:
त्वं राजा सर्वलोकस्य पितुः पुत्रो रिपोरिपुः/
पत्न्याः पतिः पिता सूनोः कस्त्वां भूप वदाम्यहं //
379.m: You are king to all the people, son to your father, enemy to your foe, / husband to your wife, father to your son—who are you, O king, that I should address?

379.s:
tvaṃ kimetacchiraḥ kinnu śirastava tathodaraṃ /
kimu pādādikaṃ tvaṃ vai tavaitat kiṃ mahīpate //
379.d:
त्वं किमेतच्छिरः किन्नु शिरस्तव तथोदरं /
किमु पादादिकं त्वं वै तवैतत् किं महीपते //
379.m: Are you this head, or is the head yours? Likewise the belly: / are you the feet and other limbs, or are these yours, O lord of the earth?

379.s:
samastāvayebhyastvaṃ pṛthagbhūto vyavasthitaḥ /
kohamityatra nipuṇaṃ bhūtvā cintaya pārthiva /
tacchratvovāca rājā tamavadhūtaṃ dvijaṃ hariṃ //
rajovāca
379.d:
समस्तावयेभ्यस्त्वं पृथग्भूतो व्यवस्थितः /
कोहमित्यत्र निपुणं भूत्वा चिन्तय पार्थिव /
तच्छ्रत्वोवाच राजा तमवधूतं द्विजं हरिं //
रजोवाच
379.m:
You exist distinct from all your limbs. / Having reflected deeply on this, O ruler of the earth, consider: 'Who am I?'"
Having heard that, the king spoke to that brāhmaṇa, the renounced ascetic, Hari:
The king said:

379.s:
śreyo 'rthamudyataḥ praṣṭuṃ kapilarṣimahaṃ dvija /
tasyāṃśaḥ kapilarṣestvaṃ mat kṛte jñānado bhuvi /
jñānavīcyudacheryasmādyacchreyastacca me vada //
379.d:
श्रेयो ऽर्थमुद्यतः प्रष्टुं कपिलर्षिमहं द्विज /
तस्यांशः कपिलर्षेस्त्वं मत् कृते ज्ञानदो भुवि /
ज्ञानवीच्युदछेर्यस्माद्यच्छ्रेयस्तच्च मे वद //
379.m: "I had set out to ask the sage Kapila about what is highest good, O brāhmaṇa; / you are a portion of that sage Kapila, granting knowledge on earth for my sake. / Since you have caused a wave of knowledge to rise, tell me what is the highest good."

379.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
bhūyaḥ pṛcchasi kiṃ śreyaḥ paramārthanna pṛcchasi /
śreyāṃsyaparamārthāni aśeṣāṇyeva bhūpate //
379.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
भूयः पृच्छसि किं श्रेयः परमार्थन्न पृच्छसि /
श्रेयांस्यपरमार्थानि अशेषाण्येव भूपते //
379.m:
The brāhmaṇa said:
"Why do you ask again about the good? Why do you not ask about the ultimate reality? / All goods other than the ultimate reality are entirely provisional, O lord of the earth.

379.s:
devatārādhanaṃ kṛtvā dhanasampattimicchati /
putrānicchati rājyañca śreyastasyaiva kiṃ nṛpa //
379.d:
देवताराधनं कृत्वा धनसम्पत्तिमिच्छति /
पुत्रानिच्छति राज्यञ्च श्रेयस्तस्यैव किं नृप //
379.m: Having performed the worship of deities, one desires abundant wealth; / one desires sons and kingship; is that indeed the highest good for him, O king?

379.s:
vivekinastu saṃyogaḥ śreyo yaḥ paramātmanaḥ /
:p 342
yajñādikā kriyā na syāt nāsti dravyopapattitā //
379.d:
विवेकिनस्तु संयोगः श्रेयो यः परमात्मनः /
:प् 342
यज्ञादिका क्रिया न स्यात् नास्ति द्रव्योपपत्तिता //
379.m:
For the discerning person, however, the highest good is union with the supreme self.
[p. 342]
There would be no rituals such as sacrifice, nor any possibility of material offerings.

379.s:
paramārthātmanoryogaḥ paramārtha itīṣyate /
eko vyāpī samaḥ śuddho nirguṇaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ //
379.d:
परमार्थात्मनोर्योगः परमार्थ इतीष्यते /
एको व्यापी समः शुद्धो निर्गुणः प्रकृतेः परः //
379.m: The union of the ultimate truth and the self is called the ultimate reality: / one, all-pervading, equal, pure, devoid of qualities, beyond primordial matter,

379.s:
janmavṛddhyādirahita ātmā sarvagato 'vyayaḥ /
paraṃ jñānamayo 'saṅgī guṇajātyādibhirvibhuḥ //
379.d:
जन्मवृद्ध्यादिरहित आत्मा सर्वगतो ऽव्ययः /
परं ज्ञानमयो ऽसङ्गी गुणजात्यादिभिर्विभुः //
379.m: free from birth, growth, and the like, the self is omnipresent and imperishable, / supreme, consisting of knowledge, unattached, all-pervasive, beyond qualities, classes, and the rest.

379.s:
nidādhaṛtusaṃvādaṃ vadāmi dvija taṃ śṛṇu(1) /
ṛturbrahmasuto jñānī tacchiṣyo 'bhūt pulastyajaḥ //
379.d:
निदाधऋतुसंवादं वदामि द्विज तं शृणु(1) /
ऋतुर्ब्रह्मसुतो ज्ञानी तच्छिष्यो ऽभूत् पुलस्त्यजः //
379.m: I shall relate the dialogue of Nidāgha and Ṛtu; listen to it, O brāhmaṇa. / Ṛtu was a wise son of Brahmā, and the son of Pulastya became his disciple.

379.s:
nidāghaḥ prāptavidyo 'smānnagare vai pure sthitaḥ /
devikāyāstaṭe tañca tarkayāmāsa vai ṛtuḥ //
379.d:
निदाघः प्राप्तविद्यो ऽस्मान्नगरे वै पुरे स्थितः /
देविकायास्तटे तञ्च तर्कयामास वै ऋतुः //
379.m: Having acquired knowledge from him, Nidāgha dwelt in a city, / on the bank of the Devikā; and Ṛtu pondered over him.

379.s:
divye varṣasahasre 'gānnidāghamavalokituṃ /
nidāgho vaiśvadevānte bhuktvānnaṃ śiṣyamabravīt /
bhuktante tṛptirutpannā tuṣṭidā sākṣayā yataḥ //
379.d:
दिव्ये वर्षसहस्रे ऽगान्निदाघमवलोकितुं /
निदाघो वैश्वदेवान्ते भुक्त्वान्नं शिष्यमब्रवीत् /
भुक्तन्ते तृप्तिरुत्पन्ना तुष्टिदा साक्षया यतः //
379.m: After a divine thousand years, he went to see Nidāgha. / At the conclusion of the Vaiśvadeva rite, Nidāgha, having eaten food, said to the disciple: / 'Has satiety arisen in you after eating, which grants satisfaction, since it is imperishable?'

379.s:
ṛtur uvāca
kṣudasti yasya bhute 'nne tuṣṭirbrāhmaṇa jāyate /
na me kṣudabhavattṛptiṃ kasmāttvaṃ paripṛcchasi //
379.d:
ऋतुर् उवाच
क्षुदस्ति यस्य भुते ऽन्ने तुष्टिर्ब्राह्मण जायते /
न मे क्षुदभवत्तृप्तिं कस्मात्त्वं परिपृच्छसि //
379.m:
Ṛtu said:
'Satisfaction arises, O brāhmaṇa, for one who has hunger when food has been eaten; / I had no hunger—why do you ask about my satiety?

379.s:
kṣuttṛṣṇe dehadharmākhye na mamaite yato dvija /
pṛṣṭohaṃ yattvayā brūyāṃ(2) tṛptirastye va me sadā //
379.d:
क्षुत्तृष्णे देहधर्माख्ये न ममैते यतो द्विज /
पृष्टोहं यत्त्वया ब्रूयां(2) तृप्तिरस्त्ये व मे सदा //
379.m: Hunger and thirst are called attributes of the body; they do not belong to me, O brāhmaṇa. / Since you asked me, I say: satiety is ever mine indeed.

379.s:
pumān sarvagato vyāpī ākāśavadayaṃ yataḥ /
ato 'haṃ pratyagātmāsmītyetadarthe bhavet kathaṃ(3) //
379.d:
पुमान् सर्वगतो व्यापी आकाशवदयं यतः /
अतो ऽहं प्रत्यगात्मास्मीत्येतदर्थे भवेत् कथं(3) //
379.m: Because this person is omnipresent and all-pervading like space, / how could there be any sense in saying, 'Therefore I am the inner self'?

379.s:
so 'haṃ gantā(4) na cāgantā naikadeśaniketanaḥ /
tvaṃ cānyo na bhavennāpi nānyastvatto 'smi vā pyahaṃ //
:n
1 nidāghaṛtusaṃvādamadvaitabuddhaye śṛṇviti kha.. , ña.. ca
2 tataḥ kṣutsambhavābhāvāditi kha.. , ña.. ca
3 kutaḥ kutra kva gantāsītyetadapyarthavat kathamiti kha.. , ña.. ca
4 bhokteti ka..
:p 343
379.d:
सो ऽहं गन्ता(4) न चागन्ता नैकदेशनिकेतनः /
त्वं चान्यो न भवेन्नापि नान्यस्त्वत्तो ऽस्मि वा प्यहं //
:न्
1 निदाघऋतुसंवादमद्वैतबुद्धये शृण्विति ख.. , ञ.. च
2 ततः क्षुत्सम्भवाभावादिति ख.. , ञ.. च
3 कुतः कुत्र क्व गन्तासीत्येतदप्यर्थवत् कथमिति ख.. , ञ.. च
4 भोक्तेति क..
:प् 343
379.m:
Such as I am, I neither go nor come, nor do I have a dwelling in any single place; / you are not another, nor am I another distinct from you.
[Notes]
1. Manuscripts kha and ña read: 'Listen to the dialogue of Nidāgha and Ṛtu for the sake of the understanding of non-duality.'
2. Manuscripts kha and ña read: 'Therefore, because of the absence of hunger...'
3. Manuscripts kha and ña read: 'Whence, whither, and where are you going?—how could this too be meaningful?'
4. Manuscript ka reads: 'the experiencer'. / [p. 343]

379.s:
mṛṇmayaṃ hi gṛhaṃ yadvanmṛdāliptaṃ sthirībhavet /
pārthivo 'yaṃ tathā dehaḥ pārthivaiḥ paramāṇubhiḥ //
379.d:
मृण्मयं हि गृहं यद्वन्मृदालिप्तं स्थिरीभवेत् /
पार्थिवो ऽयं तथा देहः पार्थिवैः परमाणुभिः //
379.m: Just as an earthen house becomes firm when smeared with clay, / so too this earthly body [is sustained] by earthy atoms.

379.s:
ṛturasmi tavācāryaḥ prajñādānāya te dvija /
ihāgato 'haṃ yāsyāmi paramārthastavoditaḥ //
379.d:
ऋतुरस्मि तवाचार्यः प्रज्ञादानाय ते द्विज /
इहागतो ऽहं यास्यामि परमार्थस्तवोदितः //
379.m: I am Ṛtu, your teacher, who have come here to impart wisdom to you, O brāhmaṇa; / now I shall depart. The ultimate reality has been declared to you.

379.s:
ekamevamidaṃ viddhi na bhedaḥ sakalaṃ jagat /
vāsudevābhidheyasya svarūpaṃ paramātmanaḥ //
379.d:
एकमेवमिदं विद्धि न भेदः सकलं जगत् /
वासुदेवाभिधेयस्य स्वरूपं परमात्मनः //
379.m: Know this entire universe to be one in this way; there is no division; / it is the essential nature of the supreme self known by the name of Vāsudeva.'

379.s:
ṛturvarṣasahasrānte punastannagaraṃ yayau /
nidāghaṃ nagaraprānte ekānte sthitamabravīt /
ekānte sthīyate kasmānnidāghaṃ ṛturabravīt //
379.d:
ऋतुर्वर्षसहस्रान्ते पुनस्तन्नगरं ययौ /
निदाघं नगरप्रान्ते एकान्ते स्थितमब्रवीत् /
एकान्ते स्थीयते कस्मान्निदाघं ऋतुरब्रवीत् //
379.m: At the end of a thousand years, Ṛtu went again to that city. / He spoke to Nidāgha, who was standing in a solitary place at the edge of the city: / 'Why are you staying in a solitary place?' Ṛtu asked Nidāgha.

379.s:
nidāgha uvāca
bho vipra janasaṃvādo mahāneṣa nareśvara /
pravivīkṣya puraṃ ramyaṃ tenātra sthīyate mayā //
379.d:
निदाघ उवाच
भो विप्र जनसंवादो महानेष नरेश्वर /
प्रविवीक्ष्य पुरं रम्यं तेनात्र स्थीयते मया //
379.m:
Nidāgha said:
'O brāhmaṇa, there is a great crowd of people [as] the king / wishes to enter this lovely city; therefore I am standing here.'

379.s:
ṛtur uvāca
narādhipo 'tra katamaḥ katamaścetaro janaḥ /
kathyatāṃ me dvijaśreṣṭha tvamabhijño dvijottama //
379.d:
ऋतुर् उवाच
नराधिपो ऽत्र कतमः कतमश्चेतरो जनः /
कथ्यतां मे द्विजश्रेष्ठ त्वमभिज्ञो द्विजोत्तम //
379.m:
Ṛtu said:
'Which one here is the king, and which is the other people? / Tell me, O best of the twice-born, for you are knowledgeable, O foremost brāhmaṇa.'

379.s:
yo 'yaṃ gajendramunmattamadriśṛṅgasamutthitaṃ /
adhirūḍho narendro 'yaṃ parivārastathetaraḥ(1) //
379.d:
यो ऽयं गजेन्द्रमुन्मत्तमद्रिशृङ्गसमुत्थितं /
अधिरूढो नरेन्द्रो ऽयं परिवारस्तथेतरः(1) //
379.m: 'This one who has mounted the lordly elephant in rut, which rises like a mountain peak, / is the king; the other is his retinue.'

379.s:
gajo yo 'yamadho brahmannuparyeṣa sa bhūpatiḥ /
ṛturāha gajaḥ ko 'tra rājā cāha nidāghakaḥ //
379.d:
गजो यो ऽयमधो ब्रह्मन्नुपर्येष स भूपतिः /
ऋतुराह गजः को ऽत्र राजा चाह निदाघकः //
379.m: 'The elephant is below, O brāhmaṇa, and above is the king.' / Ṛtu said, 'Which here is the elephant, and [which] the king?' And Nidāgha said:

379.s:
ṛturnidāgha ārūḍho dṛṣṭāntaṃ paśya vāhanaṃ /
uparyahaṃ yathā rājā tvamadhaḥ kuñjaro yathā //
379.d:
ऋतुर्निदाघ आरूढो दृष्टान्तं पश्य वाहनं /
उपर्यहं यथा राजा त्वमधः कुञ्जरो यथा //
379.m: Ṛtu mounted Nidāgha [and said]: 'Behold the illustration of the mount: / I am above like the king, and you are below like the elephant.'

379.s:
ṛtuḥ(2) prāha nidāghantaṃ katamastvāmahaṃ vade /
ukto nidāghastannatvā prāha me tvaṃ gururdhruvam //
:n
1 ārūḍho 'yaṃ gajaṃ rājā paralokastathetara iti kha.. , ña.. ca
2 ka.. pustake sarvatra ṛbhuriti ṛtusthānīyaḥ pāṭhaḥ
:p 344
379.d:
ऋतुः(2) प्राह निदाघन्तं कतमस्त्वामहं वदे /
उक्तो निदाघस्तन्नत्वा प्राह मे त्वं गुरुर्ध्रुवम् //
:न्
1 आरूढो ऽयं गजं राजा परलोकस्तथेतर इति ख.. , ञ.. च
2 क.. पुस्तके सर्वत्र ऋभुरिति ऋतुस्थानीयः पाठः
:प् 344
379.m:
Ṛtu said to Nidāgha: 'Tell me, which one is you and which am I?' / Having been addressed thus, Nidāgha bowed to him and said: 'You are surely my guru!
[Notes]
1. Manuscripts kha and ña read: 'The king is mounted on this elephant, and the other people are the rest.'
2. In manuscript ka, the reading throughout is Ṛbhu in place of Ṛtu. / [p. 344]

379.s:
nānyasmāddvaitasaṃskārasaṃskṛtaṃ mānasaṃ tathā /
ṛtuḥ prāha nidāghantaṃ brahmajñānāya cāgataḥ /
paramārthaṃ sārabhūtamadvaitaṃ darśitaṃ mayā //
379.d:
नान्यस्माद्द्वैतसंस्कारसंस्कृतं मानसं तथा /
ऋतुः प्राह निदाघन्तं ब्रह्मज्ञानाय चागतः /
परमार्थं सारभूतमद्वैतं दर्शितं मया //
379.m: No one else could have so refined my mind with the impression of non-duality.' / Ṛtu said to Nidāgha: 'I came for the sake of the knowledge of Brahman; / non-duality, the essence of the ultimate reality, has been shown by me.'

379.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
nidāgho 'pyupadeśena tenādvaitaparo 'bhavat /
sarvabhūtānyabhedena dadṛśe sa tadātmani //
379.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
निदाघो ऽप्युपदेशेन तेनाद्वैतपरो ऽभवत् /
सर्वभूतान्यभेदेन ददृशे स तदात्मनि //
379.m:
The brāhmaṇa said:
Through that instruction Nidāgha too became devoted to non-duality; / he then saw all beings without distinction within his own self.

379.s:
avāpa muktiṃ jñānātsa tathā tvaṃ muktimāpsyasi /
ekaḥ samastaṃ tvañcāhaṃ viṣṇuḥ sarvagato yataḥ //
379.d:
अवाप मुक्तिं ज्ञानात्स तथा त्वं मुक्तिमाप्स्यसि /
एकः समस्तं त्वञ्चाहं विष्णुः सर्वगतो यतः //
379.m: He attained liberation through knowledge; likewise you shall attain liberation, / for the One is everything: you and I, since Viṣṇu is all-pervading.

379.s:
pītanīlādibhedena yathaikaṃ dṛśyate nabhaḥ /
bhrāntidṛṣṭibhirātmāpi tathaikaḥ sa pṛthak pṛthak //
379.d:
पीतनीलादिभेदेन यथैकं दृश्यते नभः /
भ्रान्तिदृष्टिभिरात्मापि तथैकः स पृथक् पृथक् //
379.m: Just as the single sky appears differentiated by yellow, blue, and other [colors], / so too is the single self [perceived as] distinct through deluded perceptions.

379.s:
agnir uvāca
muktiṃ hy avāpa bhavato jñānasāreṇa bhūpatiḥ(1) /
saṃsārājñānavṛkṣārijñānaṃ brahmeti cintaya //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe advaitavrahmavijñānaṃ
namonāśītyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athāśītyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
gītāsāraḥ
379.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
मुक्तिं ह्य् अवाप भवतो ज्ञानसारेण भूपतिः(1) /
संसाराज्ञानवृक्षारिज्ञानं ब्रह्मेति चिन्तय //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अद्वैतव्रह्मविज्ञानं
नमोनाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
गीतासारः
379.m:
Agni said: / The king indeed attained liberation through the essence of knowledge from you. / Meditate on knowledge—the enemy of the tree of worldly ignorance—as Brahman.
Thus, in the great Agni Purāṇa, the knowledge of non-dual Brahman, the three hundred and seventy-ninth chapter.
Now the three hundred and eightieth chapter.
The Essence of the Gītā

380.s:
agnir uvāca
gītāsāraṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvagītottamottamaṃ /
kṛṣṇo 'rjunāya yamāha purā vai bhuktimuktidaṃ(2) //
380.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
गीतासारं प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वगीतोत्तमोत्तमं /
कृष्णो ऽर्जुनाय यमाह पुरा वै भुक्तिमुक्तिदं(2) //
380.m: Agni said: / I shall declare the essence of the Gītā, highest of all songs, / which Kṛṣṇa anciently spoke to Arjuna, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation.

380.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
gatāsuragatāsurvā na śocyo dehavānajaḥ /
ātmājaro 'maro 'bhedyastasmācchokādikaṃ tyajet //
:n
1 jñānāt sauvīrabhūpatiriti kha.. , ña.. ca
2 paṭhatāṃ bhuktimuktidamiti kha..
:p 345
380.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
गतासुरगतासुर्वा न शोच्यो देहवानजः /
आत्माजरो ऽमरो ऽभेद्यस्तस्माच्छोकादिकं त्यजेत् //
:न्
1 ज्ञानात् सौवीरभूपतिरिति ख.. , ञ.. च
2 पठतां भुक्तिमुक्तिदमिति ख..
:प् 345
380.m:
The Blessed Lord said: / Whether life is gone or not gone, the unborn embodied soul is not to be grieved for. / The self is ageless, immortal, indivisible; therefore, one should abandon grief and the like.
[...]
1. "Through knowledge, the king of the Sauvīras," thus in manuscripts kha and ña.
2. "Granting worldly enjoyment and liberation to those who recite," thus in manuscript kha. / [p. 345]

380.s:
dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate /
saṅgāt kāmastataḥ krodhaḥ krodhātsammoha eva ca //
380.d:
ध्यायतो विषयान् पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते /
सङ्गात् कामस्ततः क्रोधः क्रोधात्सम्मोह एव च //
380.m: For a man meditating on sense-objects, attachment to them is born; / from attachment arises desire, from that anger, and from anger delusion indeed.

380.s:
ammohāt smṛtivibhraṃśo buddhināśāt praṇaśyati /
duḥsaṅgahāniḥ satsaṅgānmokṣakābhī ca kāmanut //
380.d:
अम्मोहात् स्मृतिविभ्रंशो बुद्धिनाशात् प्रणश्यति /
दुःसङ्गहानिः सत्सङ्गान्मोक्षकाभी च कामनुत् //
380.m: From delusion comes loss of memory; from destruction of intellect he perishes. / Abandonment of bad company comes from good company, [and thus] desiring liberation and casting off desire,

380.s:
kāmatyāgādātmaniṣṭhaḥ sthiraprajñastadocyate /
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī //
380.d:
कामत्यागादात्मनिष्ठः स्थिरप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते /
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी //
380.m: steadfast in the self through relinquishing desire, he is then called one of steady wisdom. / That which is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled man keeps awake.

380.s:
yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ /
ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate //
380.d:
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः /
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते //
380.m: That in which beings keep awake is night for the seeing sage. / And satisfied in the self alone, for him there is no duty to be done.

380.s:
naiva tasya kṛte nārtho nākṛte neha kaś canaḥ /
tattvavittu mahāvaho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ //
380.d:
नैव तस्य कृते नार्थो नाकृते नेह कश् चनः /
तत्त्ववित्तु महावहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः //
380.m: For him there is no purpose at all in what is done here, nor in what is not done. / But the knower of truth, O mighty-armed one, regarding the divisions of gunas and actions,

380.s:
guṇā guneṣu vartante iti matvā na sajjate /
sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ santariṣyati //
380.d:
गुणा गुनेषु वर्तन्ते इति मत्वा न सज्जते /
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यति //
380.m: thinking, "The gunas operate among the gunas," is not attached. / He will cross over all sin solely by the boat of knowledge.

380.s:
jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute 'rjuna /
brahmaṇyādhāya karmāṇi saṅgantyaktvā karoti yaḥ //
380.d:
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात् कुरुते ऽर्जुन /
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गन्त्यक्त्वा करोति यः //
380.m: The fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes, O Arjuna. / Dedicating actions to Brahman, he who acts having abandoned attachment

380.s:
lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatramivāmbhasā /
sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani //
380.d:
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा /
सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि //
380.m: is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not [tainted] by water. / Seeing the self in all beings and all beings in the self,

380.s:
īkṣate yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ /
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo 'bhijāyate //
380.d:
ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः /
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टो ऽभिजायते //
380.m: the one whose self is disciplined in yoga sees with equal vision everywhere. / One fallen from yoga is born in the house of the pure and prosperous.

380.s:
na hi kalyāṇakṛt kaściddurgatiṃ tāta gacchati /
devī hy eṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā //
380.d:
न हि कल्याणकृत् कश्चिद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति /
देवी ह्य् एषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया //
380.m: For no one who does good goes to a bad state, my dear friend. / For this divine māyā of mine, composed of the gunas, is hard to overcome.

380.s:
māmeva ye prapadyante māyāmetāntaranti te /
ārto jijñāsurarthārtho jñānī ca bharatarṣabha //
380.d:
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतान्तरन्ति ते /
आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थो ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ //
380.m: Those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond this māyā. / The afflicted, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the man of knowledge, O best of the Bharatas—

380.s:
caturvidhā bhajante māṃ jñānī caikatvamāsthitaḥ /
:p 346
akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo 'dhyātmamucyate //
380.d:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां ज्ञानी चैकत्वमास्थितः /
:प् 346
अक्षरं ब्रह्म परमं स्वभावो ऽध्यात्ममुच्यते //
380.m:
fourfold are they who worship me; and the man of knowledge is established in oneness.
[p. 346]
The supreme imperishable is Brahman; essential nature is called the higher self.

380.s:
bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṃjñitaḥ /
adhibhūtaṃ kṣarobhāvaḥ puruṣaścādhidaivataṃ //
380.d:
भूतभावोद्भवकरो विसर्गः कर्मसंज्ञितः /
अधिभूतं क्षरोभावः पुरुषश्चाधिदैवतं //
380.m: The emission that brings about the origin of the existence of beings is known as action. / The perishable existence is the material realm, and the cosmic Person is the realm of the deities.

380.s:
adhiyajñohamevātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃ vara /
antakāle smaranmāñca madbhāvaṃ yātyasaṃśayaḥ //
380.d:
अधियज्ञोहमेवात्र देहे देहभृतां वर /
अन्तकाले स्मरन्माञ्च मद्भावं यात्यसंशयः //
380.m: I alone am the realm of sacrifice here in this body, O best of embodied beings. / And at the time of death, remembering me, he attains my state beyond doubt.

380.s:
yaṃ yaṃ bhāvaṃ smarannante tyajeddehantamāpnuyāt /
prāṇaṃ nyasya bhruvormadhye ante prāpnoti matparam //
380.d:
यं यं भावं स्मरन्नन्ते त्यजेद्देहन्तमाप्नुयात् /
प्राणं न्यस्य भ्रुवोर्मध्ये अन्ते प्राप्नोति मत्परम् //
380.m: Remembering whatever state of being at the end he leaves the body, to that he goes. / Placing the vital breath between the eyebrows at the end, he attains my supreme [state].

380.s:
omityekākṣaraṃ brahmavadan dehaṃ tyajantathā /
brahmādistambhaparyantāḥ sarve mama vibhūtayaḥ //
380.d:
ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्मवदन् देहं त्यजन्तथा /
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्भपर्यन्ताः सर्वे मम विभूतयः //
380.m: Pronouncing the single syllable OṂ, which is Brahman, thus casting off the body. / From Brahmā down to a blade of grass, all are my manifestations.

380.s:
śrīmantaścorjitāḥ sarve mamāṃśāḥ(1) prāṇinaḥsmṛtāḥ /
ahameko viśvarūpa iti jñātvā vimucyate //
380.d:
श्रीमन्तश्चोर्जिताः सर्वे ममांशाः(1) प्राणिनःस्मृताः /
अहमेको विश्वरूप इति ज्ञात्वा विमुच्यते //
380.m: All living beings that are prosperous and powerful are considered portions of me. / Knowing, "I alone am the universal form," one is liberated.

380.s:
kṣetraṃ śarīraṃ yo vetti kṣetrajñaḥ sa prakortitaḥ /
kṣetrakṣetrajñayorjñānaṃ yattajjñānaṃ mataṃ mama //
380.d:
क्षेत्रं शरीरं यो वेत्ति क्षेत्रज्ञः स प्रकोर्तितः /
क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्ज्ञानं यत्तज्ज्ञानं मतं मम //
380.m: He who knows the body as the field is declared to be the knower of the field. / The knowledge of the field and the knower of the field, that is considered knowledge by me.

380.s:
mahābhūtānyahaṅkāro buddhiravyaktameva ca /
indrayāṇi deśaikañca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ //
380.d:
महाभूतान्यहङ्कारो बुद्धिरव्यक्तमेव च /
इन्द्रयाणि देशैकञ्च पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः //
380.m: The great elements, ego-sense, intellect, and the unmanifest; / the eleven sense faculties, and the five objects of the senses;

380.s:
icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṅghātaścetanā dhṛtiḥ /
etatkṣetraṃ samāsena savikāramudāhṛtaṃ //
380.d:
इच्छा द्वेषः सुखं दुःखं सङ्घातश्चेतना धृतिः /
एतत्क्षेत्रं समासेन सविकारमुदाहृतं //
380.m: desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, consciousness, steadfastness: / this in brief is declared to be the field with its modifications.

380.s:
amānitvamadambhitvamahiṃsā kṣāntirārjavam /
ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyamātmavinigrahaḥ //
380.d:
अमानित्वमदम्भित्वमहिंसा क्षान्तिरार्जवम् /
आचार्योपासनं शौचं स्थैर्यमात्मविनिग्रहः //
380.m: Humility, unpretentiousness, non-violence, forbearance, uprightness, / attendance on the teacher, ritual purity, steadfastness, self-restraint,

380.s:
indriyārtheṣu vairāgyamanahaṅkāra eva ca /
janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanaṃ //
380.d:
इन्द्रियार्थेषु वैराग्यमनहङ्कार एव च /
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखदोषानुदर्शनं //
380.m: dispassion toward sense-objects, and also absence of egoism, / contemplation of the evils of birth, death, old age, disease, and suffering,

380.s:
āsaktiranabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu /
:n
1 mamāṅgā iti kha..
:p 347
nityañca samacittattvamiṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu //
380.d:
आसक्तिरनभिष्वङ्गः पुत्रदारगृहादिषु /
:न्
1 ममाङ्गा इति ख..
:प् 347
नित्यञ्च समचित्तत्त्वमिष्टानिष्टोपपत्तिषु //
380.m:
non-clinging, absence of passionate attachment toward sons, wife, home, and the like,
[...]
1. "My limbs," thus in manuscript kha. / [p. 347]
and constant even-mindedness in desired and undesired occurrences,

380.s:
mayi cānanyayogena bhaktiravyabhicāriṇī /
viviktadeśasevitvamaratirjanasaṃsadi //
380.d:
मयि चानन्ययोगेन भक्तिरव्यभिचारिणी /
विविक्तदेशसेवित्वमरतिर्जनसंसदि //
380.m: and unswerving devotion to me through disciplined focus on no other, / resort to solitary places, distaste for crowds of people,

380.s:
adhyātmajñānaniṣṭhatvantattvajñānānudarśanaṃ /
etajjñānamiti proktamajñānaṃ yadato 'nyathā //
380.d:
अध्यात्मज्ञाननिष्ठत्वन्तत्त्वज्ञानानुदर्शनं /
एतज्ज्ञानमिति प्रोक्तमज्ञानं यदतो ऽन्यथा //
380.m: steadfastness in knowledge of the supreme self, perception of the aim of knowledge of reality: / this is declared to be knowledge; that which is contrary to it is ignorance.

380.s:
jñeyaṃ yattat pravakṣyāmi yaṃ jñātvāmṛtamaśnute /
anādi paramaṃ brahma sattvaṃ nāma taducyate //
380.d:
ज्ञेयं यत्तत् प्रवक्ष्यामि यं ज्ञात्वामृतमश्नुते /
अनादि परमं ब्रह्म सत्त्वं नाम तदुच्यते //
380.m: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: / the beginningless supreme Brahman; it is called neither being nor non-being.

380.s:
sarvataḥ pāṇipādāntaṃ sarvato 'kṣiśiromukham /
sarvataḥ śrutimalloke sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati //
380.d:
सर्वतः पाणिपादान्तं सर्वतो ऽक्षिशिरोमुखम् /
सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति //
380.m: With hands and feet on all sides, with eyes, heads, and faces on all sides, / with ears on all sides in the world, it stands encompassing all.

380.s:
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam /
asaktaṃ sarvabhṛccaiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca //
380.d:
सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् /
असक्तं सर्वभृच्चैव निर्गुणं गुणभोक्तृ च //
380.m: Shining with the virtues of all the senses, yet devoid of all the senses; / unattached, yet supporting all; free of the gunas, yet experiencing the gunas;

380.s:
vahirantaś ca bhūtānāmacarañcarameva ca /
sūkṣmatvāttadavijñeyaṃ dūrasthañcāntike 'pi yat //
380.d:
वहिरन्तश् च भूतानामचरञ्चरमेव च /
सूक्ष्मत्वात्तदविज्ञेयं दूरस्थञ्चान्तिके ऽपि यत् //
380.m: outside and inside beings, moving and unmoving; / incomprehensible because of its subtlety; both far away and near;

380.s:
avibhaktañca bhūteṣu vibhaktamiva ca sthitam /
bhūtabhartṛ ca vijñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca //
380.d:
अविभक्तञ्च भूतेषु विभक्तमिव च स्थितम् /
भूतभर्तृ च विज्ञेयं ग्रसिष्णु प्रभविष्णु च //
380.m: undivided among beings, yet standing as if divided; / it should be known as the sustainer of beings, devouring them and generating them.

380.s:
jyotiṣāmapi tajjyotistamasaḥ paramucyate /
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya dhiṣṭhitaṃ //
380.d:
ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते /
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं ज्ञानगम्यं हृदि सर्वस्य धिष्ठितं //
380.m: The light even of lights, it is said to be beyond darkness; / knowledge, the object of knowledge, attainable by knowledge, seated in the heart of all.

380.s:
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecidātmānamātmanā /
anye sāṅkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare //
380.d:
ध्यानेनात्मनि पश्यन्ति केचिदात्मानमात्मना /
अन्ये साङ्ख्येन योगेन कर्मयोगेन चापरे //
380.m: By meditation, some see the self in the self by the self; / others by the yoga of knowledge, and others by the yoga of action.

380.s:
anye tvevamajānanto śrutvānyebhya upāsate /
tepi cāśu tarantyeva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ //
380.d:
अन्ये त्वेवमजानन्तो श्रुत्वान्येभ्य उपासते /
तेपि चाशु तरन्त्येव मृत्युं श्रुतिपरायणाः //
380.m: Others, not knowing thus, worship having heard from others; / they too, devoted to hearing, certainly cross beyond death quickly.

380.s:
sattvātsañjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca /
pramādamohau tamaso bhavato jñānameva ca //
:p 348
380.d:
सत्त्वात्सञ्जायते ज्ञानं रजसो लोभ एव च /
प्रमादमोहौ तमसो भवतो ज्ञानमेव च //
:प् 348
380.m:
From sattva arises knowledge, and from rajas greed; / negligence and delusion arise from tamas, as does ignorance.
[p. 348]

380.s:
guṇā vartanta ity eva yo 'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate /
mānāvamānamitrāritulyastyāgī sa nirguṇaḥ //
380.d:
गुणा वर्तन्त इत्य् एव यो ऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते /
मानावमानमित्रारितुल्यस्त्यागी स निर्गुणः //
380.m: He who stands firm, thinking only, "The gunas operate," and is not shaken, / equal in honor and dishonor, to friend and foe, renouncing [all undertakings]—he is beyond the gunas.

380.s:
ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayaṃ /
chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit //
380.d:
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययं /
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् //
380.m: They speak of the imperishable Aśvattha tree with its roots above and branches below, / whose leaves are the Vedic hymns; he who knows it is a knower of the Veda.

380.s:
dvau bhūtasargau loke 'smin daiva āsura eva ca /
ahiṃsādiḥ kṣamā caiva daivīsampattito nṛṇāṃ //
380.d:
द्वौ भूतसर्गौ लोके ऽस्मिन् दैव आसुर एव च /
अहिंसादिः क्षमा चैव दैवीसम्पत्तितो नृणां //
380.m: There are two orders of beings in this world: the divine and the demonic. / Non-violence and the like, and forbearance, belong to men of divine endowment.

380.s:
na śaucaṃ nāpi vācāro hy āsurīsampadoddhavaḥ /
narakatvāt krodhalobhakāmastasmāttrayaṃ tyajet //
380.d:
न शौचं नापि वाचारो ह्य् आसुरीसम्पदोद्धवः /
नरकत्वात् क्रोधलोभकामस्तस्मात्त्रयं त्यजेत् //
380.m: Neither ritual purity nor conduct arises from demonic endowment. / Because they lead to hell, one should abandon the triad of anger, greed, and desire.

380.s:
yajñastapas tathā dānaṃ sattvādyaistrividhaṃ smṛtam /
āyuḥ sattvaṃ balārogyasukhāyānnantu sāttvikaṃ //
380.d:
यज्ञस्तपस् तथा दानं सत्त्वाद्यैस्त्रिविधं स्मृतम् /
आयुः सत्त्वं बलारोग्यसुखायान्नन्तु सात्त्विकं //
380.m: Sacrifice, ascetic austerity, and gift are considered threefold according to sattva and the rest. / Food that promotes longevity, mental strength, physical strength, health, and happiness is sāttvika.

380.s:
duḥkhaśokāmayāyānnaṃ tīkṣṇarūkṣantu rājasaṃ /
amedhyocchiṣṭapūtyannaṃ tāmasaṃ nīrasādikaṃ //
380.d:
दुःखशोकामयायान्नं तीक्ष्णरूक्षन्तु राजसं /
अमेध्योच्छिष्टपूत्यन्नं तामसं नीरसादिकं //
380.m: Food that brings suffering, sorrow, and disease, being pungent and dry, is rājasika. / Food that is impure, remnant, foul-smelling, and tasteless is tāmasika.

380.s:
yaṣṭavyo vidhinā yajño niṣkāmāya sa sāttvikaḥ /
yajñaḥ phalāya dambhātmī rājasastāmasaḥ kratuḥ //
380.d:
यष्टव्यो विधिना यज्ञो निष्कामाय स सात्त्विकः /
यज्ञः फलाय दम्भात्मी राजसस्तामसः क्रतुः //
380.m: Sacrifice performed according to rule without desire is sāttvika; / a sacrifice [offered] for reward or out of ostentation is rājasika; [that devoid of faith and rules] is a tāmasika rite.

380.s:
śraddhāmantrādividhyuktaṃ tapaḥ śārīramucyate /
devādipūjāhiṃsādi vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate //
380.d:
श्रद्धामन्त्रादिविध्युक्तं तपः शारीरमुच्यते /
देवादिपूजाहिंसादि वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते //
380.m: Ascetic austerity prescribed by faith, mantras, and the like, [such as] worship of gods and non-violence, is called bodily; / ascetic austerity consisting of speech is said [to be]:

380.s:
anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ svādhyāyasajjapaḥ /
mānasaṃ cittasaṃśuddhersaunamātsavinigrahaḥ //
380.d:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं स्वाध्यायसज्जपः /
मानसं चित्तसंशुद्धेर्सौनमात्सविनिग्रहः //
380.m: words causing no agitation, truth, study of the Veda, and good recitation; / mental [austerity is that] of mental purity, silence, and self-restraint.

380.s:
sāttvikañca tapo 'kāmaṃ phalādyarthantu rājasaṃ /
tāmasaṃ parapīḍāyai sāttvikaṃ dānamucyate //
380.d:
सात्त्विकञ्च तपो ऽकामं फलाद्यर्थन्तु राजसं /
तामसं परपीडायै सात्त्विकं दानमुच्यते //
380.m: Ascetic austerity without desire is sāttvika, but that for the sake of fruit and the like is rājasika; / that for hurting others is tāmasika. Sāttvika gift is spoken of [as follows]:

380.s:
deśādau caiva dātavyamupakārāya rājasaṃ /
ādeśādāvavajñātaṃ tāmasaṃ dānamīritaṃ //
:p 349
380.d:
देशादौ चैव दातव्यमुपकाराय राजसं /
आदेशादाववज्ञातं तामसं दानमीरितं //
:प् 349
380.m:
it must be given in an appropriate place and the like; that for return of a favor is rājasika; / a gift given in an improper place and the like, with contempt, is declared tāmasika.
[Page 349]

380.s:
oṃtatsaditi nirdeśo brahmaṇastrividhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
yajñadānādika karma buktimuktipradaṃ nṛṇāṃ //
380.d:
ओंतत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः /
यज्ञदानादिक कर्म बुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं नृणां //
380.m: “Oṃ Tat Sat”—this is remembered as the threefold designation of Brahman. / Action such as sacrifice and gifts grants worldly enjoyment and liberation to men.

380.s:
aniṣṭamiṣṭaṃ miśrañca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ /
bhavatyatyāgināṃ(1) pretya na tu sannyāsināṃ kvacit //
380.d:
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रञ्च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलं /
भवत्यत्यागिनां(1) प्रेत्य न तु सन्न्यासिनां क्वचित् //
380.m: The threefold fruit of action—undesirable, desirable, and mixed— / comes after death to those who have not renounced, but never to renunciants.

380.s:
tāmasaḥ karmasaṃyogāt mohātkleśabhayādikāt /
rājasaḥ sāttviko 'kāmāt pañcaite karmahetavaḥ //
380.d:
तामसः कर्मसंयोगात् मोहात्क्लेशभयादिकात् /
राजसः सात्त्विको ऽकामात् पञ्चैते कर्महेतवः //
380.m: [Renunciation is] tāmasika from connection to actions through delusion, suffering, fear, and the like; / rājasika [from pain], and sāttvika without desire. These five are the causes of action:

380.s:
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇañca pṛthagvidham /
trividhāś ca pṛthak ceṣṭā daivañcaivātra pañcamaṃ //
380.d:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणञ्च पृथग्विधम् /
त्रिविधाश् च पृथक् चेष्टा दैवञ्चैवात्र पञ्चमं //
380.m: the seat [of action], likewise the agent, the various organs of action, / the various distinct endeavors, and fate as the fifth here.

380.s:
ekaṃ jñānaṃ sāttvikaṃ syāt pṛthag jñānantu rājasaṃ /
atattvārthantāmasaṃ syāt karmākāmāya sāttvikaṃ //
380.d:
एकं ज्ञानं सात्त्विकं स्यात् पृथग् ज्ञानन्तु राजसं /
अतत्त्वार्थन्तामसं स्यात् कर्माकामाय सात्त्विकं //
380.m: Knowledge [seeing one reality] is sāttvika, but knowledge [seeing] distinction is rājasika; / that devoid of truth is tāmasika. Action without desire is sāttvika;

380.s:
kāmāya rājasaṃ karma mohāt karma tu tāmasaṃ /
sīdhyasiddhyoḥ samaḥ kartā sāttviko rājaso 'tyapi //
380.d:
कामाय राजसं कर्म मोहात् कर्म तु तामसं /
सीध्यसिद्ध्योः समः कर्ता सात्त्विको राजसो ऽत्यपि //
380.m: action for desire is rājasika, while action out of delusion is tāmasika. / The agent who is impartial in success and failure is sāttvika; [passionate] is rājasika;

380.s:
śaṭho 'lasastāmasaḥ syāt kāryādidhīś ca sāttvikī /
kāryārthaṃ sā rājasī syādviparītā tu tāmasī //
380.d:
शठो ऽलसस्तामसः स्यात् कार्यादिधीश् च सात्त्विकी /
कार्यार्थं सा राजसी स्याद्विपरीता तु तामसी //
380.m: crooked and lazy is tāmasika. The intellect discerning duty and non-duty is sāttvika; / that [interpreting duty] for self-interest is rājasika, while that inverted is tāmasika.

380.s:
manodhṛtiḥ sāttvikī syāt prītikāmeti rājasī /
tāmasī tu praśokādau mukhaṃ sattvāttadantagaṃ //
380.d:
मनोधृतिः सात्त्विकी स्यात् प्रीतिकामेति राजसी /
तामसी तु प्रशोकादौ मुखं सत्त्वात्तदन्तगं //
380.m: Resolve of the mind is sāttvika; that pursuing pleasure and desire is rājasika; / but that [persisting] in grief and the like is tāmasika. Happiness arising from sattva reaches its end [in bliss];

380.s:
sukhaṃ tadrājasañcāgre ante duḥkhantu tāmasaṃ /
ataḥ pravṛttirbhūtānāṃ yena sarvamidantataṃ //
380.d:
सुखं तद्राजसञ्चाग्रे अन्ते दुःखन्तु तामसं /
अतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदन्ततं //
380.m: that pleasure is rājasika [like nectar] at first, but tāmasika brings suffering at the end. / From him is the activity of beings, by whom all this is pervaded;

380.s:
svakarmaṇā tamabhyarcya viṣṇuṃ siddhiñca vindati /
karmaṇā manasā vācā sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā //
:n
1 bhavatyayogināmiti kha..
:p 350
380.d:
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य विष्णुं सिद्धिञ्च विन्दति /
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा //
:न्
1 भवत्ययोगिनामिति ख..
:प् 350
380.m:
by worshiping Viṣṇu through one's own duty, one attains perfection— / by action, mind, and speech in all states at all times.
[...]
[Variant: 'bhavatyayoginām' in manuscript kha.] / [Page 350]

380.s:
brahmādistambhaparyantaṃ jagadviṣṇuñca vetti yaḥ /
siddhimāpnoti bhagavadbhakto bhāgavato dhruvaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe gītāsāro nāmāśītyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikāśītyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yamagītā
380.d:
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्भपर्यन्तं जगद्विष्णुञ्च वेत्ति यः /
सिद्धिमाप्नोति भगवद्भक्तो भागवतो ध्रुवं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे गीतासारो नामाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
यमगीता
380.m:
He who knows the universe from Brahmā down to a tuft of grass as Viṣṇu, / devoted to the Lord, a devotee of the Bhagavat, surely attains perfection.
Thus ends the three hundred and eightieth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled “The Essence of the Gītā.”
Now the three hundred and eighty-first chapter.
The Song of Yama.

381.s:
agnir uvāca
yamagītāṃ pravakṣyāmi uktā yā nāciketase /
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ bhuktyai muktyai mokṣārthināṃ satāṃ //
381.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
यमगीतां प्रवक्ष्यामि उक्ता या नाचिकेतसे /
पठतां शृण्वतां भुक्त्यै मुक्त्यै मोक्षार्थिनां सतां //
381.m: Agni said: / I shall declare the Song of Yama, which was spoken to Naciketas, / for the worldly enjoyment and liberation of good people who read and listen, who seek liberation.

381.s:
yama uvāca
āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaparidhānagṛhādikam /
vāñchatyaho 'timohena susthiraṃ svayamasthiraḥ //
381.d:
यम उवाच
आसनं शयनं यानपरिधानगृहादिकम् /
वाञ्छत्यहो ऽतिमोहेन सुस्थिरं स्वयमस्थिरः //
381.m: Yama said: / Alas, through extreme delusion, [man], himself unstable, desires / a seat, bed, vehicle, garments, houses, and the like to be permanently stable.

381.s:
bhogeṣu śaktiḥ satataṃ tathaivātmāvalokanaṃ /
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyānāṃ kapilodgītameva hi //
381.d:
भोगेषु शक्तिः सततं तथैवात्मावलोकनं /
श्रेयः परं मनुष्यानां कपिलोद्गीतमेव हि //
381.m: Constant attachment to sense objects, and likewise the vision of the Self, / is the supreme good for men: thus indeed was sung by Kapila.

381.s:
sarvatra samadarśitvaṃ nirmasatvamasaṅgatā /
śreyaḥ param manuṣyānāṃ gītaṃ pañcaśikhena hi //
381.d:
सर्वत्र समदर्शित्वं निर्मसत्वमसङ्गता /
श्रेयः परम् मनुष्यानां गीतं पञ्चशिखेन हि //
381.m: Impartiality everywhere, freedom from egoism, detachment— / this is the supreme good for men: indeed it was sung by Pañcaśikha.

381.s:
āgarbhajanmabālyādivayo 'vasthādivedanaṃ /
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇām gaṅgāviṣṇupragītakaṃ //
381.d:
आगर्भजन्मबाल्यादिवयो ऽवस्थादिवेदनं /
श्रेयः परं मनुष्याणाम् गङ्गाविष्णुप्रगीतकं //
381.m: Knowledge of the stages of life such as conception, birth, childhood, and the like / is the supreme good for men: [so] was proclaimed by Gaṅgā and Viṣṇu.

381.s:
ādhyātmikādiduḥkhānāmādyantādipratikriyā /
śreyaḥ paraṃ manṣyāṇāṃ janakodgītameva ca //
381.d:
आध्यात्मिकादिदुःखानामाद्यन्तादिप्रतिक्रिया /
श्रेयः परं मन्ष्याणां जनकोद्गीतमेव च //
381.m: Remedy from beginning to end for the sufferings beginning with the spiritual / is the supreme good for men: indeed it was sung by Janaka.

381.s:
abhinnayorbhedakaraḥ pratyayo yaḥ parātmanaḥ /
tacchāntiparamaṃ śreyo brahmodgītamudāhṛtaṃ //
:p 351
381.d:
अभिन्नयोर्भेदकरः प्रत्ययो यः परात्मनः /
तच्छान्तिपरमं श्रेयो ब्रह्मोद्गीतमुदाहृतं //
:प् 351
381.m:
The cognition of difference between the Supreme Self and [individual soul] which are non-different— / the pacification of that is supreme good: [thus] was uttered what was sung by Brahmā.
[Page 351]

381.s:
kartavyamiti yatkarma ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñitaṃ /
kurute śreyase saṅgān jaigīṣavyeṇa gīyate //
381.d:
कर्तव्यमिति यत्कर्म ऋग्यजुःसामसंज्ञितं /
कुरुते श्रेयसे सङ्गान् जैगीषव्येण गीयते //
381.m: Whatever rite known as Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman is performed as a duty / for the sake of the highest good through attachment, is sung by Jaigīṣavya.

381.s:
hāniḥ sarvavidhitsānāmātmanaḥ sukhahaitukī /
śreyaḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ devalodgītamīritaṃ //
381.d:
हानिः सर्वविधित्सानामात्मनः सुखहैतुकी /
श्रेयः परं मनुष्याणां देवलोद्गीतमीरितं //
381.m: Abandonment of all desires, causing the happiness of the Self, / is the supreme good for men: it was declared as sung by Devala.

381.s:
kāmatyāgāttu vijñānaṃ sukhaṃ brahma paraṃ padaṃ /
kāmināṃ na hi vijñānaṃ sanakodgītameva tat //
381.d:
कामत्यागात्तु विज्ञानं सुखं ब्रह्म परं पदं /
कामिनां न हि विज्ञानं सनकोद्गीतमेव तत् //
381.m: From renunciation of desire comes experiential knowledge, bliss, and Brahman, the supreme abode; / for those full of desire, experiential knowledge does not arise: that indeed was sung by Sanaka.

381.s:
pravṛttañca nivṛttañca kāryaṃ karmaparo 'bravīt /
śreyasāṃ śreya etaddhi naiṣkarmyaṃ brahma taddhariḥ //
381.d:
प्रवृत्तञ्च निवृत्तञ्च कार्यं कर्मपरो ऽब्रवीत् /
श्रेयसां श्रेय एतद्धि नैष्कर्म्यं ब्रह्म तद्धरिः //
381.m: He who is devoted to action has spoken of the duty of active engagement and renunciation; / this indeed is the best of all goods: actionless Brahman, that is Hari.

381.s:
pumāṃścādhigatajñāno bhedaṃ nāpnoti sattamaḥ /
brahmaṇā viṣṇusaṃjñena parameṇāvyayena ca //
381.d:
पुमांश्चाधिगतज्ञानो भेदं नाप्नोति सत्तमः /
ब्रह्मणा विष्णुसंज्ञेन परमेणाव्ययेन च //
381.m: And the man who has attained knowledge, the best of good men, finds no difference / with Brahman, named Viṣṇu, supreme and imperishable.

381.s:
jñānaṃ vijñānamāstikyaṃ saubhāgyaṃ rūpamuttamam /
tapasā labhyate sarvaṃ manasā yadyadicchati //
381.d:
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं सौभाग्यं रूपमुत्तमम् /
तपसा लभ्यते सर्वं मनसा यद्यदिच्छति //
381.m: Knowledge, experiential knowledge, faith, good fortune, and supreme beauty— / everything whatever one desires in mind is obtained through ascetic austerity.

381.s:
nāsti viṣṇusamandhyeyaṃ tapo nānaśanātparaṃ /
nāstyārogyasamaṃ dhanyaṃ nāsti gaṅgāsamā sarit //
381.d:
नास्ति विष्णुसमन्ध्येयं तपो नानशनात्परं /
नास्त्यारोग्यसमं धन्यं नास्ति गङ्गासमा सरित् //
381.m: There is no object of meditation equal to Viṣṇu; there is no ascetic austerity higher than fasting; / there is no fortune equal to health; there is no river equal to the Gaṅgā.

381.s:
na so 'sti bāndhavaḥ kaścidviṣṇuṃ muktvā jagadguruṃ /
adhaścordhaṃ hariścāgre dehendriyamanomukhe //
381.d:
न सो ऽस्ति बान्धवः कश्चिद्विष्णुं मुक्त्वा जगद्गुरुं /
अधश्चोर्धं हरिश्चाग्रे देहेन्द्रियमनोमुखे //
381.m: There is no relative whatsoever except Viṣṇu, the teacher of the universe; / Hari is below and above, in front, in the body, senses, mind, and mouth.

381.s:
ityevaṃ saṃsmaran prāṇān yastyajetsa harirbhavet /
yattad brahma yataḥ sarvaṃ yatsarvaṃ tasya saṃsthitam //
381.d:
इत्येवं संस्मरन् प्राणान् यस्त्यजेत्स हरिर्भवेत् /
यत्तद् ब्रह्म यतः सर्वं यत्सर्वं तस्य संस्थितम् //
381.m: Remembering thus, whoever relinquishes his vital breaths becomes Hari. / That which is Brahman, from which everything arises, which is all, [in it] his universe is established;

381.s:
agrāhyakamanirdeśyaṃ supratiṣṭhañca yatparaṃ /
parāparasvarūpeṇa viṣṇuḥ sarvahṛdi sthitaḥ //
381.d:
अग्राह्यकमनिर्देश्यं सुप्रतिष्ठञ्च यत्परं /
परापरस्वरूपेण विष्णुः सर्वहृदि स्थितः //
