381.m: which cannot be grasped, cannot be designated, firmly established, and supreme— / in the form of both higher and lower, Viṣṇu resides in the heart of all.

381.s:
yajñeśaṃ yajñapuruṣaṃ kecidicchanti tatparaṃ /
kecidviṣṇuṃ haraṃ kecit kecid brahmāṇamīśvaraṃ //
381.d:
यज्ञेशं यज्ञपुरुषं केचिदिच्छन्ति तत्परं /
केचिद्विष्णुं हरं केचित् केचिद् ब्रह्माणमीश्वरं //
381.m: Some desire that supreme [deity] as the Lord of sacrifice, the Spirit of sacrifice; / some as Viṣṇu, some as Hara, some as Brahmā the Lord;

381.s:
indrādināmabhiḥ kecit sūryaṃ somañca kālakam /
:p 352
brahmādistambhaparyantaṃ jagadviṣṇuṃ vadanti ca //
381.d:
इन्द्रादिनामभिः केचित् सूर्यं सोमञ्च कालकम् /
:प् 352
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्भपर्यन्तं जगद्विष्णुं वदन्ति च //

381.s:
sa viṣṇuḥ paramaṃ brahma yato nāvartate punaḥ /
suvarṇādimahādānapuṇyatīrthāvagāhanaiḥ //
381.d:
स विष्णुः परमं ब्रह्म यतो नावर्तते पुनः /
सुवर्णादिमहादानपुण्यतीर्थावगाहनैः //
381.m: That Viṣṇu is the supreme Brahman, from which one does not return again. / By great gifts such as gold, ablutions in sacred fords,

381.s:
dhyānair vrataiḥ pūjayā ca dharmaśrutyā tadāpnuyāt /
ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ rathameva tu //
381.d:
ध्यानैर् व्रतैः पूजया च धर्मश्रुत्या तदाप्नुयात् /
आत्मानं रथिनं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु //
381.m: meditations, votive observances, worship, and listening to the sacred law, one attains that. / Know the Self as the chariot-rider, and the body as the chariot;

381.s:
buddhintu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragrahameva ca /
indrayāṇi hayānāhurviṣayāṃśceṣugocarān //
381.d:
बुद्धिन्तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च /
इन्द्रयाणि हयानाहुर्विषयांश्चेषुगोचरान् //
381.m: know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins. / The senses are called the horses, and sense objects are their pasture.

381.s:
ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktetyāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ /
yastvavijñānavān bhavatyayuktena manasā sadā //
381.d:
आत्मेन्द्रियमनोयुक्तं भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः /
यस्त्वविज्ञानवान् भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा //
381.m: The wise call [the Self] joined with the senses and the mind the enjoyer. / But whoever is devoid of experiential knowledge, with mind always undisciplined,

381.s:
na satpadamavāpnoti saṃsārañcādhigacchati /
yastu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā //
381.d:
न सत्पदमवाप्नोति संसारञ्चाधिगच्छति /
यस्तु विज्ञानवान् भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा //
381.m: does not attain the good realm, and goes into worldly existence. / But whoever possesses experiential knowledge, with mind always disciplined,

381.s:
sa tatpadamavāpnoti yasmādbhūyo na jāyate /
vijñānasārathiryastu manaḥpragrahavānnaraḥ //
381.d:
स तत्पदमवाप्नोति यस्माद्भूयो न जायते /
विज्ञानसारथिर्यस्तु मनःप्रग्रहवान्नरः //
381.m: attains that state from which he is not born again. / The man who has experiential knowledge as his charioteer, who holds the reins of the mind,

381.s:
so 'dhvānaṃ paramāpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam /
indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaś ca paraṃ manaḥ //
381.d:
सो ऽध्वानं परमाप्नोति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् /
इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्य् अर्था अर्थेभ्यश् च परं मनः //
381.m: reaches the end of the road, that supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / For higher than the senses are the objects, and higher than the objects is the mind;

381.s:
manasastu parā buddhiḥ buddherātmā mahān paraḥ /
mahataḥ paramavyaktamavyaktātpuruṣaḥ paraḥ //
381.d:
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिः बुद्धेरात्मा महान् परः /
महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्पुरुषः परः //
381.m: higher than the mind is the intellect, higher than the intellect is the Great Self; / higher than the Great is the Unmanifest, higher than the Unmanifest is the Spirit (Puruṣa).

381.s:
puruṣānna paraṃ kiñcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ /
eṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhātmā na prakāśate //
381.d:
पुरुषान्न परं किञ्चित् सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः /
एषु सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढात्मा न प्रकाशते //
381.m: Higher than Puruṣa there is nothing; that is the goal, that is the supreme destination. / Hidden in all these beings, the Self does not shine forth.

381.s:
dṛśyate tvagryayā budhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ /
yacchedvāṅmanasī prājñaḥ tadyacchejjñānamātmani //
381.d:
दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुध्या सूक्ष्मया सूक्ष्मदर्शिभिः /
यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञः तद्यच्छेज्ज्ञानमात्मनि //
381.m: But it is seen by subtle intellect, / sharp, by those who perceive what is subtle. / A wise man should restrain speech in the mind; he should restrain that in knowledge, in the self;

381.s:
jñānamātmani mahati niyacchecchānta ātmani /
jñātvā brahmātmanoryogaṃ yamādyair brahma sadbhavet //
:p 353
381.d:
ज्ञानमात्मनि महति नियच्छेच्छान्त आत्मनि /
ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मात्मनोर्योगं यमाद्यैर् ब्रह्म सद्भवेत् //
:प् 353
381.m:
He should restrain knowledge in the great self, and that in the tranquil self. / Having known the union of brahman and the self by means of restraints and the rest, one becomes the true brahman.
[Page 353]

381.s:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryāparigrahau /
yamāś ca niyamāḥ pañca śaucaṃ santoṣasattapaḥ //
381.d:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहौ /
यमाश् च नियमाः पञ्च शौचं सन्तोषसत्तपः //
381.m: Non-injury, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possession: / these are the restraints; and the five observances are ritual purity, contentment, true ascetic austerity,

381.s:
svādhyāyeśvarapūjā ca āsanaṃ padmakādikaṃ /
prāṇāyāmo vāyujayaḥ pratyāhāraḥ svanigrahaḥ //
381.d:
स्वाध्यायेश्वरपूजा च आसनं पद्मकादिकं /
प्राणायामो वायुजयः प्रत्याहारः स्वनिग्रहः //
381.m: Vedic study, and worship of God. Posture is the lotus posture and the like. / Breath control is the mastery of breath. Sensory withdrawal is self-restraint.

381.s:
śubhe hy ekatra viṣaye cetaso yat pradhāraṇaṃ /
niś calatvāttu dhīmadbhirdhāraṇā dvija kathyate //
381.d:
शुभे ह्य् एकत्र विषये चेतसो यत् प्रधारणं /
निश् चलत्वात्तु धीमद्भिर्धारणा द्विज कथ्यते //
381.m: The holding of the mind firmly upon a single auspicious object, / because of immobility, is called concentration by the wise, O twice-born.

381.s:
paunaḥpunyena tatraiva viṣayeṣveva dhāraṇā /
dhyānaṃ smṛtaṃ samādhistu ahaṃ brahmātmasaṃsthitiḥ //
381.d:
पौनःपुन्येन तत्रैव विषयेष्वेव धारणा /
ध्यानं स्मृतं समाधिस्तु अहं ब्रह्मात्मसंस्थितिः //
381.m: Holding [the mind] repeatedly on that very object / is remembered as meditation. Concentration, however, is the state of the self as “I am brahman.”

381.s:
ghaṭadhvaṃsādyathākāśamabhinnaṃ nabhasā bhavet /
mukto jīvo brahmaṇaivaṃ sadbrahma brahma vai bhavet //
381.d:
घटध्वंसाद्यथाकाशमभिन्नं नभसा भवेत् /
मुक्तो जीवो ब्रह्मणैवं सद्ब्रह्म ब्रह्म वै भवेत् //
381.m: Just as space becomes identical with the sky upon the destruction of a jar, / even so the liberated individual soul, being brahman, becomes the true brahman indeed.

381.s:
ātmānaṃ manyate brahma jīvo jñānena nānyathā /
jīvo hy ajñānatatkāryamuktaḥ syādajarāmaraḥ //
381.d:
आत्मानं मन्यते ब्रह्म जीवो ज्ञानेन नान्यथा /
जीवो ह्य् अज्ञानतत्कार्यमुक्तः स्यादजरामरः //
381.m: The individual soul considers itself as brahman through knowledge, not otherwise; / for freed from ignorance and its effects, the individual soul becomes ageless and immortal.

381.s:
agnir uvāca
vaśiṣṭha yamagītoktā paṭhatāṃ bhuktimuktidā /
ātyantiko layaḥ prokto vedāntabrahmadhīmayaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yamagītā nāmaikāśītyadhikatriśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 354
:ś atha dvyaśītyadhikatriśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
āgneyapurāṇamāhātmyaṃ
381.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वशिष्ठ यमगीतोक्ता पठतां भुक्तिमुक्तिदा /
आत्यन्तिको लयः प्रोक्तो वेदान्तब्रह्मधीमयः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे यमगीता नामैकाशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 354
:श् अथ द्व्यशीत्यधिकत्रिशततमो ऽध्यायः
आग्नेयपुराणमाहात्म्यं
381.m:
Agni said: / O Vasiṣṭha, this Yama’s Song has been spoken, granting worldly enjoyment and liberation to those who recite it. / Absolute dissolution has been explained, consisting of the realization of brahman through Vedānta.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the three hundred and eighty-first chapter, named “The Song of Yama.”
[Page 354]
Now the three hundred and eighty-second chapter:
The Greatness of the Agni Purāṇa.
